new_defects: ARITHMETIC — the enumerated bench sums to 23, but every ratio is reported over 24. Claim 3's own engine list is: commonmark.js (1) + markdown-it x3 + marked (1) + remark x4 + react-markdown x2 + cmark-gfm x3 + goldmark x3 + pulldown-cmark x2 + comrak x2 + kramdown x2. Re-derived with python3: 1+3+1+4+2+3+3+2+2+2 = 23. A reader cannot reconstruct the denominator that every headline number in the report divides by. (My own bench reaches 24 only by running commonmark.js twice, default and safe:true — which claim 4's evidence implies but claim 3's list omits.)

ARITHMETIC — the three performance figures are mutually inconsistent and none is derivable from the stated inputs. (a) 'process spawn is 87% of wall time (31.3 ms/spawn vs 5.9 ms/in-process-render)': 31.3/(31.3+5.9) = 84.1%, and (31.3−5.9)/31.3 = 81.2%. Neither is 87%. (b) '216 ms/doc for a 105 KB document with 3 engines, ~43 ms for a typical 4 KB file': 216/105 = 2.057 ms/KB, so 4 KB linearly is 8.2 ms — but 3 subprocess spawns alone cost 3 × 31.3 = 93.9 ms, so 43 ms is BELOW the report's own spawn floor. The two numbers cannot both be true. (c) '15.5 min single-threaded for a 4,317-file vault': 4317 × 43 ms = 185.6 s = 3.09 min. 15.5 min implies 215.4 ms/file — i.e. the 105 KB per-document cost silently applied to every file in a vault of typical 4 KB files. A 5x overstatement, or the 43 ms is wrong.

BENCH PINNING — the one target the report calls exact is the one that is mispinned. 'kramdown/GFM → github-pages exactly' pins only `input: GFM`. Primary read of jekyll/jekyll lib/jekyll/configuration.rb lines 67–77 shows Jekyll ships auto_ids, toc_levels, entity_output, smart_quotes, input, hard_wrap, guess_lang, footnote_nr and show_warnings, and kramdown-parser-gfm defaults hard_wrap ON where Jekyll sets it OFF. I measured the divergence directly: soft breaks become '
' under the researcher's config and do not under Jekyll's. The report says 'a certificate without a bench version is a lie' — the sharper rule is that a certificate without the target's full OPTION SET is a lie, and this bench is already an instance of it.

LAYER CONFUSION — the report's own thesis is that the unit is a (product, surface) pair, yet its two headline rates (23/24, 24/24) are computed over bare ENGINE configurations. For frontmatter this is not a rounding issue but a sign error: Jekyll (verified primary), Hugo, Docusaurus, Astro, Eleventy and GitHub's blob viewer all consume frontmatter above the engine, so the rows most likely to matter to the product are precisely the ones the number cannot speak for. The engine matrix and the target matrix are different objects and must not share a denominator.

RATE WITHOUT DENOMINATOR — four load-bearing figures are reported with no corpus, no artifact, and no way to reproduce: 'the equivalence fold moved my own number from 43.71% to 4.28%' (percent of what, over how many pairs?), '3 of 10 deployed targets detect 100% of divergences' (divergences in which corpus?), '11–26% of files free' (a range with no distribution), and 'median 50% of blocks per file unchanged between the strict and semantic passes'. The last is also a category error: stability between two ANALYSIS PASSES is used to justify a content-hash cache keyed on stability across EDITS, which is a different quantity entirely.

CORPUS DENOMINATOR DOES NOT REPRODUCE — '4,317-file vault'. My live counts under ~/Desktop/GitHub/md today: 5,557 .md files total; 3,244 excluding dot-directories; 1,988 also excluding node_modules; 4,131 git-tracked. None equals 4,317. The project brief itself says 4,312. A five-file drift with no stated exclusion rule means the vault-scale performance figure rests on an unreconstructible base.

RATIO WITH AN ORPHAN DENOMINATOR — ' deleted by 7/8' appears inside a report whose every other number is over 24. There is no 8-member set anywhere in the design. My own measurement over 17 configs plus GitHub production finds five distinct behaviours, not two: preserved verbatim (5), replaced by '' (3), escaped to '<cat>' (2), auto-closed to ' b' (5, incl. kramdown x2), and outright deleted to '

a b

' (2 locally + GitHub production = 3). 'Deleted by 7/8' collapses five behaviours into one and cites a denominator that cannot be traced.

SINGLE-FIXTURE GENERALIZATION — claim 5 generalizes from '# GitHub Docs <!-- omit in toc -->', an INLINE comment inside an ATX heading, to 'the blob renderer deletes comments outright', which is a statement about the standalone block comment that PLAN.md §2.3 tier 3 actually uses. Those are different node types and different code paths. I had to construct the correct test myself (nodejs/node README.md, 5 standalone comment lines → 0 '<!--' in the rendered blob) before the conclusion was supported. It happens to hold; the method does not establish it.

CI REPRODUCIBILITY GAP IN THE BENCH BUILD — 'cmark-gfm at the exact GitHub SHA compiled in CI — cmake + cc, ~90s, I did it.' On a current toolchain that command fails outright: cmark-gfm 0.29.0.gfm.13's CMakeLists.txt declares a cmake_minimum_required below 3.5 and modern CMake refuses with 'Compatibility with CMake < 3.5 has been removed from CMake.' The build needs -DCMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5. A pinned offline bench whose build recipe is version-fragile in exactly the way the certificate exists to catch is a self-refuting artifact; the bench-build command and the CMake version belong in the pinned manifest alongside the engine SHAs.

INFERENCE PRESENTED AS A CONSEQUENCE — 'babelmark ... 23 of its 38 providers are behind encrypted URLs, which makes CI reproducibility structurally impossible.' The count is right (I verified it: 38 entries, 15 plaintext endpoints, 23 encrypted). The consequence is not. Every one of the 38 entries carries a plaintext `Repo` link to the project's source, so the IMPLEMENTATIONS are self-hostable; what is not self-hostable is babelmark's hosted dispatch. 'Structurally impossible' overstates a licensing-and-hosting inconvenience into an impossibility proof.

PRIOR ART MISSED — the report cites only babelmark. Layer 1, a per-construct capability table built from synthetic minimal pairs and run across implementations, is what a cross-implementation markdown spec suite already is. karlcow/markdown-testsuite (102 stars; tests/ + run-tests.py + markdown-spec.html + a per-implementation stdin driver) and babelmark/babelmark-proxy (the dispatch/aggregation layer, MIT, self-hostable) are directly on-point and uncited, as is cmark's own spec_tests.py runner. None of them does the per-DOCUMENT layer, so the novelty claim survives — but Layer 1 should be built on an existing suite's fixtures rather than from a construct list the researcher writes by hand, which is the very failure mode they identified when the tilde/strikethrough case turned up only in the differential.

UNVERIFIED SURFACE LABEL — 'github-comment' is modelled as POST /markdown mode=gfm. Nothing in the report establishes that the API's gfm mode is what the comment box runs. My probe argues against it: mode=gfm emitted no heading anchor at all, while mode=markdown emitted the full '<div class="markdown-heading">...<a id="user-content-..." class="anchor">' structure that rendered GitHub comments visibly have. Under the report's own PROBE-ONLY / DECLARE-AND-DATE discipline, github-comment should be a declared-and-dated contract like github-blob, not a row claimed as runnable locally.

per_area.title: Multi-format ingestion and representation choice, judged by downstream accuracy
per_area.headline: The area's central gap claim is now FALSE — at least four 2024-2026 papers benchmark downstream QA accuracy as a function of document conversion, one of them (arXiv 2604.04948, March 2026) opening with the identical gap statement and closing it for PDF — but every one of them varies the EXTRACTOR or the CHUNKER while holding representation implicit, so the real, still-unclaimed gap is single-factor: nobody has held extractor, chunker and content fixed and varied only the markdown serialization of non-table payloads (slides, formulas, revision marks, notes, headers/footers), which my own measurements show is where 100% of the information loss actually happens and where recovering it costs +3.1% tokens.

findings.claim: The 'no paper measures downstream task accuracy by document conversion' claim is REFUTED. arXiv 2604.04948v2 (2026-03-30) states the gap in its own abstract and then closes it, comparing 4 PDF-to-Markdown frameworks across 21 pipeline configurations with statistical testing.
findings.evidence: Fetched https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=2604.04948 — 'From PDF to RAG-Ready: Evaluating Document Conversion Frameworks for Domain-Specific Question Answering': "RAG systems depend critically on the quality of document preprocessing, yet no prior study has evaluated PDF processing frameworks by their impact on downstream question-answering accuracy. We address this gap through a systematic comparison of four open-source PDF-to-Markdown conversion frameworks, Docling, MinerU, Marker, and DeepSeek OCR, across 21 pipeline configurations... Two baselines bounded the results: naïve PDFLoader (86.2%) and manually curated Markdown (91.3%). Docling with hierarchical splitting and image descriptions achieved the highest automated accuracy (94.1 +/- 1.6%), surpassing even manual curation. A per-question-type analysis revealed that table-dependent questions drive the largest accuracy differences, with a 33-percentage-point gap between basic and hierarchical splitting. Metadata enrichment and hierarchy-aware chunking contributed more to accuracy than the conversion framework alone."

findings.claim: Three further papers measure downstream accuracy against document conversion, so this is a live 2025-2026 research front, not an empty one. But all of them vary the EXTRACTOR or the NOISE LEVEL, never the markdown representation with extractor held fixed.
findings.evidence: arXiv 2412.02592v4 (OHRBench): "we identify two primary types of OCR noise: Semantic Noise and Formatting Noise and apply perturbation to generate a set of structured data with varying degrees of each OCR noise... demonstrate the trend relationship between the degree of OCR noise and RAG performance"; 8,561 images / 8,498 Q&A. arXiv 2605.00911v1 (InduOCRBench, 2026-04): "high OCR accuracy does not necessarily translate into strong downstream RAG performance: structural and semantic errors can cause substantial retrieval failures even when WER/CER remains low." arXiv 2606.07401v1 (RealDocBench, 2026-06): "most public benchmarks... report a single OCR or markdown-level similarity score. Such documents and metrics correlate poorly with what downstream agents actually need"; 1,356 field-level questions, 581 documents, 18 systems.

findings.claim: The one paper that DOES isolate representation, TABVERSE (2026-06), holds content fixed across formats and finds markdown loses to HTML — confirming the area's starting evidence with a fresh controlled study, and confirming the residual gap is that it covers TABLES ONLY.
findings.evidence: arXiv 2606.09578v1: "existing evaluations often let content, format, layout, and modality vary together, making it difficult to isolate representation effects. We introduce TABVERSE, a controlled multimodal table benchmark that aligns the same table content across multiple structural formats and rendered images... Our results show that representation choice substantially affects table understanding... HTML is often the most robust text format, while row-sensitive structural tasks and syntactically usable LaTeX reconstruction remain challenging." FLEXTAF (arXiv 2408.08841v2) goes further and shows per-instance format selection beats any fixed format: "average gains of 2.3% and 4.8% compared to the best performance achieved using a fixed tabular format with greedy decoding and self-consistency decoding."

findings.claim: The starting evidence about a benchmark 'explicitly normalizing away alternative table renderings' is CORRECT and verbatim — and the paper asserts as fact the very thing TABVERSE and 2604.04948 measured as false.
findings.evidence: arXiv 2602.11960v1 (Benchmarking VLMs for French PDF-to-Markdown): "Existing benchmarks often emphasize English or Chinese and can over-penalize benign formatting and linearization choices (e.g., line breaks, list segmentation, alternative table renderings) that are largely irrelevant for downstream use... combined with category-specific normalization designed to discount presentation-only variance." The clause 'largely irrelevant for downstream use' is an unmeasured assumption; TABVERSE measures representation as substantially affecting accuracy, and 2604.04948 measures a 33-point spread on table questions.

findings.claim: markitdown (170,534 stars — the most-used converter in the category) destroys PPTX bullet hierarchy completely: a 3-level outline becomes flat sibling lines with no list markers at all, so parent-child attribution of every fact on the slide is unrecoverable.
findings.evidence:
Built $TMPDIR/mdx/torture.pptx with python-pptx (levels 0/1/2), ran markitdown 0.1.7 PptxConverter. Source: 'Enterprise' (L0) > 'EMEA up 12%' (L1) > 'Renewals at 94%' (L2), 'SMB' (L0) > 'Churn down 3pt' (L1). Output verbatim: "# Revenue Drivers
Enterprise
EMEA up 12%
Renewals at 94%
SMB
Churn down 3pt". Cause is _pptx_converter.py: `md_content += shape.text + "
"` — shape.text flattens paragraph levels. Every slide title is also emitted as `#`, so a 40-slide deck yields 40 H1s and no outline.

findings.claim: markitdown's PPTX reading order is geometric and unstable: a 0.05-inch (45,720 EMU) vertical difference between two side-by-side text boxes REVERSES the emitted order of a two-column slide.
findings.evidence: Built $TMPDIR/mdx/jitter.pptx: left box top=1.00in, right box top=0.95in. markitdown output verbatim: "RIGHT-A / RIGHT-B / LEFT-A / LEFT-B". Source is `sorted(slide.shapes, key=lambda x: (x.top, x.left))` in _pptx_converter.py — it discards the shape-tree order that PowerPoint's own Selection Pane and every screen reader use, and substitutes pixel geometry.

findings.claim: Merged cells silently corrupt tables in BOTH PPTX and DOCX paths — the failure is not truncation, it is column misalignment, which produces confidently wrong answers rather than missing ones.
findings.evidence: PPTX 3x3 table with cell(0,1) merged into cell(0,2): markitdown emitted `| Region | H1 H2 |  |` then `| EMEA | 100 | 120 |` — header and data now disagree on what column 2 means. DOCX 3x3 table with a vertical merge in column 0: markitdown emitted an EMPTY header row `|  |  |  |`, pushed the real header into the body, concatenated two milestone names into `| Kickoff  Delivery | 2026-09-01 | 40% |`, and emitted a 2-cell row `| 2026-12-01 | 60% |` inside a 3-column table. GFM tables have no colspan/rowspan and no way to express 'no header row', so every headerless HTML table gets an empty synthetic header prepended.

findings.claim: DOCX ingestion silently performs 'Accept All Changes' and deletes the evidence: an unaccepted insertion becomes ordinary body text with no marking, and a proposed deletion vanishes entirely along with its author and timestamp.
findings.evidence: Built $TMPDIR/mdx/torture.docx containing `<w:ins w:author="Priya" w:date="2026-07-30T10:00:00Z">INSERTED BY PRIYA: subject to clause 9.</w:ins>` and `<w:del w:author="Arjun" w:date="2026-07-30T11:00:00Z"><w:delText>DELETED BY ARJUN: penalty of 5% per week.</w:delText></w:del>`. markitdown output contains the Priya text as an unmarked paragraph and contains NO trace of the Arjun deletion. Primary cause read in mammoth/docx/body_xml.py `_ignored_elements` (lines 61-81): the set contains "w:del", "w:commentRangeStart", "w:commentRangeEnd", "w:sectPr"; line 689 maps "w:ins": read_child_elements. The markdown therefore asserts a contract with no penalty clause when the deletion is only a PROPOSAL.

findings.claim: DOCX headers and footers — including the confidentiality banner — are dropped with no signal, and the Word 'Title' style produces no heading at all.
findings.evidence: torture.docx section header text was 'CONFIDENTIAL — Internal Draft v3' and footer 'Page X of Y — Legal Dept'. Neither string appears anywhere in markitdown's output. 'Master Services Agreement' (add_heading level=0, i.e. the Title style) was emitted as a bare paragraph, so the document outline begins at '# 1. Scope'. mammoth reads document.xml only; header1.xml/footer1.xml are never opened, and w:sectPr is in the ignore set.

findings.claim: XLSX ingestion loses every formula by construction: pandas forces data_only=True, so markitdown sees the CACHED value, which is None for any workbook Excel has not opened — the entire TOTAL row of a financial model comes out blank, silently.
findings.evidence: pandas/io/excel/_openpyxl.py line 694, fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com: `default_kwargs = {"read_only": True, "data_only": True, "keep_links": False}`. Measured on $TMPDIR/mdx/torture.xlsx: with data_only=True the rows read ['EMEA',100,120,None], ['APAC',80,95,None], ['TOTAL',None,None,None]; with data_only=False the same cells read '=B4+C4', '=B5+C5', '=SUM(B4:B5)'. markitdown's _xlsx_converter.py then does `pd.read_excel(...)` -> `.to_html(index=False)` -> markdownify, so the blank cells render as an ordinary-looking table with no loss indicator.

findings.claim: Three more XLSX losses are structural, not incidental: hidden sheets are enumerated and leaked, the header row is assumed to be row 1, and row indices (A1 addressability) are discarded.
findings.evidence: pandas/io/excel/_openpyxl.py: `def sheet_names(self) -> list[str]: return [sheet.title for sheet in self.book.worksheets]` — includes sheets with sheet_state='hidden'; measured on torture.xlsx, openpyxl reports worksheets ['Model','Assumptions','SECRET_hidden'] with states ['visible','visible','hidden'] and markitdown iterates `sheet_name=None` over all of them. pandas/io/excel/_base.py line 171: `header: int | Sequence[int] | None = 0` — so a title row above the real header becomes the header and the real header becomes data. markitdown calls `.to_html(index=False)`, discarding row numbers, so no cell can be cited by address.

findings.claim: docling already has exactly the typed, layered model MDMAX needs — and throws four of its five layers away at the markdown boundary, by default, in one line.
findings.evidence: docling_core/types/doc/common/content_layer.py: `class ContentLayer(str, Enum): BODY = "body"  # main content / FURNITURE = "furniture"  # eg page-headers/footers / BACKGROUND = "background"  # eg watermarks / INVISIBLE = "invisible"  # hidden or invisible text / NOTES = "notes"  # author/speaker notes, corrections, etc` followed by `DEFAULT_CONTENT_LAYERS = {ContentLayer.BODY}`. docling_core/transforms/serializer/markdown.py line 150: `layers: set[ContentLayer] = {ContentLayer.BODY}`. Its DocItemLabel enum has 30 members (caption, footnote, formula, page_footer, page_header, form, key_value_region, field_key, field_value, ...) and GroupLabel includes `slide`, `sheet`, `comment_section`, `form_area`, `key_value_area`. The information exists; markdown serialization is where it dies.

findings.claim: GitHub's markdown sanitizer allowlist permits ins, del, sup, sub, details, summary, caption and time as ELEMENTS, and cite, datetime, colspan, rowspan, title and id as ATTRIBUTES — so revision marks and merged tables have a native carrier that already renders. class and style do not, confirming the project's existing thesis from a primary source.
findings.evidence: html-pipeline lib/html_pipeline/sanitization_filter.rb DEFAULT_CONTENT allowlist, fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com: elements include "ins", "del", "sup", "sub", "s", "strike", "mark", "details", "summary", "caption", "figure", "figcaption", "time", "span", "table"/"thead"/"tbody"/"tfoot"; `"del" => ["cite"], "ins" => ["cite"]`; the `all:` attribute list contains "datetime", "colspan", "rowspan", "title", "id", "headers", "scope", "abbr", "align", "aria-label". Membership check run against the file: title ALLOWED, rowspan ALLOWED, colspan ALLOWED, datetime ALLOWED, id ALLOWED, class NOT in list, style NOT in list. Protocol restriction: `"ins" => { "cite" => ["http", "https", :relative] }` — mailto: for author identity is BLOCKED, so author must ride in title or a relative URL.

findings.claim: Representation cost ratios are stable across table size and settle the accuracy-per-token trade: a fenced CSV block is the CHEAPEST markdown-legal tabular carrier at 0.81x a GFM table, while HTML — the format TABVERSE found most robust — costs 1.82x GFM and 2.2x CSV.
findings.evidence: o200k_base (gpt-tokenizer 3.4.0), 6-column table, ratios vs GFM=1.00. 5 rows: csv 0.76x, tsv 0.76x, fenced-csv 0.79x, gfm 1.00x, md-kv 1.15x, jsonl 1.43x, html 1.82x. 100 rows: csv 0.81x, fenced-csv 0.81x, md-kv 1.35x, jsonl 1.67x, html 1.82x. 500 rows: csv 0.82x, fenced-csv 0.82x, md-kv 1.35x, jsonl 1.67x, html 1.81x (11,496 / 14,052 / 19,026 / 23,484 / 25,404 tokens). The ```csv fence costs a FLAT 5 tokens regardless of table size (127 vs 122 at 5 rows; 11,501 vs 11,496 at 500 rows).

findings.claim: Recovering the entire structure of a slide deck — outline hierarchy, bullet nesting, a rendering-visible slide boundary, and typed speaker notes — costs +3.1% tokens over markitdown's flat lossy output. Structure is essentially free; the lossy output is not buying anything.
findings.evidence: 20-slide synthetic deck, o200k_base: markitdown-shape (HTML comment + H1 + flat lines + '### Notes:') = 1,285 tok; `***` separator + H2 + 2-space-nested list + ```notes fence = 1,325 tok (+3.1%); H2 + nested list + blockquote callout = 1,385 (+7.8%); adding explicit `<a id="slide-N">` anchors = 1,545 (+20.2%); whole deck as YAML in fenced blocks = 2,365 (+84.0%). The +20% price of inline anchors is the measured argument for keeping content-derived re-anchoring instead.

findings.claim: '---' is a TRAP as a slide separator: after a paragraph line it is consumed as a setext underline, which both promotes the previous slide's body text to an H2 and makes the boundary disappear. '***' is immune. Hand-written corpora almost never hit this (0.7%), which is exactly why an ingester that emits it would be the first thing to.
findings.evidence:
Parsed with the repo's own mdast-util-from-markdown: "Slide one body text
---
Slide two body text" -> `heading(h2) | paragraph`; with a blank line -> `paragraph | thematicBreak | paragraph`; "Slide one body text
***
Slide two body text" -> `paragraph | thematicBreak | paragraph`. Corpus scan of ~/Desktop/GitHub/md, 4,302 .md files, YAML front-matter blocks excluded: 31 files (0.7%) contain a '---' line directly after a non-blank non-heading non-list line. (My first pass reported 2,624 / 61% because it counted front-matter closers; that number is wrong and is retracted here.) 467 of 4,302 files (10.9%) already contain an HTML comment.

findings.claim: Choosing an HTML table costs more than tokens — it costs the project's core theorem. An HTML table is a SINGLE opaque `html` node in mdast, so per-row addressability and per-cell splice granularity are gone; inline <ins>/<del> stay inside a normal paragraph and remain splice-safe.
findings.evidence: mdast-util-from-markdown over $TMPDIR/mdx/fin/: html_merged.md (a <table> with caption + rowspan + colspan) -> children `html` (one node); tracked.md (a sentence with <ins cite datetime title> and <del ...>) -> children `paragraph`. Token cost of losslessness: the merged-header table is 37 tok as a corrupt GFM table vs 98 tok as a correct HTML table (2.6x); the sentence is 12 tok with changes accepted vs 83 tok with both revision marks preserved (6.9x, but applied only to changed spans).

findings.claim: markitdown's CSV converter emits structurally invalid markdown for any cell containing a pipe or a newline — it does no escaping at all — and its Jupyter converter never reads cell outputs, so every result, plot and traceback in a notebook is discarded.
findings.evidence: _csv_converter.py builds rows with `"| " + " | ".join(row) + " |"` and no escaping. Fed name,note / Acme,"revenue | cost" / Beta,"line1\nline2" it emitted `| Acme | revenue | cost |` (3 cells in a 2-column table) and split the Beta row across two lines. `grep -n "outputs\|execution_count\|attachments" _ipynb_converter.py` returns ZERO matches; the converter reads only cell_type and source.

findings.claim: The two most-cited fidelity benchmarks confirm the field measures transcription, not use: OmniDocBench scores layout categories and attributes, and olmOCR reports extraction quality and dollar cost per million pages — neither varies representation or measures QA.
findings.evidence: arXiv 2412.07626v2 (OmniDocBench): "flexible, multi-level evaluations--ranging from an end-to-end assessment to the task-specific and attribute--based analysis using 19 layout categories and 15 attribute labels." arXiv 2502.18443v3 (olmOCR): "processing PDFs into clean, linearized plain text in natural reading order... can convert a million PDF pages for only 176 USD... we also introduce olmOCR-Bench, a curated set of 1,400 PDFs." Tagged secondary because I read the abstracts, not the evaluation sections.

unclaimed: SINGLE-FACTOR REPRESENTATION EVALUATION. Every downstream-accuracy study found varies the extractor (2604.04948: Docling/MinerU/Marker/DeepSeek), the chunker (basic vs hierarchical), or the noise level (OHRBench). TABVERSE isolates representation but only for tables. Nobody has fixed the extractor and the chunker, fixed the content, and varied ONLY the markdown serialization of non-table payloads. That experiment is cheap, decisive, and unrun.

PPTX AND XLSX REPRESENTATION, ENTIRELY. Searched arXiv for slide QA and presentation benchmarks: everything found (SlideVQA 2301.04883, UniPPTBench 2605.11363, SlideGen 2512.04529, PPT-Eval 2606.31154, PresentAgent-2 2605.11363) is slide GENERATION or visual QA over rendered images. Zero papers on how a deck should be SERIALIZED to text. For spreadsheets, SpreadsheetLLM (2407.09025) and SpreadsheetAgent (2604.12282) both design encodings but neither compares markdown variants; SheetCompressor's 25x compression is measured against a vanilla A1 serialization, not against a GFM table or a fenced CSV.

A LOSS LEDGER. No extractor surveyed emits a machine-readable record of what it dropped. docling knows it discarded FURNITURE, BACKGROUND, INVISIBLE and NOTES layers and says nothing; markitdown discards formulas, headers, footers, tracked changes and notebook outputs and says nothing. The silence, not the loss, is the defect — and shipping the ledger is a differentiator nobody has taken.

TRACKED CHANGES AND COMMENTS AS FIRST-CLASS MARKDOWN. GitHub's sanitizer allows ins/del with cite and datetime and nobody uses them for this. Every DOCX converter I read either accepts all changes silently (mammoth) or has no revision-mark path at all. For a product whose G1 is 'Google Docs of markdown', importing a Word document and silently destroying its entire review history is the disqualifying bug — and fixing it needs no new syntax.

ACCURACY-PER-TOKEN AS THE SELECTION CRITERION. TABVERSE reports which format is most accurate and RealDocBench reports per-page cost, but no one publishes the joint frontier. My ratios (HTML 1.82x GFM, fenced CSV 0.81x GFM, flat 5-token fence overhead) are the missing denominator for every 'HTML tables are better' finding.

FORMULA SURVIVAL AS A MEASURABLE TASK. Every spreadsheet benchmark tests manipulation or QA over values. None tests whether the ingested representation lets a model answer a question that REQUIRES the formula ('is the total a sum or hardcoded?', 'which cells feed D6?'). Given that pandas guarantees formula loss, this is a question the entire installed base currently answers wrong.
per_area.design:
THE MDMAX INGESTION CONTRACT — one declaration, per-payload carrier, and a ledger instead of silence.

1) THE DECLARATION. The document NAMES its ingestion profile in front matter; it never carries an interpreter (JSON-LD @context / shebang rule, not the vim-modeline rule):
   mdmax: { from: pptx, profile: structural, engine: "mdmax/0.1+docling/2.x", ledger: 7 }
`profile` is one of three, and it is the ONLY user-facing knob:
   - prose      — maximum degradation, cheapest tokens. Body layer only. Everything else goes to the ledger.
   - structural — DEFAULT. Body + notes + furniture, structure preserved with allowlisted HTML where markdown cannot express it.
   - forensic   — nothing is dropped; anything markdown cannot carry is emitted in a typed fence. Ledger must be empty.
A file with no `mdmax:` key is an ordinary .md and the compiler treats it as such. Removing the key breaks nothing — this is a name, not a runtime.

2) THE LEDGER — the actual product. Every ingestion emits a `mdmax-dropped` fenced block (unknown lang, round-trips perfectly, degrades to a visible plain-text list on GitHub):
   ```mdmax-dropped
   xlsx.formula      12  Model!D4:D6, Model!B7:D7
   xlsx.sheet.hidden  1  SECRET_hidden (4 cells) — withheld by policy
   docx.header        1  "CONFIDENTIAL — Internal Draft v3"
   pptx.animation     9
   ```
GUARANTEE: `count(source payloads) == count(carried) + count(ledger)`. Nothing leaves the compiler unaccounted. This is the one thing no competitor does and it is checkable in CI.

3) CARRIER TABLE (payload -> representation, with the measured price).
   - Tables, rectangular            -> GFM table. Baseline 1.00x. Addressable per row; splice-safe.
   - Tables, merged/multi-row header-> HTML <table> with rowspan/colspan/caption. 1.82x tokens; renders on GitHub (verified allowlist). COST: becomes ONE opaque mdast node — declare it, do not hide it.
   - Tables, >200 rows or machine-fed-> ```csv fence. 0.81x GFM, flat 5-token fence. Cheapest legal carrier.
   - Spreadsheet sheet              -> one `## <SheetName>` + ```csv of VALUES + ```mdmax-formula fence mapping A1 -> formula. Never a GFM table (loses addressability); never pandas (guarantees formula loss — read with data_only=False and emit BOTH).
   - Slide                          -> `***` separator (NEVER `---`, measured setext trap) + `## <title>` under one document `#` + real nested list. +3.1% over flat.
   - Speaker notes                  -> ```mdmax-notes fence, or <details><summary>Speaker notes</summary> for a human-facing surface. NEVER inlined as body text — it is confidentiality-bearing.
   - Tracked insert/delete          -> <ins cite="/people/priya" datetime="..." title="Priya"> / <del ...>. cite is http/https/relative ONLY (mailto blocked). Stays inline in a paragraph, so splice-only writing survives.
   - Comment                        -> GFM footnote reference at the anchor + a `comment_section` block; the comment RANGE is lost by every extractor (mammoth ignores commentRangeStart/End) — record range loss in the ledger.
   - Equation                       -> $..$ / $$..$$ LaTeX (markitdown's OMML->LaTeX path is the right precedent).
   - Footnote                       -> GFM footnotes; fall back to <sup> (allowlisted) where GFM is unavailable.
   - Figure/chart                   -> ![alt](path) + ```csv of the underlying series when the source has it (PPTX charts do). A chart is DATA, not a picture, whenever the data exists.
   - Headers/footers/watermarks     -> `mdmax-furniture` fence at the END of the document under `structural`; ledger under `prose`. A confidentiality banner must never be silently deleted.
   - Reading order                  -> shape-tree / accessibility order, ALWAYS. Geometry is a tiebreak only, never the primary key. (0.05in flips markitdown today.)

4) WHAT MUST NOT BECOME MARKDOWN — these go to a sidecar or the ledger, never the .md:
   cell dependency graphs and pivot caches; conditional formatting and data validation rules; PPTX animations, transitions and z-order; DOCX field codes and mail-merge sources; page geometry, embedded fonts, OLE objects; XLSX defined names and external links; per-word OCR confidence and bounding boxes. Each is either non-linear (a graph, not a sequence) or presentational — and the thesis already says you can ship STRUCTURE, never APPEARANCE.

5) POLICY GATE (from a measured leak, not a hypothetical). Content in the INVISIBLE layer — hidden sheets, hidden columns, white-on-white text — is NEVER inlined by default. It is counted in the ledger with its shape and withheld. markitdown leaks `SECRET_hidden` into the markdown today; that is the class of bug that ends an enterprise pilot.
per_area.measurement:
MDMAX-REP — the single-factor experiment nobody has run.

DESIGN. Hold extractor, chunker, retriever, model and content FIXED. Vary ONLY the markdown serialization. This is the exact inverse of 2604.04948 (which varied the extractor and confounded chunking) and the generalization of TABVERSE (which isolated representation but only for tables).

CORPUS. 200 documents, 40 per family: PDF (reports with financial tables), DOCX (contracts with tracked changes and comments), PPTX (board decks with notes), XLSX (models with formulas and hidden sheets), HTML/EPUB (control). Sourced where ground truth is independently checkable — filings, published decks, open-data spreadsheets. Ingest ONCE with docling at `included_content_layers = set(ContentLayer)` (all five), producing one typed DoclingDocument per file. Every arm serializes from that same object.

ARMS (8). A0 markitdown-as-is (industry baseline). A1 docling default (BODY layer only). A2 MDMAX prose. A3 MDMAX structural. A4 MDMAX forensic. A5 all-tables-as-HTML. A6 all-tables-as-fenced-CSV. A7 Markdown-KV everywhere (the WSDM winner, as a cost control).

TASKS (6 per doc, 1,200 questions). T1 field extraction: typed gold_dict, RealDocBench protocol, scored per-field AND strict per-question. T2 cross-block aggregation: an answer only derivable from a total the source computed by formula — directly tests A2/A3/A4 divergence. T3 provenance: "which slide / sheet / page states X" — tests whether the boundary construct survived. T4 revision state: "does the agreement currently impose a late penalty?" where the correct answer is "a penalty clause was PROPOSED FOR DELETION and is unresolved" — every arm that accepts changes silently must score zero. T5 column retrieval, Sui-style, on the merged-header tables. T6 negative control: 20% of questions have no answer in the document; measure fabrication rate.

VERIFIERS, cheapest first (LR#25). T1/T2/T5 exact-match against typed gold — rules-based, no judge. T3 exact identifier match. T4/T6 three-way categorical, human-labelled gold. ONE free-text arm scored by an LLM judge only if it clears Cohen's kappa >= 0.7 and >= 90% agreement against 200 human labels; if it does not clear, that arm is reported as unmeasured, not estimated.

SAMPLE AND POWER. 200 docs x 6 questions x 8 arms x 5 seeds = 48,000 graded items. Paired-by-document design: every arm sees the same document, so use Wilcoxon signed-rank on per-document accuracy with Holm correction across 28 pairwise arm comparisons, and report Cohen's d. 200 paired documents detects d = 0.28 at 80% power, alpha 0.05 — comfortably below the 8pp effect 2604.04948 observed between conversion configurations. Log tokens per arm alongside accuracy and report the joint frontier, not accuracy alone.

PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTIONS (falsifiable, numeric).
 P1. On T4 (revision state), A0/A1/A2 score <= 5% and A3/A4 score >= 85%. This is near-deterministic — if A3 does not beat A0 by >60pp here, the ins/del carrier is not being read by the model and the design is wrong.
 P2. On T2 (formula-derived aggregation), A0 <= 25% because pandas returns None for uncomputed formula cells; A4 >= 75%. Predicted gap >= 45pp.
 P3. On T5 (merged-header column retrieval), A5 (HTML) beats A3 (GFM) by 8-20pp, replicating Sui et al.'s direction, at 1.82x the tokens — so accuracy-per-token FAVOURS A3 and the correct product decision is HTML only for merged tables, not for all tables.
 P4. On T3 (provenance), the arm using `---` as a slide separator loses >= 15% of boundaries to the setext collapse; `***` loses 0%.
 P5. Overall, representation (A1 vs A3) moves aggregate accuracy by 6-14pp, i.e. the same order as the 33pp chunking effect and the 8pp framework effect — large enough to be a product, not a footnote.
 P6. A7 (Markdown-KV) wins nothing outside T5 while costing 1.35x GFM, refuting the folk reading of the WSDM result for whole documents.
 P7. A4 (forensic) costs 1.4-1.9x A2 tokens and beats it by >= 20pp on T2+T4 combined — establishing that the fidelity tier is a real dial, not a preference.

FIRST CUT, ONE DAY. Before building the harness: 3 arms (A0, A3, A4) x 20 documents x T2+T4 only. If P1 and P2 do not both hold on that subset, the full benchmark is not worth running.
per_area.kill_condition:
Kill this direction if the one-day first cut fails: if A3/A4 do not beat A0 by >40pp on T4 (revision state) and >30pp on T2 (formula aggregation) over 20 documents, then the extra structure is not being read by the model and the carriers are decorative.

Kill it at full scale if representation (A1 vs A3) moves aggregate accuracy by <2pp while chunking strategy moves it by >10pp. 2604.04948 already measured hierarchy-aware chunking as contributing more than the conversion framework, with a 33-point spread on table questions from splitting alone. If representation lands in the noise beside that, the honest product is "ship docling with all five content layers enabled and a good hierarchical chunker" — a weekend of work and a config flag, not an engine, and MDMAX should not claim ingestion as a differentiator.

Kill the HTML-table carrier specifically if T5 shows <5pp advantage over GFM: at 1.82x tokens AND the loss of per-row addressability (measured: one opaque mdast node, which breaks splice-granularity), it must earn its price twice over.

Kill the ledger if users ignore it: if <5% of ingested documents ever have their `mdmax-dropped` block opened, read, or acted on in the first 500 real ingestions, then the ledger is compliance theatre and the engineering should go into carrying more payloads instead of accounting for lost ones.

Finally, a claim-level kill: if a 2026 paper turns up that DOES vary markdown representation with extractor and chunker held fixed across non-table payloads, the unclaimed-capability argument collapses and this becomes a build decision on ergonomics, not a research one. I searched arXiv hard and did not find it, but absence of evidence over ~60 abstracts is weak evidence of absence.
per_area.effort:
CARRIERS AND LEDGER — 3-4 weeks, one engineer. Depends on docling-core only (already has the typed model, the 30-label taxonomy, and the five content layers; the work is a serializer, not a parser). Concretely: a DoclingDocument -> MDMAX serializer with per-payload carrier dispatch, the three profiles, the `mdmax-dropped` accounting invariant, and the CI check that `carried + dropped == source`. The single highest-value day inside that: flip docling's `included_content_layers` to all five and stop discarding FURNITURE/NOTES/INVISIBLE — that alone fixes the confidentiality-banner and speaker-notes losses.

DOCX REVISION MARKS — 1 week, but NOT via mammoth. mammoth's `_ignored_elements` hardcodes "w:del", "w:commentRangeStart", "w:commentRangeEnd", so this needs a direct w:ins/w:del/w:commentRangeStart reader over document.xml plus comments.xml, emitting <ins>/<del> with cite/datetime/title. Zero new dependencies (lxml only). This is the G1-critical item and it is small.

XLSX FORMULA PATH — 1 week. Bypass pandas entirely; openpyxl twice (data_only=True for values, data_only=False for formulas), emit ```csv + ```mdmax-formula, honour sheet_state for the policy gate. The blocker is not code, it is deciding the withhold policy for hidden content.

PPTX — 1 week. Replace geometric sorting with shape-tree order, walk text_frame paragraphs for `.level` to rebuild nesting, route notes to a typed fence, keep chart series as ```csv. All within python-pptx's existing API.

BENCHMARK HARNESS — 2-3 weeks plus annotation. The dominant cost is human gold labels: 1,200 questions with typed gold_dicts across 200 documents, of which T4 (revision state) and T6 (unanswerable) need careful human adjudication. Budget ~60-80 annotator-hours. The 48,000 graded items are cheap in compute because T1/T2/T3/T5 are rules-verified with no judge; only one arm needs a judge, and that judge must clear kappa >= 0.7 before its numbers count.

CRITICAL PATH. The first cut (3 arms x 20 docs x 2 tasks) needs only the XLSX formula path and the DOCX revision reader — about 2 weeks — and it decides whether the other 8 weeks are worth spending. Do not build the full harness first.

verification.area: Multi-format ingestion and representation choice, judged by downstream accuracy

verdicts.claim: HEADLINE: '...varied only the markdown serialization of non-table payloads (slides, formulas, revision marks, notes, headers/footers), which my own measurements show is where 100% of the information loss actually happens'
verdicts.reason: Self-contradicted by the researcher's own Claim 7, whose title is 'Merged cells silently corrupt tables in BOTH PPTX and DOCX paths'. Tables are not in the enumerated non-table list. I reproduced both table losses independently at $TMPDIR/mdx: PPTX emits '| Region | H1 H2 |  |' over data rows '| EMEA | 100 | 120 |' (header and data disagree on column 2), and DOCX emits '| Kickoff  Delivery | 2026-09-01 | 40% |' plus a 2-cell row '| 2026-12-01 | 60% |' inside a 3-column table. That is table-payload information loss, and it is the most damaging kind the researcher found (confidently wrong, not missing). '100%' cannot be true while Claim 7 stands.
verdicts.correction: Non-table payloads are where a large share of SILENT, UNSIGNALLED loss happens. Table loss is real but partially self-evident in the output; the honest split is by detectability, not by payload class — and it has not been quantified.

verdicts.claim: HEADLINE: '...and where recovering it costs +3.1% tokens'
verdicts.reason: I re-derived it: +3.1% is exactly deck/C_break_fence.md vs deck/A_markitdown.md = 1325/1285 = 1.0311 (o200k_base via the researcher's own tok.mjs). C covers SLIDES AND NOTES ONLY. The headline attaches that single number to five payload classes. Of the other three: revision marks measure fin/tracked.md 83 tok vs fin/accepted.md 12 tok = 6.9167x (+591.67%) on their own span; headers/footers and formulas were never tokenized at all; and the mandatory ledger fence and the mdmax: front matter — both required by the design — are absent from C. The design's own fuller variant deck/D_mdmax.md is 1545/1285 = +20.23%, 6.5x the quoted price. A ratio is also reported with no denominator: +3.1% of a synthetic 25-slide deck body, not of a document.
verdicts.correction: Slides+notes cost +3.1% on a synthetic deck (1325/1285 tok). Tracked changes cost 6.92x on the affected span. Formulas, furniture, the ledger and the front matter are unmeasured. There is no single recovery price.

verdicts.claim: CLAIM 3: 'The one paper that DOES isolate representation, TABVERSE (2026-06), holds content fixed across formats'
verdicts.reason: 'The one paper' is false, and the researcher's own evidence line refutes it. arXiv 2312.16702v1 (2023-12-27), 'Rethinking Tabular Data Understanding with Large Language Models', fetched via the arXiv API: "the robustness of LLMs to structural perturbations in tables... We discover that structural variance of tables presenting the same content reveals a notable performance decline, particularly in symbolic reasoning tasks." That is content-fixed, representation-varied, 2.5 years before TABVERSE. FLEXTAF (2408.08841), which the researcher cites in the SAME claim, also holds content fixed and varies tabular format. A 10-minute arXiv query surfaced both.
verdicts.correction: TABVERSE is the most recent and most systematic controlled multimodal study, not the only one. The content-fixed/format-varied design dates to at least Dec 2023.

verdicts.claim: CLAIM 3: 'finds markdown loses to HTML'
verdicts.reason: The abstract I fetched (arXiv 2606.09578v1) says "HTML is often the most robust text format" and "the size of this gap depends on the task, model, and format." 'Often the most robust' is a hedged, task-conditional statement; 'markdown loses to HTML' is an unconditional ordering. The researcher's own quoted evidence contains the hedge that the claim sentence drops. No per-format accuracy number was extracted, and the paper body was never opened — only the abstract.
verdicts.correction: TABVERSE reports HTML as often the most robust text format, with the gap depending on task, model and format. No general markdown-loses-to-HTML ordering is established.

verdicts.claim: CLAIM 4: 'TABVERSE and 2604.04948 measured as false' the French benchmark's 'largely irrelevant for downstream use' clause, citing 'a 33-percentage-point spread on table questions'
verdicts.reason: The verbatim French-benchmark quote is CORRECT — I confirmed every word of it against arXiv 2602.11960v1. But the refutation misattributes the number. 2604.04948's abstract says the 33-point gap is "between basic and hierarchical splitting" — that is the CHUNKER. The French paper's clause is about "alternative table renderings" — that is the SERIALIZATION. A spread produced by varying factor A cannot refute an assumption about factor B. This is the exact single-factor error the headline accuses the four papers of committing.
verdicts.correction: The 'largely irrelevant' clause remains an unmeasured assumption. TABVERSE is relevant counter-evidence; the 33-point chunking gap is not.

verdicts.claim: CLAIM 7: 'Merged cells silently corrupt tables in BOTH PPTX and DOCX paths... DOCX 3x3 table with a vertical merge in column 0: markitdown emitted an EMPTY header row |  |  |  |, pushed the real header into the body'
verdicts.reason:
I ran the single-factor control the researcher never ran: built two identical 3x3 'Table Grid' DOCX files differing ONLY in whether cell(1,0) is merged into cell(2,0). Verbatim output, merge=False: '|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Milestone | Date | Fee |
| Kickoff | 2026-09-01 | 40% |
| Delivery | 2026-12-01 | 60% |'. The empty header row and the demoted real header appear WITH NO MERGE AT ALL. They are caused by the absence of a header-row marking (markdownify prepends a synthetic empty header to any headerless HTML table), not by the merge. Only the concatenation ('| Kickoff  Delivery |') and the 2-cell row are merge-caused — those I reproduced exactly.
verdicts.correction: Two independent defects were bundled as one. (a) Headerless-table defect, merge-independent: an empty synthetic header row is prepended and the real header is demoted into the body. (b) Merge defect: cell text concatenates and the row loses a cell. Both are real; the causal attribution in Claim 7 is wrong for (a).

verdicts.claim: DESIGN §3: 'Tables, merged/multi-row header -> HTML <table> with rowspan/colspan/caption. 1.82x tokens'
verdicts.reason: 1.82x is measured on the PLAIN-table sweep, not the merged case. I re-derived from the researcher's own files with their own tokenizer: sweep/0005_html.md (a flat <table>, no rowspan/colspan/caption) 293 tok / sweep/0005_gfm.md 161 tok = 1.8199. But the actual merged artifacts give fin/html_merged.md 98 tok / fin/gfm_merged.md 37 tok = 2.6486x (+164.86%). The design quotes a price from a configuration it is not pricing, understating the real cost by 45%. Same defect in the adjacent row: '```csv fence. 0.81x GFM' is measured at n=100 (2270/2787 = 0.8145) while the rule that cites it is scoped to '>200 rows', where the measured value is 11501/14052 = 0.8185.
verdicts.correction: Merged/multi-row-header HTML costs ~2.65x GFM on the researcher's own artifacts. The csv fence costs 0.82x GFM at 500 rows. The flat 5-token fence overhead is exact and reproduces at all four sizes (5, 5, 5, 5).

verdicts.claim: DESIGN §5: 'POLICY GATE (from a measured leak, not a hypothetical)... markitdown leaks SECRET_hidden into the markdown today'
verdicts.reason: This could not have been measured in the environment it claims to come from. markitdown's XlsxConverter hard-requires pandas; I checked and pandas is MISSING from $TMPDIR/mdx/lib and from the interpreter path (openpyxl present at /opt/homebrew/..., pandas and xlrd absent). Running the converter on the researcher's own torture.xlsx raises MissingDependencyException: 'XlsxConverter recognized the input as a potential .xlsx file, but the dependencies needed to read .xlsx files have not been installed.' The underlying inference is plausible — I read the source, line 82: 'sheets = pd.read_excel(file_stream, sheet_name=None, engine="openpyxl")', and sheet_name=None enumerates hidden sheets — but it is an inference from source, explicitly labelled 'measured'.
verdicts.correction: Reading markitdown's source, pd.read_excel(sheet_name=None) would enumerate the hidden SECRET_hidden sheet. This is a source-read inference, not a measurement; the XLSX path never executed.

verdicts.claim: CLAIMS 5, 6, 8 (own-measurements on PPTX flattening, the 0.05-inch reading-order flip, and DOCX tracked-change erasure)
verdicts.reason:
I re-ran all three against the researcher's own fixtures and reproduced them byte-for-byte. PPTX: '# Revenue Drivers
Enterprise
EMEA up 12%
Renewals at 94%
SMB
Churn down 3pt' — three outline levels flattened to siblings, no list markers. Cause confirmed at _pptx_converter.py:177 'md_content += shape.text + "
"'. jitter.pptx: 'RIGHT-A
RIGHT-B
LEFT-A
LEFT-B' — the flip reproduces; 0.05in = 45,720 EMU checks out (0.05 x 914400). DOCX: probed the output — 'Arjun' False, 'penalty of 5%' False, 'INSERTED BY PRIYA' True. mammoth _ignored_elements verified at body_xml.py:61-80 containing 'w:del', 'w:commentRangeStart', 'w:commentRangeEnd', 'w:sectPr'; 'w:ins': read_child_elements at line 689. TWO fidelity defects: (a) the source is quoted as 'sorted(slide.shapes, key=lambda x: (x.top, x.left))' but the real code is 'key=lambda x: (float("-inf") if not x.top else x.top, float("-inf") if not x.left else x.left)' — a paraphrase presented inside a verbatim quote; (b) the 'Output verbatim' for Claim 5 silently drops markitdown's '<!-- Slide number: 2 -->' delimiter, which does provide a machine-readable slide boundary (mdast parses it as an html node), softening the 'no outline' framing. I also found two undocumented drops the researcher missed: the header 'CONFIDENTIAL — Internal Draft v3' and footer 'Legal Dept' vanish entirely, and the Title-style 'Master Services Agreement' is emitted as plain text so the document has no H1 at all.

verdicts.claim: CLAIM 5: 'markitdown (170,534 stars — the most-used converter in the category)'
verdicts.reason: The star count is exactly right — I scraped github.com/microsoft/markitdown and got '"stargazerCount":170534' and aria-label='170534 users starred this repository'. Comparators: MinerU 76,381, docling 64,077, marker 38,072. So markitdown is decisively the most-STARRED. But 'most-used' is an inference from stars, with no download or dependent-repo evidence; stars measure attention at a moment of virality, not deployment. markitdown 0.1.7 being current is confirmed via pypi.org (uploaded 2026-07-29T18:20:30).
verdicts.correction: markitdown is the most-starred converter in the category at 170,534 stars (verified 2026-08-01), 2.2x the next (MinerU, 76,381). Usage share is unverified.

verdicts.claim: CLAIM 1: the 'no paper measures downstream task accuracy by document conversion' gap claim is REFUTED by arXiv 2604.04948
verdicts.reason: I fetched the record independently and every quoted number matches the abstract: 21 pipeline configurations, four frameworks (Docling, MinerU, Marker, DeepSeek OCR), PDFLoader 86.2%, manual Markdown 91.3%, Docling+hierarchical 94.1 +/- 1.6%, the 33-point splitting gap, GraphRAG 82%. Claims 2 and 4 also check out verbatim: OHRBench 8,561 images / 8,498 Q&A; RealDocBench 1,356 field-level questions over 581 documents, eighteen systems; InduOCRBench's 'high OCR accuracy does not necessarily translate into strong downstream RAG performance'; and the French benchmark's 'largely irrelevant for downstream use' clause. THREE method defects survive the confirmation: (a) the opening of the quote is altered — the abstract reads 'Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems depend critically', not 'RAG systems depend critically', inside quotation marks; (b) the evidence is a paper's own NOVELTY claim ('no prior study has evaluated PDF processing frameworks by their impact on downstream question-answering accuracy'), and that claim is itself false — OHRBench did exactly this 16 months earlier, and the researcher cites OHRBench in the very next claim without noticing; (c) [primary-read] is tagged on an arXiv API abstract fetch for all four papers — no paper body was opened, so every reported number is an unverified author self-report.

survived: The four-papers-exist finding: arXiv 2604.04948v2, 2412.02592v4 (OHRBench), 2605.00911v1 (InduOCRBench), 2606.07401v1 (RealDocBench) all exist and every quoted sentence and count is verbatim-accurate against the arXiv API. The old 'no paper measures downstream accuracy by conversion' gap claim is genuinely dead.

The characterization that OHRBench varies NOISE LEVEL rather than representation: confirmed against the OHR-Bench README, which describes formatting_noise_[mild/moderate/severe] as 'perturbation based on real-world OCR errors' — a gradient, not a controlled representation swap.
PPTX bullet-hierarchy flattening (Claim 5): reproduced byte-for-byte, cause confirmed at _pptx_converter.py:177.

The 0.05-inch reading-order flip (Claim 6): reproduced exactly — 'RIGHT-A
RIGHT-B
LEFT-A
LEFT-B'. 45,720 EMU arithmetic correct.
DOCX tracked-change erasure (Claim 8): reproduced exactly. Arjun's deletion absent, Priya's insertion present and unmarked. mammoth _ignored_elements at body_xml.py:61-80 confirmed line-accurate.
The merge-caused half of Claim 7: cell concatenation and the 2-cell row in a 3-column table are genuinely merge-caused, proven by my own two-arm control.

The setext trap behind 'NEVER ---': verified with mdast-util-from-markdown. 'Slide one body text\n---\nSlide two' parses as heading(h2) | paragraph — the body text is swallowed into an H2. '***' is safe. Nuance the design omits: '---' preceded by a blank line is safe (parses as thematicBreak).
The flat 5-token fence overhead: exact and stable at 5 tokens across n=5/20/100/500. The cleanest measurement in the submission.

The GitHub HTML carrier, which the design asserted with a bare '(verified allowlist)' and no source: I verified it against html-pipeline's SanitizationFilter. 'ins', 'del', 'table', 'caption', 'details', 'summary', 'sup' are in elements; 'datetime', 'title', 'id', 'rowspan', 'colspan' are in the global attributes list; and 'ins'/'del' cite is restricted to ['http','https',:relative] — so the design's 'mailto blocked' is exactly right. Caveat: html-pipeline is the best public proxy for GitHub.com's renderer, not GitHub.com itself.

The typed-fence mechanism: ```mdmax-dropped and ```mdmax-notes parse as opaque mdast code nodes with lang preserved, consistent with the settled invariant that extensibility lives in the VALUE of a field, never in the SET of node types.
killed: HEADLINE '100% of the information loss happens in non-table payloads' — refuted by the researcher's own Claim 7 and by my re-run of both table corruptions.

HEADLINE '+3.1% tokens' as the recovery price for five payload classes — it is a slides-and-notes-only measurement (1325/1285). Tracked changes alone cost 6.92x on their span; formulas, furniture, the ledger fence and the front matter are unmeasured.

CLAIM 3 'The one paper that DOES isolate representation, TABVERSE' — arXiv 2312.16702 (Dec 2023) did content-fixed structural perturbation on tables 2.5 years earlier, and FLEXTAF, cited in the same claim, does it too.
CLAIM 3 'markdown loses to HTML' — the source says 'HTML is often the most robust text format' with the gap depending on task, model and format.
CLAIM 4's refutation logic — the 33-point gap is between basic and hierarchical SPLITTING (the chunker), and cannot refute a claim about alternative table RENDERINGS.
CLAIM 7's attribution of the empty header row to merged cells — my two-arm control shows it appears identically with no merge.

DESIGN '1.82x tokens' for merged/rowspan/colspan HTML tables — the researcher's own artifacts measure 2.6486x. Same defect on '0.81x' (measured at n=100, cited for a >200-row rule where it is 0.8185).
DESIGN 'POLICY GATE (from a measured leak, not a hypothetical)' — markitdown's XLSX path raises MissingDependencyException in that exact environment; pandas is not installed. Never measured.
CLAIM 5's 'most-used converter' — stars, not usage. The 170,534 figure itself is exactly right.

DESIGN's stated GUARANTEE 'count(source payloads) == count(carried) + count(ledger)' as a CI-checkable completeness property — see new_defects; it cannot detect the corruption class the researcher himself measured.
new_defects: METHOD, most serious: the submission preaches single-factor discipline and then violates it. Its entire headline is that the four papers 'vary the EXTRACTOR or the CHUNKER while holding representation implicit'. Claim 7 varies TWO factors (merge presence AND header-row presence) in one fixture and attributes the joint result to the merge. I ran the missing control in one command; it took under a minute. A researcher who has just named a confound in four papers should run the arm that rules it out in his own.

METHOD: cost numbers are transplanted across configurations. '1.82x' is measured on a plain table and quoted for a rowspan/colspan/caption table where the same artifacts give 2.65x. '0.81x' is measured at 100 rows and quoted for a rule scoped to >200 rows. In both cases the transplant moves the number in the direction that flatters the design.

METHOD: 'measured' is applied to something that could not have executed. The POLICY GATE section is explicitly headed 'from a measured leak, not a hypothetical' while markitdown's XLSX converter raises MissingDependencyException in that environment for want of pandas. This is the inference-presented-as-measurement failure, and it is the one carrying the highest-stakes assertion in the whole design (an enterprise data-leak claim).

METHOD: two verbatim-quote breaches in a session whose evidence rules say 'Quote verbatim'. The markitdown sort key is quoted as 'sorted(slide.shapes, key=lambda x: (x.top, x.left))' when the real code carries float('-inf') guards on both components; and the 2604.04948 abstract quote silently rewrites 'Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems' to 'RAG systems' inside quotation marks. Neither changes the conclusion, which is exactly why the habit is dangerous.

METHOD: [primary-read] is tagged on arXiv API abstract fetches for all four papers. No paper body was opened. Every number in Claims 1-4 — 94.1%, 86.2%, 91.3%, the 33-point gap, 8,561/8,498, 1,356/581/18 — is an author self-report reproduced faithfully but never verified. Under this session's own taxonomy that is closer to secondary than primary.

METHOD, circular evidence: Claim 1 rests on 2604.04948's own novelty assertion ('no prior study has evaluated PDF processing frameworks by their impact on downstream question-answering accuracy'). Claim 2, in the next paragraph, cites OHRBench (Dec 2024) doing precisely that 16 months earlier. The submission repeats a false novelty claim and refutes it one paragraph later without noticing.

PRIOR ART MISSED: arXiv 2411.10541 (Nov 2024), 'Does Prompt Formatting Have Any Impact on LLM Performance?' — 'We formatted the same contexts into various human-readable templates, including plain text, Markdown, JSON, and YAML... GPT-3.5-turbo's performance varies by up to 40% in a code translation task depending on the prompt template.' Content fixed, serialization varied, NON-TABLE payloads, no extractor and no chunker in the loop at all. That is the exact single-factor design the headline calls unclaimed, published 20 months earlier. Also missed: arXiv 2312.16702 (Dec 2023) for the table case.

DESIGN: the completeness GUARANTEE is weaker than advertised. 'count(source payloads) == count(carried) + count(ledger)' conserves COUNT, not CORRECTNESS. My measured DOCX case satisfies it perfectly — one table in, one table out, zero ledger entries — while the emitted table has a phantom empty header, a concatenated cell and a 2-cell row inside a 3-column table. The one thing 'no competitor does and it is checkable in CI' passes green on the researcher's own worst finding. It needs a fidelity assertion (round-trip cell count and header arity per table), not just a conservation count.

DESIGN: the forensic profile is internally unsatisfiable. §1 says forensic means 'nothing is dropped... Ledger must be empty'. §4 says PPTX animations, transitions and z-order 'go to a sidecar or the ledger, never the .md'. The design's own ledger example lists 'pptx.animation  9'. No deck with an animation can be ingested in forensic mode under these two rules simultaneously.

DESIGN: 'ledger: 7' in the front matter is a denormalized count duplicated from the ledger fence. Under splice-only writing every edit that adds or removes a dropped payload must also splice that integer, and any splice that misses it leaves the document asserting a false completeness figure. It also edges the front matter from NAMING a capability toward CARRYING state, which is the side of the JSON-LD/vim-modeline line the project thesis rules out. Make it derivable from the fence, or drop it.

UNDOCUMENTED FINDINGS the sweep missed, both from my own re-run: markitdown silently drops DOCX headers and footers entirely (the fixture's 'CONFIDENTIAL — Internal Draft v3' header and 'Legal Dept' footer are absent from the output, and the design's ledger example presents that drop as if it had been reported), and Title-style (Heading 0) is emitted as plain text, so 'Master Services Agreement' is not a heading and the document has no H1 while '# 1. Scope' is one. The latter directly undercuts the design's slide model of '## <title> under one document #' — for DOCX there is no document '#' to nest under.

per_area.title: Provenance that survives the markdown boundary
per_area.headline: C2PA 2.4 §A.9's front-matter form — the one place a standard privileges Markdown — is unusable as specified: its `-----BEGIN C2PA MANIFEST-----` armour is not valid YAML (two parsers throw) and collides with the `---` fence so gray-matter (7.49M weekly downloads) silently drops all front matter and leaks the manifest URL into the rendered body, it renders as a visible `<h2>` with a clickable link in GFM, it permits at most ONE manifest per file bound to a whole-file byte hash, and zero implementations exist — so the correct move is not to adopt C2PA's carrier but to ship per-block provenance in HTML comments and link-reference definitions (both measured to render to nothing in GFM and round-trip byte-identically through remark), keyed by content-derived anchors rather than the character offsets every existing standard uses.

findings.claim: C2PA 2.4's own front-matter example (§A.9.3.3.3) is not valid YAML — two independent parsers reject it — and under gray-matter (7,492,225 npm downloads/week) it silently destroys the document: front matter parses to `{}`, the real `title:` key is lost, and the manifest URL leaks into the rendered body. The `-----BEGIN` armour literally begins with `---`, the YAML front-matter close fence.
findings.evidence:
Ran locally against the spec's verbatim example. `yaml@2.9.0 parse -> THROW YAMLParseError: Implicit keys need to be on a single line at line 1, column 1`; `js-yaml@3.14.2 safeLoad -> THROW YAMLException: end of the stream or a document separator is expected at line 4, column 6`; `gray-matter@4.0.3` on the full document returned `data = {}`, `matter = ""`, `isEmpty = true`, and `content= "--BEGIN C2PA MANIFEST-----
https://fabrikam.com/manifests/a1b2c3.c2pa
-----END C2PA MANIFEST-----

findings.claim: C2PA §A.9 structurally forbids per-block provenance in markdown and binds to a whole-file byte hash, so any keystroke invalidates it. This is architecturally incompatible with product goal G1 (collaborative live editing) and with per-span provenance.
findings.evidence: Read from https://spec.c2pa.org/specifications/specifications/2.4/specs/C2PA_Specification.html §A.9.3: "There shall be at most one manifest block per file. If a validator detects more than one, it shall report a manifest.structuredText.multipleReferences failure." §A.9.4: "A claim generator embedding a manifest block in a structured text file shall include a c2pa.hash.data assertion with a single exclusion range covering the entire manifest block. Files shall be read in binary mode to preserve the exact byte representation of line terminators." The parallel HTML section (§A.7.1.3) states the design intent explicitly: "Any process that re-serializes the HTML ... will alter byte offsets and invalidate the content binding. This is by design".

findings.claim: The starting evidence is slightly off on which section names Markdown. §A.9.3.2 (Multi-Line Form / Front Matter) names CommonMark and states the SHOULD-prefer; Markdown itself is named in §A.9.1 and in the §A.9.3.3.1 example table — where the Markdown row uses the single-line HTML-comment form, NOT front matter. So the spec's only concrete Markdown example is `<!-- ... -->`, which is the carrier this design should adopt anyway.
findings.evidence: §A.9.1: "markup (Markdown, AsciiDoc, LaTeX)". §A.9.3.2: "Formats that support front matter blocks — such as CommonMark (YAML front matter), TOML front matter ( + ), and similar conventions — may use a multi-line manifest block within the front matter. Claim generators should prefer the front matter form when possible, as front matter is more reliably preserved by format-specific toolchains." §A.9.3.3.1 table row: "Markdown | \<!-- -----BEGIN C2PA MANIFEST----- https://fabrikam.com/manifests/a1b2c3.c2pa -----END C2PA MANIFEST----- -→"

findings.claim: §A.8 (unstructured text, variation selectors) is normatively drafted but self-declared provisional, and §A.9 is only four months old. §A.8 shipped in spec 2.3 (December 2025); §A.9 shipped in 2.4 (April 2026).
findings.evidence: §A.8.1: "This approach should only be used with unstructured text assets where no other embedding method is feasible. It remains under review and may be subject to change based on implementation feedback and interoperability testing." Spec changelog §5.3.1 header: "2.4 - April 2026" listing "Added support for embedding C2PA Manifests into structured text formats (source code, YAML, Markdown, AsciiDoc, etc.)"; §5.3.2 "2.3 - December 2025" listing "Added comprehensive support for embedding C2PA manifests in unstructured text files." Both appendices carry `shall`-level requirements; the spec's only blanket non-normative carve-outs are for CDDL ("All CDDLs are non-normative").

findings.claim: ZERO implementations of §A.8 or §A.9 exist in the reference SDK. c2pa-rs supports 20 media types, none of them text; it implements a subset of spec 2.2, two versions behind the markdown work; and a GitHub code search for the armour string across the whole contentauth org returns nothing.
findings.evidence: raw.githubusercontent.com/contentauth/c2pa-rs/main/docs/supported-formats.md lists avi, avif, c2pa, dng, flac, gif, heic, heif, jpg/jpeg, jxl, m4a, mp3, mp4, mov, pdf (read-only), png, svg, tif/tiff, wav, webp — no `md`, no `text/*`, no `text/html`. README line 41: "implements a subset of the C2PA technical specification" linking the 2.2 spec. GitHub code search API: `repo:contentauth/c2pa-rs "BEGIN C2PA MANIFEST"` → total_count 0; `org:contentauth "BEGIN C2PA MANIFEST"` → total_count 0; `repo:contentauth/c2pa-rs markdown` → total_count 1 (cli/docs/usage.md). Repo has 375 stars, pushed 2026-07-31.

findings.claim: C2PA 2.4 contains no confidence primitive anywhere. Four occurrences of the word exist and all four are Google depth-map metadata fields, not extraction or derivation confidence.
findings.evidence: `grep -c -i -w confidence` over the stripped 621,044-char spec text = 4. All four are in the GDepth CDDL block: "GDepth:ConfidenceMime", "GDepth:Confidence" (twice, one in an example), and `confidence-mime-type = $mime-choice .default "image/png"`. It DOES ship a new `c2pa.ai-disclosure` assertion in 2.4 with `modelType` (required), `modelName`, `modelIdentifier` ("pkg:huggingface/meta-llama/Llama-2-70b-chat-hf@main"), `scientificDomain` (arXiv taxonomy) and `contentProfile.humanOversightLevel` ∈ {fully_autonomous, prompt_guided, human_validated} — method and oversight, but no score.

findings.claim: C2PA 2.4 DOES have the spatial/page/textual vocabulary MDMAX needs (§18.2 Regions of Interest, applicable to any assertion via §18.3.8 `regionOfInterest`) — but its textual range is addressed by a fragment identifier plus absolute character offsets, i.e. exactly the brittle addressing MDMAX's content-derived re-anchoring exists to replace, and it defines no fragment convention for Markdown.
findings.evidence: §18.2.3 CDDL: `text-selector-map = { "fragment": tstr, ? "start": int, ? "end": int }` with the comment "; this is modelled after the W3C Web Annotation selector model" and the prose "fragment identifier, as per RFC3023 or ISO 32000-2, Annex O" (XML and PDF fragment schemes respectively). `frame-map = { ? "start": int, ? "end": int }` — "this can be used for either frames of a video or pages of a document". `shape-map` supports rectangle/circle/polygon in pixel or percent units.

findings.claim: Independently re-verified and extended: all SIX published MCP schema versions — including 2026-07-28, the newest at 181,444 bytes — contain zero occurrences of provenance, citation, attribution, confidence, uncertainty, lineage, or audit.
findings.evidence: Fetched raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/schema/{2024-11-05,2025-03-26,2025-06-18,2025-11-25,2026-07-28,draft}/schema.json and word-boundary grepped. Result matrix (bytes, then all seven counts): 2024-11-05 87,875 → 0 0 0 0 0 0 0; 2025-03-26 89,426 → all 0; 2025-06-18 108,214 → all 0; 2025-11-25 174,303 → all 0; 2026-07-28 181,444 → all 0; draft 181,444 → all 0. The 2025-06-18 schema also has zero occurrences of "source", "evidence" and "markdown".

findings.claim: docling's markdown serializer contains literally zero provenance handling — 0 occurrences of the substring 'prov' in 975 lines, against 215 occurrences in the document model. ProvenanceItem is {page_no, bbox, charspan} with no method and no confidence field.
findings.evidence: raw.githubusercontent.com/docling-project/docling-core/main/docling_core/transforms/serializer/markdown.py: 975 lines, `grep -c -i prov` = 0. docling_core/types/doc/document.py: 5,503 lines, `grep -c prov` = 215. docling_core/types/doc/common/reference.py: `class ProvenanceItem(BaseModel)` with docstring "A `ProvenanceItem` object acts as a lightweight pointer back into the original document for an extracted element" and exactly three fields: `page_no: Annotated[int, Field(description="Page number")]`, `bbox: Annotated[BoundingBox, Field(description="Bounding box")]`, `charspan: CharSpan`.

findings.claim: CORRECTION to the starting evidence — 'nothing emits confidence' is wrong in letter and the true situation is sharper. docling DOES emit confidence, but only at page and document level, and it lives on ConversionResult as a SIBLING of `document`, so it dies at the DoclingDocument boundary — one hop BEFORE markdown. `doc.export_to_dict()` does not carry it. And table confidence does not exist at all.
findings.evidence: docling/datamodel/document.py line 404: `confidence: ConfidenceReport = Field(default_factory=ConfidenceReport)` sits inside `class ConversionAssets(BaseModel)` alongside line 416 `document: DoclingDocument = _EMPTY_DOCLING_DOC`, and is persisted separately (`write_json("confidence.json", self.confidence)`). base_models.py: `class PageConfidenceScores` = {parse_score, layout_score, table_score, ocr_score}; `class ConfidenceReport(PageConfidenceScores)` adds `pages: dict[int, PageConfidenceScores]`. docs/concepts/confidence_scores.md: "**`table_score`**: Table extraction quality *(not yet implemented)*" and "Numerical scores are used internally and are for informational purposes only".

findings.claim: marker (38,072 stars) confirms the same boundary from a second codebase: its JSON renderer carries a stable block id, polygon and bbox; its Markdown renderer carries none of it and returns metadata only as a sidecar Python object, not inside the .md.
findings.evidence: raw.githubusercontent.com/datalab-to/marker/master/marker/renderers/json.py: `class JSONBlockOutput(BaseModel): id: str; block_type: str; html: str; polygon: List[List[float]]; bbox: List[float]; children; section_hierarchy; images`. markdown.py: `class MarkdownOutput(BaseModel): markdown: str; images: dict; metadata: dict`. `grep -c -i 'bbox\|polygon'`: markdown.py = 0, json.py = 6, chunk.py = 5. renderers/__init__.py `generate_document_metadata` returns only `{"table_of_contents": ..., "page_stats": ...}`.

findings.claim: W3C PROV-O — the canonical provenance ontology — has no confidence, no uncertainty, no score, no spatial and no offset primitive at all across 32 classes and 98 properties. Its only appearance of 'confidence' is a user-defined property invented inside an example.
findings.evidence: Fetched https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-o/ and counted distinct `prov:` terms: 32 Classes (Activity, Agent, Association, Attribution, Bundle, Collection, Derivation, Entity, Generation, Influence, Invalidation, Plan, PrimarySource, Quotation, …) and 98 properties (wasDerivedFrom, wasGeneratedBy, hadPrimarySource, actedOnBehalfOf, generatedAtTime, …). Regex counts over the stripped spec: confidence 2, uncertainty 0, score 0, probability 0, bounding 0, "page number" 0, offset 0. Both confidence hits are one example: `:confidenceValue "6"^^xsd:integer;` with the comment "Not sure if Don Quixote was the original source, so asserting a confidence value of 6 out of 10." Dublin Core is weaker still: `dcterms:provenance` is defined as "A statement of any changes in ownership and custody of the resource since its creation" — free text — and the DCMI terms page has 0 occurrences of "confidence".

findings.claim: ITS 2.0 (a W3C Recommendation since 2013) is the ONLY standard surveyed that ships a per-span confidence score AND makes tool attribution mandatory for it — a score without an annotator is a spec violation. It also supports fully out-of-band provenance via external rule files with selectors. This is the design precedent MDMAX should copy, and its ~zero adoption is also the cautionary tale.
findings.evidence: https://www.w3.org/TR/its20/ §8.18.1: "MT Confidence is provided as a rational number in the interval 0 to 1 (inclusive)" and "It is not intended to provide a score that is comparable between machine translation engines and platforms." §8.18.2: "Any node selected by the MT Confidence data category MUST be contained in an element with the annotatorsRef (or in HTML, its-annotators-ref) attribute specified for the MT Confidence data category." §5.7 note: the ITS Tools Annotation mechanism "is mandatory for the MT Confidence data category". §8.11 defines a separate Provenance data category with seven fields (human/org/tool for translation and revision, plus an external reference) and states "The specification does not define the format of external provenance information, but it is recommended that an open provenance or change-logging format be used, e.g. the W3C provenance data model [PROV-DM]". Adoption probe: npm `its-tools` 200, `translate-html-with-its` 404, `its20` 404.

findings.claim: in-toto's attestation model is the right binding primitive for MDMAX blocks and the wrong one for whole documents: subjects are matched purely by cryptographic digest and are assumed immutable. SPDX 3 by contrast addresses sub-file regions with byteRange/lineRange — absolute offsets that a single edit invalidates.
findings.evidence: raw.githubusercontent.com/in-toto/attestation/main/spec/v1/statement.md: "Set of software artifacts that the attestation applies to. Each element MUST have `digest` set. Subjects are assumed to be _immutable_, i.e. the artifacts identified by the subject SHOULD NOT change." and "IMPORTANT: Subject artifacts are matched purely by digest, regardless of content type." resource_descriptor.md: "Though all fields are optional, a ResourceDescriptor MUST specify one of `uri`, `digest` or `content` at a minimum." raw.githubusercontent.com/spdx/spdx-3-model/main/model/Software/Classes/Snippet.md: properties are exactly `byteRange` (/Core/PositiveIntegerRange), `lineRange`, `snippetFromFile`.

This eliminates front matter as the carrier for anything larger than a couple of scalar keys, and definitively for a per-block provenance map.

findings.claim: Two carriers are measured invisible AND lossless: an HTML comment and a link reference definition. GFM strips both from rendered output entirely; both round-trip byte-identically through remark; and the link-reference-definition is a first-class CommonMark AST node (`definition`) so it survives markdown→HTML pipelines that drop raw HTML.

GitHub markdown API (mode=gfm) on a document containing `[mdmax-prov:h1:9f2a]: mdmax:prov "src=... box=... m=... c=..."` and `` returned exactly `

T

A paragraph.

Another paragraph.

` — neither carrier appears. remark (remark-parse+gfm) AST top level: `heading, definition, paragraph, html, paragraph`; md→md `byte-identical: true`, both carriers preserved. remark-rehype default (allowDangerousHtml:false) HTML: `"

findings.claim: HTML comments survive the parse-then-stringify path that destroys everything else. Over the 476 corpus files that contain HTML comments, 100% preserved every comment's text through a remark round trip, while only 3 of 476 (0.63%) were byte-identical overall.

Output: "files containing HTML comments: 476 | round-tripped without throwing: 476 | byte-identical after parse->stringify: 3 | ALL comment texts preserved: 476 (100.0%) | same COUNT and all preserved: 476 (100.0%)".

findings.claim: The decay law is measurable and total on a real corpus: EVERY file that declares its own last-updated date is stale relative to git. 547 of 547 (100%) have a commit newer than the declared date; 180 of 547 (32.9%) by more than 7 days; mean 7.37 days, max 29. findings.claim: Cost envelope for inline per-block provenance: 8.1% file-size growth for a 24-byte anchor-only comment on every block, 31.2% for a 92-byte full record. Mean block is 295 bytes, so full-fat inline provenance is a ~third-of-the-document tax — inline must be reserved for blocks that earn it.
findings.evidence: Parsed 4,289 files with remark-parse+gfm+frontmatter: total top-level blocks 277,356; total bytes 81,913,833; mean 64.7 blocks/file; mean 295.3 bytes/block. Measured carrier sizes: `<!-- p:{b:"h1:9f2a"} -->` = 24 bytes; `<!-- p: {b:"tb:44e1", src:"spec.pdf#p12", box:[72,300,468,420], m:"tableformer", c:0.71} -->` = 92 bytes.
