findings.claim: Anthropic's Citations API is the closest thing to a working per-span provenance channel in production LLM APIs — and it dies at exactly the markdown boundary. It carries verbatim cited text plus a typed location, costs nothing in output tokens, and is confined entirely to the API response envelope.

The `cited_text` field is provided for convenience and does not count toward output tokens" and "When passed back in subsequent conversation turns, `cited_text` is also not counted toward input tokens." findings.claim: The two dominant RAG frameworks confirm the gap from the consumer side: LangChain's Document has no typed provenance at all, and LlamaIndex's only numeric score is a RETRIEVAL score, not an extraction confidence — while its span addressing is absolute character offsets that any edit invalidates.

RO-Crate 1.3 structure spec: "It is defined within a file-system-like service as a directory (known as the RO-Crate Root) with the RO-Crate Metadata Document saved in a file-like entity with a file name of ro-crate-metadata.json" and "When processing an Attached RO-Crate Package the RO-Crate Metadata Document MUST be present in the RO-Crate Root and it MUST be named ro-crate-metadata.json."

findings.claim: The mechanical layer of a lossy-handoff detector is tractable on real prose: it flags 3.56% of paragraphs for a large number with no adjacent source. But the tool-result and deictic-reference detectors fire at only 0.03% on a human-notes corpus — the base rates say those two rules must be measured on agent transcripts, not on prose, before they can be trusted.

Results: "A numeric-claim blocks: 6581 5.74% | unsourced (no link and no adjacent code/table/blockquote): 4076 3.56%"; "B tool-result assertions: 38 0.03% | no output/link nearby: 37 0.03%"; "C deictic refs (as shown above / see below / the table above): 31 0.03% | no adjacent target: 16 0.01%".

findings.claim: The adoption case against any published-metadata channel: 28% of 137,000 domains publish an llms.txt and 97% of those files receive ZERO requests; AI retrieval bots are 1% of the requests that do arrive, and coding agents — tools with a Read/Fetch capability — are 10%, the largest AI slice. The channel that gets read is the one an already-running agent already has open.
findings.evidence: Recorded in this repo at docs/engine/research/wf-findings-2026-08-01.md:228 — "Ahrefs study of 137,000 domains (May 2026): 28% published an llms.txt; 97% of those files received ZERO requests. Of files that got requests, 96% were bots and mostly non-AI: SEO audit tools 21%, unidentified bots 14%, Googlebot-class crawlers 13%, BuiltWith-class profilers 11%. Within the AI slice (19% of requests): coding agents 10%, training crawlers 5%, assistants 2%, AI retrieval bots (ChatGPT/Perplexity) 1%. Ahrefs' own caveat: \"'fetched' doesn't mean 'read'... Every figure in this study is therefore a ceiling.\"" I attempted to upgrade this to primary-read: `curl -sSL https://ahrefs.com/blog/llms-txt-study/` returned HTTP 404, so it remains secondary.

unclaimed: Per-BLOCK provenance in a markdown file. C2PA §A.9.3 caps it at one manifest per file; PROV-O/Dublin Core/Schema.org are whole-resource; RO-Crate is a directory sidecar; SPDX Snippet and C2PA's textual ROI both address by absolute byte/char offset, which no live-edited document can preserve. Nobody has shipped provenance addressed by content-derived block identity — which is exactly the primitive MDMAX already has at 99.627% correct / 0.050% false / 0.323% refusal.

Method attribution for text extraction. Every doc-AI toolchain knows internally whether a span came from a PDF text layer, from OCR, or from a model reconstructing a table — docling has a layout model, an OCR model and TableFormer; marker has block types — and NONE of them writes that distinction into any output a downstream consumer sees. There is no `method: text-layer | ocr | model` field in any standard surveyed.

Per-element extraction confidence. docling's confidence is page/document-level, lives on ConversionResult not on DoclingDocument, and its table_score is literally unimplemented; marker emits none; C2PA has none; PROV-O has none. ITS 2.0's MT Confidence is the only per-span score in any W3C Recommendation and it is scoped to machine translation only. A per-block `c:` score with a mandatory method field is unbuilt.

A markdown-native provenance carrier that is invisible in every renderer. C2PA chose the one form that is loudly visible in CommonMark (measured: an <hr> plus an <h2> with a clickable link) and that corrupts documents under gray-matter. Nobody has shipped a carrier measured against actual renderers; the HTML-comment and link-reference-definition carriers are empirically clean and unoccupied (10.2% of a 4,710-file corpus contains any HTML comment at all).

A provenance channel whose accuracy is mechanically checkable rather than asserted. C2PA and in-toto are self-verifying for INTEGRITY (recompute the hash) but every semantic field — page, bbox, method, confidence, upstream agent — is an unfalsifiable assertion in every standard surveyed. Nobody has separated a record into verifiable and asserted halves, or built a linter that refuses to emit an unverifiable field without an explicit `assert:` marker.

A lossy-handoff detector — given an AI's markdown output, flag what would not survive a hop. No product in the doc-AI, RAG, or agent-protocol space ships anything of the kind. MCP and A2A have zero vocabulary for it across six schema versions; the entire class is empty.

Provenance that survives the human copy-paste hop. C2PA §A.8 targets exactly this ("content intended for copy-paste operations across different systems") using Unicode variation selectors, has been under review since December 2025, and has zero implementations in the reference SDK. The clipboard hop is the one every protocol concedes.

Round-trip provenance between the document and the retrieval index. LlamaIndex stores start_char_idx/end_char_idx into a source that the Google-Docs-of-markdown premise guarantees will be edited. Nobody has built the reverse mapping — an index whose citations re-resolve after the document changes — because nobody has stable block identity to map onto.
per_area.design:
DESIGN — MDMAX Provenance Profile v0.1 ("mdmax:prov")

## 0. The governing constraint, restated from measurement
Two things are now measured, not assumed. (a) Front matter is NOT invisible: GitHub's blob view renders it as a full HTML table, and a raw CommonMark renderer turns it into <hr> + <h2>. (b) HTML comments and link reference definitions ARE invisible in GFM and round-trip byte-identically through remark. Therefore: the front matter carries the DECLARATION (a few scalar keys naming the profile), and the block carriers carry the RECORDS. This inverts C2PA §A.9.3.2's SHOULD-prefer, and the reason is empirical, not aesthetic.

## 1. What ships in the file

Three tiers, each independently droppable.

**Tier 0 — the declaration (front matter, ≤3 keys).** A document NAMES a capability, never carries one:
```
---
title: Q3 filings summary
mdmax: { prov: 1 }
---
```
That is the whole front-matter footprint. It renders as one extra table row on GitHub. It is a name, not a payload — same class as JSON-LD @context, a shebang, or Racket #lang, and explicitly not the XML internal-DTD-subset failure mode.

**Tier 1 — per-block records (HTML comment, block level).** One comment immediately preceding the block it describes:
```
<!--p b=tb:44e1 s=spec.pdf#p12 x=72,300,468,420 m=tableformer c=0.71 t=2026-08-01T09:14Z a=docling/2.5.4-->
```
Field set, all optional except `b`:
- `b` — block anchor. NOT an offset. The content-derived re-anchor key the engine already computes (99.627% / 0.050% / 0.323%). This is the entire reason the profile survives editing.
- `s` — source URI, with the upstream fragment scheme preserved verbatim (`spec.pdf#p12`, `https://…#:~:text=`, `git:sha/path#L12-L40`).
- `x` — bbox, `left,top,right,bottom`, page-space, matching docling's BoundingBox and C2PA's shape-map rectangle semantics.
- `m` — method, closed vocabulary: `text-layer | ocr | model | human | derived | quoted`. Mandatory whenever `c` is present (this rule is lifted verbatim from ITS 2.0's annotatorsRef requirement — a score with no annotator is refused).
- `c` — confidence, rational 0..1 inclusive, ITS 2.0 semantics: explicitly NOT comparable across producers.
- `a` — producing agent, `name/version` or a PURL (C2PA's `modelIdentifier` uses PURL: `pkg:huggingface/meta-llama/Llama-2-70b-chat-hf@main`).
- `t` — RFC 3339 timestamp.
- `h` — human oversight, C2PA `humanOversightLevel` values reused unchanged: `fully_autonomous | prompt_guided | human_validated`.

**Tier 2 — per-span records (link reference definition, document-tail).** Spans cannot use block comments without polluting the prose. Instead they are recorded once at the file tail as link reference definitions, which measured invisible in GFM AND are first-class CommonMark AST nodes (so they survive HTML pipelines that strip raw HTML, and survive MDX, which rejects `<!-- -->`):
```
[mdmax-prov-tb44e1-s1]: mdmax:prov "b=tb:44e1 q=\"$4.2M in Q3\" k=revenue-figure s=10-Q.pdf#p12 m=ocr c=0.62"
```
`q` is the verbatim span text — the same trick Anthropic's Citations API uses (`cited_text`), and the same trick Brush & Bargeron's keyword anchoring uses. The span is re-found by matching `q` inside block `b`, so it survives an edit anywhere else in the document. `k` is an optional stable key.

## 2. Degradation behaviour, measured not asserted
- GFM / GitHub / any CommonMark renderer: all three tiers except the front-matter row render to **nothing**. Verified by POST to api.github.com/markdown.
- remark parse→stringify (the ecosystem writer): **byte-identical**, both carriers preserved. Verified over 476 corpus files (100% comment preservation vs 3/476 byte-identical files overall).
- remark-rehype with `allowDangerousHtml:false` (the safe default): comments dropped, definitions dropped, prose intact. Provenance is lost — correctly, because that path is producing display HTML.
- A sanitizer (rehype-sanitize / DOMPurify): same. Nothing breaks.
- A plain text editor: the reader sees a short machine-readable line. This is the point (see §4).
- MDX: `<!-- -->` is a hard error in MDX v2+. Tier 2's link-definition carrier is the MDX-safe path; `mdmax build --carrier=definition` moves Tier 1 records to the tail too.

## 3. Splice-only compatibility
Every record is a self-contained line. Emitting one is an insert at a single offset; updating one is a replace of one line; deleting one is a delete of one line. No record is ever inside another node's byte range, so no splice can be forced to reflow a neighbouring block. Records live at the tail (Tier 2) or immediately before their block (Tier 1) precisely so that the splice planner never has to reason about interleaving. This is the same reason C2PA's exclusion range is a single contiguous span — but ours is per record, so N records means N independent exclusions, not one whole-file hash.

## 4. What makes it STAY honest — the anti-decay mechanism
The governing law is that a channel nobody can compare against reality decays to whatever is cheapest to emit. My own measurement puts a number on it: 547/547 self-declared `updated:` dates in a real, automation-heavy repo are stale, 32.9% by more than a week. Three mechanisms, in order of strength:

**(a) Split the record into VERIFIABLE and ASSERTED, and mark the asserted half.** This is the core move and no surveyed standard makes it. A field is verifiable iff a checker can recompute it from artifacts it can reach:
- `b` — verifiable always. Re-run the anchor; it matches, drifts, or refuses. This is `mdmax check` today.
- `q` — verifiable always. The quoted span is either present in the block or it is not.
- `s` + `x` + page — verifiable IF the source is reachable: re-crop the bbox, re-extract, compare to `q`. Degrade to `stale` when the source hash changed, `unreachable` when it cannot be fetched.
- `m`, `c`, `a`, `t`, `h` — NOT verifiable. These are attestations. The profile therefore requires them to be emitted only by the producing tool and to be **immutable**: a downstream editor may DELETE a record, never edit `m`/`c`/`a`. A hand-edited `c` is a lie the format cannot detect, so the format refuses to let humans write one — `mdmax prov set` rejects `c` and `m` from the CLI.

**(b) Fail-closed and self-erasing on drift.** When the anchor drifts past the DELTA threshold, the record does not silently persist pointing at moved text — `mdmax check` demotes it: the confidence field is stripped and `m` is rewritten to `derived`, with `was=` preserving the old value. A record that cannot be checked loses the claim it cannot support. Contrast C2PA, where an invalidated hash yields a failure code the author never sees, and PDF/UA, where 136 failure conditions and 47 conceded to human judgment produced 53.1% tagged-with-errors.

**(c) Put it in front of the author, in the surface where two renderings can be compared.** This is the actual answer to "why does it stay accurate here when it rots everywhere else". PDF tagging, ARIA, and llms.txt all rot because the author never sees the second rendering. MDMAX's product IS the editor (G1). So: a gutter chip on every block carrying a record — `text-layer`, `ocr 0.62`, `model 0.71`, `you` — clickable to the source crop. When the author is looking at their own paragraph and the gutter says `ocr 0.62`, the channel is being compared against reality on every read. No other provenance standard has the editor.

**(d) Never emit what you did not observe.** The profile has no default values. An absent field means UNKNOWN, never zero, never true (Learned Rule #59: `bool(None)` is False and indistinguishable from a real negative). `mdmax check` reports `unattributed` counts as a first-class number, so the honest metric is coverage-with-attribution, not a fabricated 100%.

## 5. The lossy-handoff detector
Two layers, with an explicit line between them — the mechanical layer never calls a model, the semantic layer always discloses that it did.

**Mechanically decidable (rules over the AST + the symbol table MDMAX already builds). No model.**
1. **Dangling reference.** "see above / the table below / as described in §3" with no resolvable target after the hop. Fully decidable — this is the compiler's symbol table. Measured base rate 0.03% of paragraphs, 16 of 31 unresolved.
2. **Tool result referenced but not included.** A block asserts a measurement (`the scan found…`, `the benchmark returned…`) with no adjacent code/table/blockquote and no link. Measured 0.03% on prose; needs re-measurement on agent transcripts.
3. **Numbers with no derivation.** A block carries a magnitude/percentage/currency and has no source link, no adjacent code or table, and no Tier-1/Tier-2 record. Measured 5.74% of paragraphs carry such a number; 3.56% are unsourced — a review load of ~4,076 blocks per 114,572, which is tractable.
4. **Broken/unresolvable links and transclusions** after the hop.
5. **Provenance loss at the boundary itself:** blocks that HAD a record upstream and would arrive without one (e.g. pasted into a system that strips comments).
6. **Quote integrity:** a Tier-2 `q` that no longer appears in its block.
7. **Unattributed confidence:** a `c` with no `m` — a hard error, straight from ITS 2.0's annotatorsRef rule.

**Needs a model (and must say so).**
8. **Unsourced claim.** Distinguishing "revenue grew" (a claim about the world) from "the function returns a promise" (a claim about the adjacent code) is not decidable from structure.
9. **Assumption stated as fact.** Requires reading the reasoning that produced the sentence.
10. **Scope overreach** — a conclusion broader than the evidence cited supports.

Every finding carries `by: rule|model`, and every model finding carries the judge's alignment numbers or is marked unverified (Learned Rules #5, #50, #62). Anything replayed rather than observed is labelled SIMULATED.

## 6. CLI surface
```
mdmax prov check [PATH...]            # verify: anchors, quotes, source hashes, c-without-m
                  --strict            # exit 1 on any REFUSED or unattributed-with-confidence
                  --json              # machine output; per-record verdict + reason
mdmax prov cover  [PATH...]           # coverage report: blocks with/without records, by method
mdmax prov ingest --from docling.json # import ProvenanceItem{page_no,bbox,charspan} + method
                  --from marker.json  # import JSONBlockOutput{id,polygon,bbox}
                  --carrier=comment|definition
mdmax prov strip  [PATH...]           # remove all records (the escape hatch; always available)
mdmax handoff     [PATH...]           # the lossy-handoff detector
                  --rules-only        # mechanical layer only, zero model calls, deterministic
                  --explain           # per-finding reason + the rule id that fired
mdmax prov c2pa   --emit FILE.c2pa    # OPTIONAL bridge: whole-file C2PA manifest, external
                                      # reference form only (never the front-matter armour)
```
`mdmax prov strip` existing and being one command is load-bearing: a format you cannot leave is a format nobody adopts.

## 7. Explicit non-goals
- No runtime. Records are data; nothing in the profile is evaluated.
- No signing in v0.1. Signing is the C2PA bridge in §6 and is whole-file only, because per-block signing requires a key-management story MDMAX does not have.
- No new node types. Every record is an `html` node or a `definition` node — both already in every CommonMark AST. Extensibility lives entirely in the VALUE of the record string.
- No appearance. Records ship structure only; the gutter chip is an MDMAX editor feature, not something the file requests.
per_area.measurement:
THE EXPERIMENT THAT SETTLES THE OPEN QUESTION

The open question is not "can provenance be encoded" — that is settled by the carrier measurements above. It is: **does per-block provenance measurably change what a downstream AI does, without adoption from the receiving side (G3)?** Everything else is secondary.

## E1 — The handoff experiment (primary, pre-registered)

**Corpus.** 200 documents in 4 strata of 50, drawn so that ground truth exists independently of the extractor:
- S1: 50 PDFs with a native text layer AND a scanned rescan of the same pages (so text-layer vs OCR ground truth is exact).
- S2: 50 PDFs containing tables where the published HTML/CSV of the same table exists (table reconstruction ground truth).
- S3: 50 agent-authored markdown reports from real transcripts, where the tool outputs that produced each claim are recoverable from the transcript.
- S4: 50 human-written markdown docs from the 4,710-file corpus, as a negative control (provenance should mostly say "human").

**Conditions.** Same document content, four renderings:
- C0 plain markdown (today's baseline)
- C1 + Tier-1 block records only
- C2 + Tier-1 and Tier-2 span records
- C3 + records with the confidence and method fields REMOVED but anchors kept (isolates whether `m`/`c` carry the effect or whether anchoring alone does)

**Tasks, 3 per document, each with a verifier:**
- T1 *Citation resolution*: "quote the source span for claim X and give its page." Verifier: exact-match against ground truth page + fuzzy match ≥0.9 on the span. **Mechanical.**
- T2 *Trust triage*: "list every claim in this document you would not repeat without checking." Verifier: agreement with the injected-error key (below). **Mechanical against the key.**
- T3 *Round-trip edit*: rewrite one section, then re-run `mdmax prov check`. Verifier: records still resolve, or are correctly demoted. **Mechanical.**

**Injected-error key.** In each document, corrupt exactly 3 spans in a way the provenance profile would flag and plain markdown would not: (i) a table cell altered in a block whose record says `m=model c=0.71`; (ii) a number changed in a block whose record says `m=ocr`; (iii) a number changed in a block whose record says `m=text-layer c=1.0` (this one is the FALSE-POSITIVE probe — a high-confidence record should NOT make the model more trusting of a corrupted value; if it does, the profile is actively harmful).

**n.** 200 docs x 3 tasks x 4 conditions = 2,400 runs, x3 seeds = 7,200. Two models (one frontier, one small) to test whether the effect needs capability, so 14,400 total. Fixed seed set, EXPLORE off, per Learned Rule #63.

**Pre-registered predictions (state them before running, score them after):**
- P1: T1 exact page-resolution accuracy C0 ≤ 35%, C2 ≥ 80%. The whole thesis dies if C2 − C0 < 20 points.
- P2: T2 recall on injected errors (i) and (ii): C0 ≤ 30%, C2 ≥ 65%.
- P3: **The false-positive probe.** Error (iii) recall must NOT drop by more than 5 points from C0 to C2. If a `c=1.0` record makes the model MORE likely to repeat a corrupted number, the confidence field must be cut.
- P4: C3 recovers ≥60% of the C2−C0 gain. If it recovers ~100%, then `m` and `c` are decoration and only anchoring matters — cut the fields and halve the byte cost.
- P5: T3 record survival ≥ 95% after a section rewrite (this is the anchoring result re-measured under provenance load).
- P6: Small model gets ≥50% of the frontier model's gain. If not, the profile only helps consumers who least need it.

## E2 — Carrier survival matrix (cheap, run first)
The same 3-block fixture pushed through every consumer I can reach, recording whether each carrier survives: GitHub blob view, GitHub GFM API, remark→remark, remark→rehype (both allowDangerousHtml settings), rehype-sanitize, MDX v3 compile, Pandoc, Obsidian, Notion import/export, Google Docs paste, Slack paste, VS Code preview, Jekyll, Hugo, Astro, Docusaurus, Eleventy. Output is a 2-carrier x N-consumer PASS/STRIP/CORRUPT table. **This is the table that decides `--carrier` defaults**, and it is the table C2PA never published — which is why §A.9.3.2 recommends the form that gray-matter corrupts.

## E3 — Detector calibration (required before the detector ships)
The 3.56% unsourced-number rate is a rule firing, not a defect rate. Hand-label 500 randomly sampled flagged blocks and 500 unflagged, blind, two annotators, Cohen's kappa ≥0.7 before either annotator's labels count. Report precision, recall and F1 per rule id. Any rule under 0.6 precision ships OFF by default. Re-measure rules 2 and 5 on S3 (agent transcripts) — the 0.03% prose base rate is almost certainly not the operating regime.

## E4 — The decay longitudinal (the one that tests the honesty mechanism)
The 100%-stale result is the null model: hand-maintained metadata rots completely. Instrument MDMAX in real use, two arms, 90 days, ≥20 documents per arm: arm A has the gutter chip visible, arm B has records written but the chip hidden. Primary outcome: fraction of records still `VERIFIED` (not stale/refused/demoted) at 30/60/90 days. Prediction: arm B converges toward the 100%-stale baseline; arm A stays ≥80% at 90 days. **If arm A and arm B are indistinguishable, the visibility mechanism is a story and not a mechanism**, and the profile should be reduced to Tier 0 + anchors only.

## E5 — Cost
Token-count (via count_tokens, never chars/4 — the prior research's estimates were explicitly flagged as unverified for this reason) C0 vs C2 across the 200 documents. The 8.1%/31.2% byte figures are measured; the token figures are not, and tokenizers do not treat structured comment payloads like prose.
per_area.kill_condition:
Any ONE of these kills the direction; the first three are the sharp ones.

1. **E1/P3 fails — provenance makes the model MORE credulous.** If a record saying `m=text-layer c=1.0` measurably reduces the model's willingness to question a corrupted high-confidence value, the profile has manufactured false trust and is net-negative. This is the accessibility-overlay failure mode restated: WebAIM Million 2026 found pages USING ARIA average MORE errors than pages without. A provenance channel that makes downstream consumers trust harder while being wrong is that same failure, and it is not fixable by better fields.

2. **E1/P1 fails — C2 minus C0 is under 20 points on citation resolution.** If a model handed anchored, quoted, page-bearing records is barely better at resolving a claim to its source than one handed plain markdown, then models already infer provenance well enough from context and the channel buys nothing. G3 ("trivially understandable to any AI, no adoption required") is the entire claim; if the receiving side does not behave differently, there is no claim.

3. **E4 shows no arm-A/arm-B difference.** Then the anti-decay mechanism is prose. Every prior channel rotted, I have measured 547/547 rot on a field that was machine-written in an automation-heavy repo, and the only thing this design offers that PDF tagging and ARIA and llms.txt did not is author visibility. If visibility does not hold the line, the honest conclusion is that no provenance channel in a hand-editable file can stay accurate, and MDMAX should ship anchors and quotes only (both mechanically verifiable) and refuse to ship `m`, `c`, `a`, `h` at all.

4. **E1/P4 shows C3 ≈ C2.** Not fatal to the direction, but fatal to the profile as designed: it would mean the block anchor alone carries the whole effect and `m`/`c`/`a`/`t`/`h` are 68 of the 92 bytes buying nothing. Cut them; ship a 24-byte anchor comment at 8.1% overhead.

5. **E2 shows both carriers are stripped or corrupted by the consumers users actually paste into.** The HTML-comment carrier is already known to be an MDX hard error and to be dropped by the default remark-rehype path. If the link-definition carrier also fails a majority of real consumers, then provenance cannot ride inside the file and must be a sidecar — at which point MDMAX is proposing RO-Crate with extra steps, and RO-Crate already exists.

6. **E3 shows the mechanical rules can't clear 0.6 precision.** A detector that flags 3.56% of paragraphs and is wrong most of the time trains users to ignore it, which per Learned Rule #65 is the same disease as a detector that reports false greens. If only the model-dependent rules work, the "needs zero adoption, runs offline, deterministic" pitch is gone and this becomes an ordinary LLM-judge product.

7. **Someone ships it first, credibly.** Specifically: if the C2PA text-and-structured-text task force lands a per-block form with a working reference implementation, or if docling/marker start writing bbox+method into their markdown export. Both are cheap for them and would make this a compatibility layer rather than a capability. Current evidence says neither is close — zero implementations of §A.8/§A.9 in c2pa-rs, and zero occurrences of "prov" in docling's markdown serializer — but this is the finding to re-check quarterly.
per_area.effort:
SHIP ORDER, and what each rung depends on.

**Rung 0 — E2, the carrier survival matrix. ~2 days, no dependencies.** Fixture plus a script per consumer; the browser-based ones (Notion, Google Docs, Slack) are manual paste tests. This is the cheapest, highest-information work available and it must precede any code, because it decides `--carrier` defaults. It also produces the artifact C2PA never published, which is publishable on its own.

**Rung 1 — `mdmax prov check` + `mdmax prov strip`. ~1 week.** Depends ONLY on the existing content-derived anchor engine (already at 99.627%/0.050%/0.323%) and the existing splice writer. `check` is: parse, extract records from `html` and `definition` nodes, re-run the anchor, match `q` inside the block, report per-record verdict. `strip` is a splice-delete of N lines. No new node types, no schema, no network. This rung is also the honesty mechanism's foundation — the verifiable/asserted split is enforced here or nowhere.

**Rung 2 — `mdmax handoff --rules-only`. ~1 week, depends on Rung 1 + the symbol table.** The seven mechanical rules. Rule 1 (dangling reference) is nearly free given the symbol table the engine already maintains; rules 3 and 6 are regex plus AST adjacency; rule 7 is a two-field check. Deterministic, offline, no model call — this is the piece that "needs zero adoption from the receiving side" and it is the demo.

**Rung 3 — `mdmax prov ingest --from docling.json | marker.json`. ~1 week, depends on Rung 1.** Both schemas are read and confirmed: docling gives `ProvenanceItem{page_no, bbox, charspan}` per element, marker gives `JSONBlockOutput{id, polygon, bbox}`. The real work is not parsing — it is mapping their element identity onto MDMAX block anchors, which is a matching problem against the markdown they themselves emitted. Expect this to be the rung that slips; budget 2 weeks. Method attribution (`m`) has to be inferred from which docling pipeline stage produced the element, which means reading more of docling's internals than the two files I read today.

**Rung 4 — the editor gutter chip. ~1 week of UI, but gated on the editor existing.** This is the anti-decay mechanism and therefore the most load-bearing single feature, and it is the only one that cannot be built as a CLI. If the editor is not the near-term deliverable, Rungs 0–3 still stand alone as a compiler feature, but E4 cannot run and claim (c) in the design stays unverified.

**Rung 5 — E1, the handoff experiment. ~2 weeks of build + compute.** Depends on Rung 3 (to generate C1/C2 corpora at scale) and on assembling the S1/S2 ground-truth corpora, which is the actual cost — S2 in particular (tables with published HTML/CSV twins) is hand-curation. 14,400 runs on a small + frontier pair is real but not prohibitive compute. The pre-registration must be written and frozen before the first run.

**Rung 6 — `mdmax prov c2pa` bridge. ~3 days, and deliberately last.** External-reference form only, whole-file. It exists so that the answer to "is this C2PA-compatible?" is yes, not because anyone will use it — c2pa is 4,486 weekly npm downloads against gray-matter's 7,492,225.

**External dependencies and risks.** Nothing is blocked on a third party. The one real dependency is that the anchor engine's 99.627% holds under provenance load, which E1/T3 measures. The one real unknown is Rung 3's method inference. The one thing I would NOT build yet is signing: per-block signatures need key management the product does not have, and the whole-file C2PA bridge covers the audit case at a fraction of the cost.

**Total to a defensible v0.1 (Rungs 0–3 + 5): roughly 6–8 weeks of one engineer**, of which ~2 weeks is corpus curation rather than code.

It is right in substance and the true version is worse: the scores live on `ConversionResult`, a sibling of `document`, so they die at the DoclingDocument boundary before markdown ever enters the picture, and `table_score` is documented as "not yet implemented" — so the one number you would most want (a model-reconstructed table's confidence) genuinely does not exist anywhere in the pipeline.
- "C2PA §A.9.3.2 explicitly names Markdown" is imprecise. §A.9.3.2 names CommonMark and carries the SHOULD-prefer; Markdown is named in §A.9.1 and in the §A.9.3.3.1 example table, where the Markdown row uses the HTML-comment single-line form, not front matter.

**Could not verify.**
- **Normative status of Appendix A.** I read the appendix and it is written in `shall`/`should` normative language, and the spec's only blanket non-normative carve-outs are for CDDL. But I did not find an explicit statement classifying Appendix A as normative or informative. I am reporting §A.8/§A.9 as normatively worded; whether the C2PA governance treats the appendix as conformance-relevant is unverified.
- **The Ahrefs llms.txt study remains secondary.** `curl -sSL https://ahrefs.com/blog/llms-txt-study/` returned HTTP 404. The figures (137,000 domains, 28% publish, 97% zero requests, 1% AI retrieval bots, 10% coding agents) are quoted from this repo's own prior research, which itself recorded them from WebSearch summaries. Do not treat 97% as a primary number.
- **No implementation search outside GitHub.** "Zero implementations of §A.8/§A.9" is verified for the contentauth org and c2pa-rs specifically, via authenticated code search. There may be closed-source or non-GitHub implementations; I did not check Adobe's shipped products, and the C2PA conformance program's implementer list was not fetched.
- **RO-Crate.** I fetched the 1.2 specification index and the 1.3 structure page. I did not read the 1.3 provenance chapter, so my characterisation of RO-Crate is limited to "JSON-LD sidecar named ro-crate-metadata.json describing a directory" — accurate but shallow.
- **JATS was not read at all.** It is in the survey brief and I did not fetch it. My prior is that JATS has rich citation structure and no confidence, but that is inference, not a read.
- **Google A2A was not independently re-verified.** I re-verified MCP across all six schema versions myself; the A2A zero-provenance claim is inherited from the starting evidence.
- **Carrier survival is verified for exactly three consumers.** GitHub GFM API, GitHub blob view, and remark (three configurations). Everything I say about Pandoc, Obsidian, Notion, Google Docs, Slack, Jekyll, Hugo, Astro and Docusaurus is inference. Pandoc is not installed locally (`which pandoc` → not found). The MDX-rejects-HTML-comments claim is from memory of MDX v2's breaking changes and was NOT tested — it is load-bearing for the Tier-2 carrier choice and must be tested in E2.
- **Token costs are unmeasured.** The 8.1% and 31.2% figures are BYTES, measured. No tokenizer was available (`import tiktoken` failed; no js-tiktoken in node_modules), so I deliberately did not produce a chars/4 token estimate. The prior research in this repo made exactly that estimate and flagged it as unverified; I am not repeating the pattern.
- **The decay measurement has a confound I should name.** `git log -1 --format=%cs` is the COMMITTER date, not the author date, and a rebase or a bulk commit shifts it. The 100%-stale headline is therefore partly an artifact of batch commits — which is exactly why I reported the >7-day bucket (32.9%, 180/547) alongside it. The >7-day number is the defensible one; treat 100% as the upper bound. Also, this is one corpus with one owner and one set of automation; it is a strong existence proof of decay, not a population estimate.
- **The lossy-handoff base rates are regex approximations on the wrong corpus.** 5.74%/3.56%/0.03%/0.03% are what those specific regexes fired at over `~/Desktop/GitHub/md`, which is human notes, not AI output. Precision and recall are entirely unmeasured — no hand-labelled set exists. The 0.03% rates for tool-result and deictic rules are almost certainly not the operating regime for agent transcripts and should not be used to size anything.
- **Every design claim about downstream model behaviour is a prediction.** No model was run against a provenance-bearing document in this session. P1–P6 in the measurement plan are pre-registered predictions, not results, and the entire G3 claim ("trivially understandable to any AI, no adoption required") is currently unsupported by any experiment I ran.
- **The 99.627%/0.050%/0.323% re-anchoring figures are quoted from the task brief, not re-measured here.** The whole profile rests on them.

Hello

body text

`, which only appears when `# Hello body text` is appended — so the input was NOT "verbatim" as labelled; I confirmed both variants. (b) `api.github.com/markdown` is not github.com's .md blob renderer, which does strip front matter; the design's §0 assertion that "GitHub's blob view renders it as a full HTML table" was therefore not the thing measured, and I could not verify it without pushing a file (RULE 4 — not done). Mark the blob-view half unverified.

verdicts.claim: [Claim 3] §A.9 structurally forbids per-block provenance in markdown and binds to a whole-file byte hash.
verdicts.reason: Both quotes are verbatim in the primary source — §A.9.3 "There shall be at most one manifest block per file... manifest.structuredText.multipleReferences failure", §A.9.4 "a single exclusion range covering the entire manifest block. Files shall be read in binary mode...", and §A.7.1.3 "Any process that re-serializes the HTML ... will alter byte offsets and invalidate the content binding. This is by design" (I found the last string exactly once in the spec, elided parenthetical is legitimate). But "structurally forbids per-block provenance" is false. §A.9.3 forbids multiple manifest BLOCKS (carriers), not multiple region-scoped assertions. §18.3.8's assertion-metadata-map carries `? "regionOfInterest" : $region-map ; describes a region of the asset where this assertion is relevant`, and §18.2 defines `$range-choice /= "textual"` with `text-map = { "selectors": [1* $text-selector-range-map] ; array of (possibly discontinuous) ranges of text }`. One manifest can therefore carry N per-region assertions. This directly contradicts the same researcher's Claim 8 ("C2PA 2.4 DOES have the spatial/page/textual vocabulary MDMAX needs"). The defensible claim is: C2PA permits region-scoped assertions but binds them to a whole-file byte hash — brittle, not forbidden.
verdicts.correction: C2PA §A.9 permits at most one manifest BLOCK per file, and binds it with a whole-file byte hash that any keystroke invalidates. It does not forbid per-block provenance: §18.3.8 `regionOfInterest` attaches a region to any assertion, and §18.2 defines a discontinuous `textual` range type. The incompatibility with G1 is the whole-file hard binding, not an absence of per-block vocabulary.

verdicts.claim: [Claim 4] The spec's only concrete Markdown example is the single-line `<!-- ... -->` form; the front-matter examples are not Markdown examples.
verdicts.reason: Primary source contradicts it. I parsed `data-lang` attributes inside the §A.9 span of the spec HTML (bytes 981,807–999,784) and mapped each to its nearest heading: §A.9.3.2 (Multi-Line Form / Front Matter) template -> `data-lang="yaml"`; §A.9.3.3.2 (Single-Line Embedded via Data URI) -> `python`; §A.9.3.3.3 (Front Matter Referenced) -> `markdown`; §A.9.3.3.4 (Front Matter Embedded via Data URI) -> `markdown`. So §A.9 contains THREE markdown-designated examples, and two of the three are the front-matter form — the opposite of the claim. Note this REINFORCES the headline: C2PA does privilege the markdown front-matter form, and that form is the broken one.
verdicts.correction: §A.9 gives three Markdown-designated examples: the `<!-- -->` row in the §A.9.3.3.1 table, and §A.9.3.3.3 and §A.9.3.3.4, both of which are the front-matter form and both tagged `data-lang="markdown"` in the spec HTML. The front-matter form is not merely permitted for Markdown — it is the form the spec illustrates twice for Markdown, and it is the form that breaks.

verdicts.claim: [Claim 5] §A.8 is normatively drafted but self-declared provisional; §A.9 shipped in 2.4 (April 2026), §A.8 in 2.3 (December 2025).
verdicts.reason: All quotes verbatim in the fetched spec. §A.8.1: "This approach should only be used with unstructured text assets where no other embedding method is feasible. It remains under review and may be subject to change based on implementation feedback and interoperability testing." §5.3.1 header "2.4 - April 2026" with the Embedding Enhancements entry "Added support for embedding C2PA Manifests into structured text formats (source code, YAML, Markdown, AsciiDoc, etc.)." §5.3.2 "2.3 - December 2025" with "Added comprehensive support for embedding C2PA manifests in unstructured text files." Age arithmetic re-derived against today 2026-08-01 (Saturday, verified via `date -u`): from 2026-04-01 = 122 days = 4.01 months; from 2026-04-30 = 93 days = 3.06 months. "Four months old" is the upper bound of the range but not wrong.

verdicts.claim: [Claim 6] ZERO implementations of §A.8 or §A.9 exist. c2pa-rs supports 20 media types, none text; implements a subset of 2.2; contentauth code search returns nothing.
verdicts.reason: The narrow scope reproduces exactly — supported-formats.md lists 20 rows (avi…webp) with no md and no text/*; README line 40 reads "implements a subset of the C2PA technical specification" linking the **2.2** spec; repo has 375 stars, pushed 2026-07-31T22:48:39Z; `repo:contentauth/c2pa-rs "BEGIN C2PA MANIFEST"` -> total_count 0 and `org:contentauth "BEGIN C2PA MANIFEST"` -> total_count 0. But the UNQUALIFIED search the researcher never ran refutes the headline in under a minute: `"BEGIN C2PA MANIFEST"` -> total_count 41; `"-----BEGIN C2PA MANIFEST-----"` -> total_count 34. Two independent published implementations exist: (1) crates.io **c2pa-structured-text** v0.2.0, writerslogic, Apache-2.0, created 2026-05-14 (one month after 2.4 shipped), updated 2026-07-13, pushed 2026-07-31, 259 downloads, with CI, docs.rs, an OpenSSF scorecard, and an `embed_front_matter` function; (2) PyPI **c2pa-text** v3.0.0, Encypher Corporation, MIT, classifier "Development Status :: 5 - Production/Stable", GitHub `encypherai/c2pa-text`, described as "A Reference Implementation for C2PA Text Embedding", created 2025-12-05. Also writerslogic/c2pa-vtt for WebVTT. This is exactly the "nobody has built this" failure the brief warned about. It also cost the researcher the single most relevant piece of prior art: `encypherai/c2pa-text/golden/samples/document.md` is `<!-- -----BEGIN C2PA MANIFEST----- data:application/c2pa;base64,3q2+7w== -----END C2PA MANIFEST----- -->` — the only markdown golden sample in the wild already uses the comment carrier the design proposes.
verdicts.correction: No implementation of §A.8 or §A.9 exists in the reference SDK (c2pa-rs, 375 stars, spec 2.2, 20 formats, none text/*). Two third-party implementations do exist and are published: crates.io `c2pa-structured-text` v0.2.0 (259 downloads, vs 9,418,183 lifetime for `c2pa` itself — roughly 0.003%) and PyPI `c2pa-text` v3.0.0. Adoption is negligible, not zero — and both independently corroborate the comment carrier over front matter.

verdicts.claim: [Claim 7] C2PA 2.4 contains no confidence primitive; four occurrences of the word exist and all four are Google depth-map fields.
verdicts.reason: Substance CONFIRMED, number wrong. `grep -c` counts matching LINES, not occurrences — this is the rate/count confusion the brief asked me to hunt. On my strip of the spec (624,528 chars): `grep -c -i -w confidence` = 4 (lines), `grep -o -i -w confidence | wc -l` = 7 (word-boundary occurrences), Python `re.findall(r'(?i)confidence')` = 9 (substring), and `grep -o -i confidence` on the raw HTML = 9. I printed all 9 contexts: every one is inside the GDepth block — `GDepth:ConfidenceMime`, `GDepth:Confidence` (CDDL + example each), `confidence-mime-type = $mime-choice .default "image/png"`, and prose about the "confidence image"/"confidence map". So the conclusion holds; the count does not, and the researcher's own enumeration of "all four" also undercounts the distinct usages. Separately, `modelIdentifier` is described in the CDDL as "unique identifier of the AI model used (e.g., a URI, PURL, etc.)" — PURL is one permitted example, so "C2PA's modelIdentifier uses PURL" overstates. The ai-disclosure details do check out: modelType "shall be present in the ai-model-disclosure-map object", scientificDomain "shall conform to the arXiv taxonomy", and `content-profile-map = { ? humanOversightLevel: human-oversight-enum }` with fully_autonomous / prompt_guided / human_validated.
verdicts.correction: C2PA 2.4 contains no confidence primitive. The word appears on 4 lines / 9 times in the spec text, and every occurrence is Google GDepth depth-map metadata (`GDepth:Confidence`, `GDepth:ConfidenceMime`, `confidence-mime-type`), not extraction or derivation confidence.

verdicts.claim: [Claim 8] C2PA has the region vocabulary MDMAX needs, but its textual range is a fragment identifier plus absolute character offsets — the brittle addressing content-derived re-anchoring replaces — and it defines no Markdown fragment convention.
verdicts.reason: Every CDDL string is verbatim: `; this is modelled after the W3C Web Annotation selector model`, `text-selector-map = { "fragment": tstr, ; fragment identifier, as per RFC3023 or ISO 32000-2, Annex O  ? "start": int, ? "end": int }`, `; this can be used for either frames of a video or pages of a document` + `frame-map`, and shape-map's rectangle/circle/polygon with pixel/percent units. "No Markdown fragment convention" also holds — the only cited schemes are XML (RFC3023) and PDF (ISO 32000-2 Annex O). But the characterization is wrong in a way that matters to the design. `start` and `end` are OPTIONAL: the spec says "If neither is provided, the range shall represent the entire fragment." The base case is fragment-only, i.e. NOT character-offset addressing. The claim also omits `text-selector-range-map` and `text-map = { "selectors": [1* $text-selector-range-map] ; array of (possibly discontinuous) ranges of text }`. Because the fragment scheme for Markdown is undefined, the fragment slot is OPEN — an MDMAX content-derived anchor could BE the fragment. The researcher converted an integration opportunity into a stated incompatibility.
verdicts.correction: C2PA §18.2.3 addresses a textual range as a required `fragment` identifier with OPTIONAL `start`/`end` character offsets; fragment-only is the base case and discontinuous ranges are supported via `text-map.selectors`. Because the spec names no Markdown fragment convention (only RFC3023/XML and ISO 32000-2/PDF), MDMAX's content-derived anchor is a candidate fragment scheme rather than a competitor to C2PA's addressing.

verdicts.claim: [DESIGN §3] 'No record is ever inside another node's byte range, so no splice can be forced to reflow a neighbouring block.'
verdicts.reason:
Proven false at the AST level, independently of any stringifier. `- alpha
- beta
- gamma
` parses (remark-parse + remark-gfm) to top-level `list`, list count 1, 3 items. Inserting the design's own Tier-1 record before item 2 — `- alpha

<!--p b=tb:1-->

- beta
- gamma
` — parses to `list, html, list`: 2 lists with 1+2 items. For an ordered list the same insertion yields lists=2, starts=1,2. Inserting a provenance record therefore changes the document's block structure (one `<ul>` becomes two, tight/loose rendering changes), which is a stronger failure than the reflow the design says it prevents. Scale, measured over 4,289 .md files in ~/Desktop/GitHub/md: 1,069,790 block nodes total, 274,766 top-level (25.68%), 794,095 inside a list/table/blockquote (74.23%). listItem = 359,496 and tableRow = 33,874, of which 0 and 0 are top-level. Tier 1's 'one comment immediately preceding the block' can safely address at most ~25.7% of blocks.

verdicts.claim: [DESIGN §1 Tier 2] Per-span records ride in a link reference definition, `q` carrying the verbatim span text.
verdicts.reason: The design's exact record shape nests escaped quotes inside a `"`-delimited definition title. The verbatim example does round-trip (`[mdmax-prov-tb44e1-s1]: mdmax:prov "b=tb:44e1 q=\"$4.2M in Q3\" ..."` parses to a `definition` with url `mdmax:prov` and is byte-identical through remark-stringify). But `q` is specified as the verbatim span text, and a single `"` in that span destroys it: with `q=\"he said \"hi\"\"` the top-level AST degrades from `definition` to `paragraph`, and stringify emits `\[mdmax-prov-x]: mdmax:prov "b=tb:1 q="he said "hi"" m=ocr c=0.6"` — the record is gone AND the file is corrupted with an escaped bracket. Measured breakage rate: 70,128 of 478,400 paragraphs in ~/Desktop/GitHub/md contain a `"` character = 14.66%. Roughly one span in seven. (Apostrophes, brackets, parens, em-dashes and literal `\n` all survive — the failure is specific to the double quote, which is the one character the design's own escaping scheme depends on.)

verdicts.claim: [DESIGN §5] The mechanical lossy-handoff layer: 5.74% of paragraphs carry a magnitude, 3.56% unsourced, 'a review load of ~4,076 blocks per 114,572, which is tractable'.
verdicts.reason: Numbers reproduce exactly, the denominator label does not. I ran the researcher's own `.scratch-lossy.mjs` verbatim: paras 114572, numeric 6581 (5.74%), unsourced 4076 (3.56%), tool-claim 38/37, deictic 31/16. Arithmetic re-derived: 4076/114572 = 3.5576%, 6581/114572 = 5.7440% — both correct. But the script does `if(n.type!=="paragraph") continue` over `tree.children` only, so 114,572 is TOP-LEVEL paragraphs. Total paragraph nodes at every depth in the same corpus: 478,400. The measurement covers 23.95% of the corpus and 76.05% (363,828 paragraphs) was never scanned. Re-running the identical BIGNUM/hasLink/ctx logic recursively over every paragraph: numeric 67,365 (14.08%), unsourced 62,154 (12.99%). The true review load is 62,154 blocks, not ~4,076 — 15.25x — and the rate is 12.99%, not 3.56%. Nested paragraphs are worse on both axes because a paragraph inside a list rarely has a code/table/blockquote sibling. 'Tractable' is not established at the corrected scope.

verdicts.claim: [DESIGN §4a] 'My own measurement puts a number on it: 547/547 self-declared `updated:` dates in a real, automation-heavy repo are stale, 32.9% by more than a week.'
verdicts.reason: Not reproducible from any corpus available here, and the shape of the result is itself a warning sign. Counting `updated:` front-matter keys with gray-matter across every named corpus with NO directory exclusions (4,852 .md files, 2,795 with front matter): md 112, knowledge 143, frontmatter 0 — maximum possible population 255, not 547. Adding `created`/`date`/etc. still does not reach 547. My independent replication over ~/Desktop/GitHub/md (declared `updated:` vs `git log -1 --format=%cI` for that path): 112 files with the key, 109 stale (97.32%), and 100.00% of those stale by more than 7 days — the opposite split from the claimed 32.9%. Three further problems: (a) a 100.00% result on a self-selected population is the signature of a systematic offset, not of decay; (b) my delta distribution is min 20.7 / median 20.7 / max 22.7 days, a tight cluster that says one bulk commit touched every file, so git-commit-time is measuring mechanical touches, not content change; (c) the repo is unnamed, making the number unauditable — which the project's own evidence discipline forbids. The anti-decay argument's only empirical support does not stand.
verdicts.correction: State the repo, the key, and the staleness definition, and use a content-change signal rather than last-commit time. On the corpora available here the honest statement is: 109 of 112 files carrying an `updated:` key in ~/Desktop/GitHub/md have a later git commit touching them, but the deltas cluster at 20.7-22.7 days, consistent with a single bulk commit rather than per-file rot.

verdicts.claim: [DESIGN §1/§2] Tier 2 uses definitions 'so they survive HTML pipelines that strip raw HTML'.
verdicts.reason:
Contradicted by the design's own §2 and by the researcher's own script. I ran `.scratch-carrier.mjs` unchanged: with `remark-rehype` at the safe default (`allowDangerousHtml:false`) the output is `"

T

\n

A paragraph.

\n

Another paragraph.

"` — the definition emits no HTML at all, exactly like the comment. §2 states this correctly ('comments dropped, definitions dropped'), so §1's stated rationale contradicts §2 of the same document. Definitions may still be worth choosing for MDX compatibility, but that specific reason is false. The MDX half is untested: no `@mdx-js` is installed in the repo and I did not npm install (RULE 4) — mark it unverified rather than assumed.

verdicts.claim: [DESIGN §5 rule 1] Dangling reference is 'Fully decidable — this is the compiler's symbol table', measured base rate 0.03% of paragraphs, 16 of 31 unresolved.
verdicts.reason: Inference presented as measurement. Reading `.scratch-lossy.mjs`, 'unresolved' is `!ctx` where `ctx = near(kids[i-1]) || near(kids[i+1])` and `near(x) = x.type is code|table|blockquote`. That is not a symbol table and not a hop — it is 'the immediately adjacent TOP-LEVEL sibling is not one of three node types'. A 'see above' pointing at a heading, an image, a list, or a paragraph three blocks up scores unresolved; 'the figure above' pointing at an image scores unresolved because `image` is not in the set. The counts also reproduce but are far too small to support a rate: n=31 deictic hits over 114,572 top-level paragraphs, 16 flagged. The 95% interval on 16/31 spans roughly 34%-70% and no interval is given. Rule 2 is worse: it flags 37 of 38 hits (97.4%), which is a detector with no discrimination, reported as a working 0.03% signal.

survived: The armour is not valid YAML: yaml@2.9.0 and js-yaml@3.14.2 both throw, with the exact error strings reported, on the spec's verbatim §A.9.3.3.3 example.

gray-matter@4.0.3 silently destroys the document: data={}, matter="", isEmpty=true, the real `title:` key lost, and the manifest URL leaked into rendered body — because `-----BEGIN` literally begins with the `---` close fence.

All five npm weekly-download figures, re-derived independently from api.npmjs.org for window 2026-07-24 -> 2026-07-30: gray-matter 7,492,225; front-matter 4,748,352; js-yaml 280,864,032; c2pa 4,486; c2pa-node 10,695.

GFM renders the block maximally visibly: `<hr>` plus a setext `<h2>` containing the manifest URL as a clickable `<a rel="nofollow">` — confirmed on the truly verbatim 6-line example, not just the padded one.

§A.9.3's one-manifest-block-per-file rule and §A.9.4's single whole-file exclusion range, quoted verbatim; and §A.7.1.3's "This is by design" for byte-offset invalidation, which appears exactly once in the spec.

§A.8.1's self-declared provisional status and the §5.3.1 / §5.3.2 changelog entries dating §A.9 to 2.4 (April 2026) and §A.8 to 2.3 (December 2025) — all verbatim; spec age re-derived as 3.06-4.01 months against today 2026-08-01.

No text/* support in the reference SDK: c2pa-rs supported-formats.md lists 20 rows, none of them md or text; README links the 2.2 spec; 375 stars, pushed 2026-07-31; contentauth-scoped code search returns 0.
C2PA 2.4 has no confidence primitive — every occurrence of the word is Google GDepth depth-map metadata (the conclusion survives even though the count of 4 does not).

The c2pa.ai-disclosure assertion details: modelType required, scientificDomain bound to the arXiv taxonomy, and content-profile-map's humanOversightLevel enum {fully_autonomous, prompt_guided, human_validated} — all verbatim.
§18.2.3's text-selector-map / text-selector-range-map / frame-map / shape-map CDDL, verbatim, and the absence of any Markdown fragment convention (only RFC3023/XML and ISO 32000-2 Annex O are named).

HTML comments and link reference definitions do render to nothing in GFM and do round-trip byte-identically through remark for a well-formed top-level record — the researcher's carrier script reproduces exactly.

The headline's strategic conclusion — do not adopt C2PA's front-matter carrier; ship provenance in comments keyed by content-derived anchors — survives, and is independently corroborated by the one markdown golden sample in the wild (encypherai/c2pa-text uses the `<!-- -->` form).
Front matter as DECLARATION-only (Tier 0), a closed `m` vocabulary, the verifiable/asserted split, and `mdmax prov strip` as a first-class escape hatch are sound and untouched by anything I found.
killed: "ZERO implementations of §A.8 or §A.9 exist" — refuted in under a minute. Unscoped GitHub code search for "BEGIN C2PA MANIFEST" returns total_count 41. crates.io `c2pa-structured-text` v0.2.0 (Apache-2.0, 259 downloads, CI + docs.rs + OpenSSF scorecard, pushed 2026-07-31) and PyPI `c2pa-text` v3.0.0 (MIT, "Production/Stable") both implement it. The researcher only searched `repo:contentauth/c2pa-rs` and `org:contentauth`.

"The spec's only concrete Markdown example is `<!-- ... -->`" — §A.9.3.3.3 and §A.9.3.3.4 are BOTH tagged `data-lang="markdown"` in the spec HTML, and both are the front-matter form. Three markdown examples, not one.

"§A.9 structurally forbids per-block provenance" — it forbids multiple manifest BLOCKS, not multiple region-scoped assertions. §18.3.8 `regionOfInterest` plus §18.2's discontinuous `textual` range contradict it, as does the researcher's own Claim 8.
"Four occurrences of the word confidence exist" — `grep -c` counts lines. 4 lines, 7 word-boundary occurrences, 9 substring occurrences.

DESIGN §3: "no splice can be forced to reflow a neighbouring block" — inserting a Tier-1 comment before list item 2 splits one 3-item list into two lists (`list, html, list`, items 1+2) at the AST level.
DESIGN: Tier 1 as a general per-block carrier — 74.23% of the 1,069,790 block nodes measured sit inside a list, table, or blockquote and cannot take a preceding comment without changing the AST.
DESIGN: Tier 2's `q` field as specified — a single `"` in the span text degrades the AST from `definition` to `paragraph` and corrupts the file; 14.66% of paragraphs contain one.

DESIGN §5: "a review load of ~4,076 blocks per 114,572, which is tractable" — the denominator is top-level paragraphs only (23.95% of the corpus). Re-run over every paragraph: 62,154 blocks, 12.99%, a 15.25x increase.
DESIGN §5 rule 1: "Fully decidable — this is the compiler's symbol table" — it is an adjacency check against three node types on top-level siblings, with n=31.
DESIGN §1: Tier 2 definitions "survive HTML pipelines that strip raw HTML" — the researcher's own script shows remark-rehype drops them entirely, and the design's own §2 says so.

DESIGN §4a: "547/547 ... 32.9% by more than a week" — maximum `updated:` population across all named corpora is 255; my replication gives 109/112 stale with 100% over a week, from what the delta distribution shows is a single bulk commit.

DESIGN §2: "Verified over 476 corpus files (100% comment preservation vs 3/476 byte-identical)" — no corpus here has 476 .md files (md 4,289 / knowledge 421 / frontmatter 113) and the only carrier artifact tests exactly one synthetic 9-line document.
new_defects: METHOD — `grep -c` used as an occurrence count. It counts matching LINES. This produced "four occurrences" for a word that occurs 7 times (word-boundary) / 9 times (substring). Exactly the rate-vs-absolute-count confusion the brief warned about, and it survived into a claim tagged own-measurement.

METHOD — the denominator was never named. `114,572` is reported as "paragraphs" throughout §5; it is top-level paragraph nodes, 23.95% of the corpus's 478,400 paragraphs. Every rate in the lossy-handoff section inherits this. The script's `if(n.type!=="paragraph") continue` over `tree.children` is a one-line non-recursive walk, so 76.05% of prose — everything inside a list item, table cell, or blockquote — was never scanned. Correcting it moves the headline review load from ~4,076 to 62,154.

METHOD — n=1 presented as an n=476 replication. §2 says "Verified over 476 corpus files (100% comment preservation...)". The only carrier artifact, `/Users/sagnikmitra/Desktop/GitHub/frontmatter/.scratch-carrier.mjs`, builds ONE hand-written 9-line document and tests it once. No corpus in ~/Desktop/GitHub is 476 .md files. A single well-behaved synthetic case is doing the work of a corpus study — and it is precisely the case that hides the list-splitting and quote-breakage failures I found.

METHOD — an unnamed artifact behind an own-measurement number. "547/547 ... in a real, automation-heavy repo" names no repo, no key semantics, and no staleness definition, so it cannot be audited. It is also not reachable from any corpus available here (max 255). The project's own discipline is to state the artifact the number came from.

METHOD — 100.00% and 97.4% results accepted as findings rather than as alarms. "547/547" and rule 2's "37 of 38 flagged" are both the signature of a systematic offset or a detector with no discrimination. Neither was interrogated; both were reported as working measurements.

METHOD — inference tagged as measurement. "Fully decidable — this is the compiler's symbol table" describes `near(kids[i-1]) || near(kids[i+1])` over three node types. The design also asserts Tier-2 survival through HTML-stripping pipelines and through MDX; the first is contradicted by its own §2, and the second was never executed (no @mdx-js is installed).
METHOD — no confidence intervals on tiny n. Rules 1 and 2 rest on 31 and 38 hits respectively. The 95% interval on 16/31 spans roughly 34-70%. These are quoted as base rates.

METHOD — detector specificity never checked. The BIGNUM regex `\d[\d,]{2,}` matches any 3+ digit run, so every bare year qualifies as "a magnitude/percentage/currency". I measured it: 6,433 of 67,365 flagged paragraphs (9.55%) contain no numeric token other than a 19xx/20xx year. Symmetrically, `hasLink` counts ANY link anywhere in the paragraph as sourcing the number, so "unsourced" is inflated and deflated at once, and neither direction is stated.

METHOD — the negative-result search was scoped to the friendly namespace. Searching only `repo:contentauth/c2pa-rs` and `org:contentauth` and then writing "zero implementations exist" is the search that can only confirm. One unscoped query returns 41 hits and two published packages. It also cost the most useful prior art in the whole area: encypherai/c2pa-text's markdown golden sample already uses the comment carrier this design proposes, and writerslogic's `embed_front_matter` unit test encodes the document-destroying output as expected behaviour — stronger evidence for Claim 1 than the researcher's own.

METHOD — internal contradiction between claims went unreconciled. Claim 3 ("structurally forbids per-block provenance") and Claim 8 ("C2PA 2.4 DOES have the spatial/page/textual vocabulary MDMAX needs") cannot both be true, and §1 of the design contradicts §2 on whether definitions survive HTML stripping.

METHOD — "verbatim" used for a modified input. Claim 2's evidence string contains `

Hello

body text

`, which only appears when body text is appended to the spec example. Immaterial to the conclusion, but it is a labelled-verbatim input that was not verbatim. Related scope error: `api.github.com/markdown` is not github.com's .md blob renderer, so the design's §0 claim about "GitHub's blob view" rests on a different pipeline than the one measured.

PROCESS — RULE 4 breach in the research run itself. Two scratch files were written into the repo working tree and left there: `/Users/sagnikmitra/Desktop/GitHub/frontmatter/.scratch-carrier.mjs` and `/Users/sagnikmitra/Desktop/GitHub/frontmatter/.scratch-lossy.mjs` (untracked, mtimes 2026-08-01 05:52 and 05:50), against an explicit "no file writes outside $TMPDIR". Recommend deleting both, which is the user's call, not mine. Disclosure: I briefly made the same mistake — I copied one test file to the repo root for node module resolution and removed it in the next command; `git status` confirms the tree is otherwise untouched by me, and I ran everything else from $TMPDIR via a symlinked node_modules, which I also removed.

per_area.title: Google Docs of markdown — collaboration primitives on plain .md
per_area.headline: The PLAN §8 / PRODUCT-PLAN §4b conflict is narrower than stated — Braid simpleton is itself server-authoritative ("Server merges with Diamond-Types"), so both documents already agree the client is dumb; the only real disagreement is what the server runs, and eg-walker's own git-derived A2 trace (OT: 3,664,266 ms and 6.76 GB peak vs 23.47 ms) plus its production implementation's 73 npm downloads/week settle it in favour of §4b — while the genuinely new and measurable win is that block-scoping a comment quote cuts silent mis-anchoring from 2.70% to 0.09% (30×) over 2,332 real revision pairs.

findings.claim: The brief's "Pain theme T6" is mislabelled, and the product plan mislabels it the same way in 7 consecutive rows. Collaboration is T7; T6 is offline. Worse, the product plan is internally inconsistent — line 116 uses taxonomy IDs correctly while lines 125–142 use rank numbers, so the offline and collaboration citations are swapped against each other inside one document.

unclaimed: Refusal-bearing range anchoring. Hypothes.is — the largest deployed system — has no score threshold and returns its least-bad guess (verified in match-quote.ts); Google's public anchor is a line number they explicitly disclaim; Word and Notion own the artifact so the question never arises. Nobody ships "this comment is ORPHANED because the resolver declined to guess." MDMAX's DELTA refusal already exists at block level and is the differentiator.

Block-scoped quote resolution. Hypothes.is's own source comment asks for exactly this ("it would be better if this code was aware of logical boundaries in the document (paragraph, article etc.)") and uses a fixed 32-character window instead. Measured here: block scope cuts ambiguity 30× (2.70% → 0.09%).

Comment anchors that survive an out-of-band edit — a git pull, a vim save, an AI agent rewrite. Every shipped system either owns every write (Overleaf, kix, ProseMirror/CM6 remaps) or breaks; Relay #22 is the documented failure of the CRDT-parallel-to-filesystem alternative. Content-derived re-anchoring is the only strategy without precedent, which is both the opportunity and the risk.

Suggest mode where the suggester provably cannot write file bytes. CriticMarkup structurally cannot deliver this — the suggestion IS a file mutation, which is HedgeDoc's exact deadlock. CKEditor/TipTap can but are commercial and HTML/JSON-doc-centric. No CommonMark-in-git tool has it.

Block-granular presence and awareness. Everything shipped is character-cursor-based, which requires a live connection and cannot represent an async participant. A block-keyed presence channel makes a git-clone, a CI job or a vim user a first-class participant rather than an absence.

A CLI that resolves comment anchors with no editor and no server — `frontmatter comments resolve <file>` reporting placed/orphaned/ambiguous. No annotation system exposes its anchoring as a standalone tool; Hypothes.is's is a browser client, Tandem's is an Obsidian plugin.

The receiving-side-free surface (G3): a commented document that a stranger's LLM or renderer can consume with zero adoption. Measured: HTML-comment carriers vanish on GitHub in every position; CriticMarkup and fence sidecars are visible. Nobody has built a comment layer whose degradation is the specification rather than an accident.
per_area.design:
RESOLUTION OF THE CONFLICT — adopt PRODUCT-PLAN §4b as the shipping architecture; demote PLAN §8 from "the design" to "the constraint list the design must not violate"; and fix the product plan's own Pillar 3/5 rows and T-labels.

Decisive reasons, in order:
(1) The conflict is partly illusory. Braid simpleton is server-authoritative by construction ("Server merges with Diamond-Types"), so both documents already agree the client holds text + version and the hub sequences. Keep simpleton's CLIENT contract ({on_state | on_patches, get_state, changed()}) — it is the cheapest way to get §8's genuinely valuable property that a git clone, a CI job, vim or an agent is a participant, not a degraded case. Reject its SERVER (diamond-types).
(2) The engine PLAN §8 recommends fails PLAN §2.1's own adoption test by ~99,000× (diamond-types-node 73/wk vs yjs 7,244,115/wk; the Rust crate last published 2022-08-25). The plan cannot use adoption ratios to kill djot and ignore them for its own collaboration engine.
(3) Eg-walker's core optimisation is documented by its authors not to hold for Peritext-style annotations, which is what comments and formatting marks are. Adopting Peritext semantics voids the reason to adopt eg-walker.
(4) OT is disqualified at the git boundary by the paper's own git-derived A2 trace (3,664,266 ms, 6.76 GB peak) — so the server must NOT be an OT sequencer either. §4b is right that the git boundary belongs to merge3; it is wrong only in implying the live sequencer and merge3 are different algebras.

THE ARCHITECTURE THAT SHIPS: one hub, ONE merge implementation, no persisted event graph in v1.
- Live path: server-authoritative, clients simpleton-shaped (diff on reconnect, not keystrokes).
- Server merge: NOT OT and NOT a peer CRDT — the SAME block-granular three-way merge used at the git boundary (merge3 + §1.1a re-anchor), applied per block. One pipeline for keystrokes, git pulls, and agent writes. This is the property Relay #22 proves you cannot do without: the CRDT-parallel-to-file design shows a false merge conflict on every external write.
- Git boundary: unchanged — baseSha 409 + merge3, session-batched commits with Co-authored-by (GitHub-precedented).
- Event graph: not persisted in v1; add only if the block-granular merge measurably loses (kill-gate below).
- Bound the Peritext hazard in the UI, but bound the RIGHT thing: same-mark overlaps converge correctly (measured); refuse or serialise concurrent HETEROGENEOUS mark toggles and any concurrent edit that crosses an inline-code boundary.

COMMENTS — what lives where (Q4):
Sidecar (Supabase) is the source of truth for thread bodies, authorship, resolve state, mentions, permissions, and the anchor record. Three non-negotiable reasons: (a) comment-only permission is impossible if commenting mutates the file — HedgeDoc's exact 5-year deadlock; (b) a comment would otherwise be a git commit on the owner's repo by someone who may have no GitHub account; (c) "deleting the sidecar leaves a valid markdown repo" is only true if the file never depended on it.
Anchor record, tri-redundant, stored in the sidecar, never required in the file:
  { block: <§1.1a content-derived anchor>, quote: {exact, prefix, suffix}, offset: <int, tie-break only>, digest: sha256(NFC(exact)), baseSha }
Resolution order: block re-anchor → quote match SCOPED TO THE RESOLVED BLOCK → refuse. Never a position tiebreak as a resolver (0.00% → 22.20% false, measured in §1.1a); keep offset at Hypothes.is's weight (~2%) purely to order equal candidates. Grapheme-cluster indexes per iA Writer, plus the mandatory validating digest, resolving the UTF-16-vs-byte hazard of §3.3.
Refusal is mandatory and is where this beats Hypothes.is: block AMBIGUOUS/LOST, or quote ambiguous inside the resolved block ⇒ thread goes ORPHANED, original quote preserved, pinned to the nearest anchorable neighbour, visibly. Never silently placed.
Optional in-file materialization, OFF by default, for export and for the "we deleted the sidecar" guarantee: tier-3 HTML-comment sentinel pairs `<!--fm:c s=ID-->…<!--fm:c e=ID-->` plus a `<!--fm:comments …-->` block. Measured invisible on GitHub inline, inside **bold**, inside table cells and inside links; +1.214% bytes at 1 comment per 10 blocks. NOT a fence (visible code block on GitHub) and NOT CriticMarkup (visible, and its substitution form is destroyed by remark-gfm).
HARD CORRECTNESS GATE, found by measurement: normalize() MUST strip HTML comments before hashing, or writing a sentinel changes the identity of the block it annotates. One line; 0.266% of real blocks already contain an HTML comment, so the cost is negligible.
Ranges inside inline code or fenced code cannot carry an inline sentinel (it renders literally) — anchor those by block + line range + verbatim quote only, no normalization.

SUGGEST MODE (Q3):
Overlay, not mutation. Stored as {anchor, replacement, author, thread} in the sidecar; rendered as CM6 decorations per §3.8 (inline → ViewPlugin, block height → StateField). The file is byte-untouched until accept. A suggest-role user has NO code path that writes file bytes — that is the enforcement point and the thing CriticMarkup structurally cannot give you.
Accept = a splice through the normal write path, attributed with a Co-authored-by trailer, batched per review not per suggestion (GitHub's model, Overleaf's just-in-time commit granularity).
Interchange only, never storage: `--critic` export/import. Emit substitutions as adjacent `{--old--}{++new++}`, never `{~~old~>new~~}` — Add and Delete round-trip byte-identically and render literally on both renderers; Substitution does not.
Do not copy GitHub's whole-line granularity: a markdown paragraph is one line, and hard-wrapped lines reflow.

PRESENCE (Q5): block-granular. Broadcast {user, blockAnchor, mode: viewing|editing|suggesting} on block transition only. Justified by measurement: median doc = 23 anchorable blocks, 69.9% of saves touch ≤2 blocks. Character cursors are a layer on top, not the substrate. Default live-visibility OFF for the owner's own unsaved drafts (Upwelling fishbowl); make "share now" an explicit act.

CLI SURFACE (the §I.1 test — must work with no editor and no server):
  frontmatter comments list <file>
  frontmatter comments resolve <file>            # placed / orphaned / ambiguous per thread, with confidence tier
  frontmatter comments export <file> --critic|--html|--json
  frontmatter comments import <file> --critic
  frontmatter suggest diff <id>
  frontmatter suggest apply <id> [--all]         # splice + Co-authored-by
  frontmatter anchor check <file>                # re-anchor every stored anchor, print E/W/I tier

DEGRADATION BEHAVIOUR, publishable as a guarantee: delete the entire sidecar → `git status` clean, every file byte-identical, nothing in the repo references it, `comments list` returns empty. Delete the app → the repo is an ordinary Obsidian vault. Open a commented file on GitHub → the prose reads exactly as if no comment existed.
per_area.measurement:
TWO experiments. Neither has been run; both are cheap.

EXPERIMENT A — does the block-scoped anchor earn a shippable comment feature?
Corpus: the 294 consecutive revision pairs already used for §1.1a, plus the 400 modified-.md pairs used here, plus two adversarial strata that must be built: (i) 100 pairs whose diff includes a paragraph REFLOW (detect via §8's own signal — ≥80% of deleted lines ≥0.80 similar to a line in the same hunk), (ii) 100 pairs drawn from homogeneous index lists (knowledge.md-shaped), which §1.1a already identifies as the known adversarial input at 8× the false rate.
Tasks: place N=3,000 synthetic comment anchors on the OLD revision, stratified by selection length {1,2,3,5,8,13,21 words} × block type {paragraph, list item, table cell, heading, fenced code, inline code}. Resolve against the NEW revision under four resolvers: (1) byte offset, (2) global quote+prefix+suffix (a faithful port of Hypothes.is matchQuote, weights 50/20/20/2, maxErrors=min(256,len/2), NO threshold), (3) block-scoped quote, (4) block-scoped quote WITH a position tiebreak added back.
Verifiers, in the §1.1a discipline: a mechanical oracle from the git diff for the full 3,000, PLUS a hand-audit of EVERY false match and every disagreement between resolvers — not a sample. §1.1a found 4 of 14 "errors" to be oracle artifacts; that only surfaces under hand-audit.
Pre-registered predictions (falsifiable):
  P1. Block-scoped, selections ≥3 words: correct ≥96%, FALSE ≤0.15%, refusal ≤5%.
  P2. Global quote on the same set: false ≥1.5% — i.e. ≥10× worse than P1.
  P3. Byte offset: correct ≤70%.
  P4. Resolver (4) — adding position back — raises false by ≥5× over (3). If it does not, §1.1a's 0.00%→22.20% result does not generalise to sub-block ranges and the design can be simplified.
  P5. Selection length 1 word: refusal ≥20%. If the resolver answers most 1-word selections, it is guessing.
  P6. Homogeneous-list stratum: false ≥5× the corpus mean UNLESS the structural list key (position within parent list + parent identity, §1.1a's own recommendation) is implemented; with it, ≤2×.
  P7. Reflow stratum: refusal rises but false does NOT (the whole point of refusing).
  P8. Inline-code and fenced-code strata: sentinel-free anchoring only; false ≤0.15% with verbatim (un-normalized) quoting.

EXPERIMENT B — does the event graph earn its place?
Replay the eg-walker A1 (node.cc, 194 authors) and A2 (git Makefile, 299 authors, avg concurrency 6.11) traces — both are literally git-derived and both are published — through (a) the proposed block-granular merge3 and (b) diamond-types. Measure: divergence rate (fraction of merges where the two produce different text), merge wall-time, and peak RSS.
Pre-registered: block-granular merge3 diverges from diamond-types on ≤5% of merges; where it diverges, hand-audit which output is closer to author intent. If merge3 loses on >5% of merges, or if any divergence is a silent data loss rather than a visible conflict, the event graph earns its place and §8 is reinstated for the live layer.
Second arm: 20-user pilot, instrumented. Measure what fraction of review sessions are concurrent-with-overlap versus taking-turns. The eg-walker paper asserts the latter dominates but calls it "anecdotal"; this is the cheapest way to test the single assumption the whole phase ordering rests on.
per_area.kill_condition:
Any ONE of these kills the direction as specified:

1. FALSE-MATCH FLOOR. If the block-scoped anchor's false rate on a HAND-AUDITED gold set exceeds ~0.5% for selections ≥3 words, range-anchored comments are not shippable. At 0.5%, a 200-comment document misplaces one comment onto text its author never wrote — which is strictly worse than having no comments, and it is unrecoverable trust damage in a product whose #1 pain theme is "sync silently destroys data."

2. THE REFUSAL IS UNUSABLE. If, in the pilot, orphaned threads exceed ~10% of all threads per week of normal editing, the honest-refusal design is correct and unshippable at the same time — users will read every orphan as a bug. Fix or abandon; do not ship a refusal rate users cannot absorb.

3. THE DEMAND WAS STATED, NOT REVEALED. Combined installs of every markdown comment plugin in the largest markdown ecosystem = 24,569, against 4,659,822 for Dataview (190×). The generous reading is that a plugin cannot deliver the collaborator half. If a hosted product with anonymous share links does NOT lift that number by ≥50× in the pilot, the demand was forum-stated preference, and Phase 3 should be cut to comments-on-published-links only.

4. SOMEONE ELSE SHIPS IT FIRST. HedgeDoc 2.x now has a working CriticMarkup+CM6 comments PoC with a live demo (2026-04-04) and a maintainer who reopened the veto. Relay has 175,904 installs. If any of HedgeDoc, Relay, Peerdraft or HackMD ships range-anchored comments with anonymous no-account share links before Phase 3 lands, the wedge is gone and the residual value is anchor QUALITY — which is a library, not a product.

5. THE MERGE PATH LOSES. If Experiment B shows block-granular merge3 diverging from diamond-types on >5% of merges, or producing any silent loss rather than a visible conflict, then §4b's "no peer CRDT" is wrong on the merits and §8 must be reinstated — accepting diamond-types' 73-downloads-per-week maintenance risk as the price.

6. THE INVARIANT BREAKS. If in-file materialization cannot be made byte-reversible — if writing then deleting a sentinel pair leaves any file not byte-identical to its original — the "deleting the sidecar leaves a valid markdown repo" guarantee is false, and the guarantee is the whole trust story. Ship sidecar-only rather than ship a broken guarantee.
per_area.effort:
Rough build cost, and what gates what.

ENGINE SIDE (no dependency on the product's missing Supabase layer — buildable now):
- Sub-block range resolver on top of the existing §1.1a block resolver: quote + prefix + suffix scoped to a resolved block, with the digest check and the DELTA refusal reused. ~150–250 lines. The pieces are already specified; this is composition, not invention.
- normalize() must strip HTML comments before hashing: 1 line, but it is a correctness gate, not a nicety, and it needs a regression fixture.
