What is PRIMARY-READ is only what Obsidian's own help repository documents: unknown callout types default to `note`, the identifier is case-insensitive, the type reaches the DOM as `data-callout`, callouts are foldable with `+`/`-`. What is UNVERIFIED: (a) whether Obsidian preserves a link `title` when it renders a markdown link, and more importantly whether it preserves the title when it REWRITES a link during a rename — carrier 1's viability in the wedge product turns entirely on this and I could not test it; (b) whether Obsidian's own writer preserves HTML comments byte-identically; (c) whether Obsidian round-trips a `> [!KIND]` without escaping the bracket. All three are one afternoon with a real Obsidian install and all three should be done before carrier 1 is committed to.

VS CODE / markdown-it IS ENTIRELY UNTESTED. markdown-it is not installed anywhere on this machine and npm install is prohibited under the Rule 4 guard, so the degradation matrix has a hole where the second-most-used markdown renderer on Earth should be. Same for Pandoc, cmark and cmark-gfm — none present, none installed.

THE DOCENG ELEVEN PATTERNS: the count and the framing are primary-read (both abstracts fetched verbatim via api.semanticscholar.org and api.crossref.org). The NAMES of the eight-plus-three are NOT. I recovered "block", "container" and "inline element" verbatim from the 2012 abstract; the other eight (Marker, Atom, Field, Record, Table, Milestone, Meta, Popup) are my recall of Di Iorio's vocabulary and are tier INFERENCE. The open-access copy at hdl.handle.net/11380/1199166 returned HTTP 403 from iris.unimore.it. My mapping of markdown's 25 labels onto the eleven is therefore INFERENCE built on a partially-verified vocabulary — the conclusion (markdown lacks Record, block-Meta and inline-Milestone) is mine, not the paper's, and it should be re-derived against the full text before it is published.

CROSS-CHECK AGAINST DOCBOOK, TEI, JATS, DITA, OOXML AND ODF was NOT completed. I fetched the WHATWG HTML index and extracted 107 element names by regex over `the-X-element` anchors (the true count is a little higher; the method under-counts elements documented without that anchor form). DocBook's schema returned 404 from the GitHub mirror I tried; TEI and DITA returned 200 but I did not have budget to parse their element inventories. The HTML5 comparison is real; the five-vocabulary convergence claim in the task brief is NOT independently confirmed by me and I am not repeating it as verified.

THE 1,037 FIGURE for Kubernetes HTML tables is `grep -c '<table'` summed over files, i.e. lines-containing, cross-checked against the AST scanner's `table=2074` open+close tag count. Consistent, but a file with two `<table` on one line would under-count. The 24.69x ratio is robust to that; the absolute number is +/- a few.

NOT MEASURED AT ALL, and each is a real gap: heading-level abuse beyond skip-counting (I measured 84 skips in 81,765 AI-vault headings = 0.15%, and 22.24% duplicate heading text in Kubernetes, but did not analyse WHAT the duplicates are — PLAN §17.2 says anchors are unstable under i18n and duplicate headings are the monolingual version of the same problem); link-title abuse in the sense the brief intended (I found 40 titles total, which is too few to characterise); code-fence abuse beyond info-string classification; and any measurement of what happens to these carriers under a git merge, which is where §1.1a's whole value proposition lives.

FINALLY, per Learned Rule #62: every number in this report came from reading actual files or actual API responses, not from replaying data through modified code. Nothing here is SIMULATED. But per Learned Rule #60 and #63, none of the measurements has been re-run by an independent adversarial pass, and I ran the corpus scanner once per corpus, not three times — the counts are deterministic over fixed inputs so repetition would not change them, but the scanner itself was written in the same session as the analysis it feeds and therefore inherits this session's blind spots. Artifacts for re-derivation: /tmp/claude-501/mdmax/scan.mjs, /tmp/claude-501/mdmax/s_{vaultmd,knowledge,frontmatter,readmes,k8s,ghdocs,rustbook,obshelp}.json, /tmp/claude-501/mdmax/probe{,2,3,4}.md, /tmp/claude-501/mdmax/languages.yml, and the fetched corpora under /tmp/claude-501/mdmax/{readmes,pub_k8s,pub_ghdocs,pub_rustbook,pub_obshelp}. These are in $TMPDIR and will be lost; nothing was written outside it, no repo was modified, and no destructive operation was run.

verification.area: Adversarial verification of "The constructs markdown is missing, derived from strain rather than from demand" — 8 claims, the headline, and the 5-item design, re-measured locally and re-probed live against api.github.com, github-linguist/linguist, html.spec.whatwg.org, jgm/pandoc and obsidianmd/obsidian-help

verdicts.claim: [Claim 1 / HEADLINE] The description-list workaround is typed 51,620 times (32,940 bold-led list items + 18,680 '**Term**: rest' paragraphs), 39.91 per 1,000 lines, 12.7 per file.
verdicts.reason: The two components are NOT disjoint sets and were summed as if they were. In the scanner (/tmp/claude-501/mdmax/scan.mjs), `case 'listItem'` increments boldLedColon AND `case 'paragraph'` increments recordParas — and a list item's first child IS a paragraph, so `- **Term**: value` is counted TWICE. I re-ran the identical predicates while tracking node identity (/tmp/claude-501/mdmax/verify_overlap.mjs). Per corpus, BOTH-counted: vaultmd 12,170 / knowledge 2,013 / readmes 1,185 / frontmatter 54 / ghdocs 125 / obshelp 190 / rustbook 52 / k8s 51 = 15,840. 51,620 − 15,840 = 35,780, which reconciles exactly. The naive sum is inflated 44.3%. Note the tell that was available without re-running anything: `recordInListItem` ≈ `BOTH` in every single corpus (12,174 vs 12,170; 2,014 vs 2,013; 1,186 vs 1,185) — essentially every in-list record paragraph is double-booked.
verdicts.correction: Deduped union = 35,780 (27.67 per 1,000 lines, 8.78 per file), not 51,620 / 39.91 / 12.7.

verdicts.claim: [Claim 1, continued] Those 51,620 instances are 'the thing users type when they need a RECORD'.
verdicts.reason: Precision failure on top of the double-count. I split the deduped 35,780 by which sub-rule fired (/tmp/claude-501/mdmax/prec2.mjs): strong-then-':' = 5,729; strong-then-em/en-dash/hyphen = 12,951; bold text itself ending ':' = 11,336; bold text ending '.' = 5,764. Sum 35,780, reconciles. The 5,764 'ends with a period' bucket comes from the `[:.]$` disjunct in the researcher's own predicate and is a pure false positive — it is a bolded lead SENTENCE, not a record. Verbatim samples: '**Stable Zustand selectors only.** Never return a new object/array/Set from a selector'; '**One front door.** Today the brand is spread across separate LinkedIn surfaces'. The 12,951 dash bucket is mixed: '**Up to ₹5,000** — UPI app prompts biometric' is record-shaped, but '**Full redesign of the landing page** — modern, credible, conversion-focused' is prose apposition. Only the two colon buckets are unambiguous RECORDs ('**Last commit:** 2026-07-04').
verdicts.correction: Defensible RECORD count is 17,065 (33.1% of the claimed figure), or at most 30,016 if the entire ambiguous dash bucket is granted. 13.19 per 1,000 lines, 4.19 per file.

verdicts.claim: [Claim 1, continued] The workaround outnumbers the footnote 'by 8,603 to 1'; the footnote 'appears 6 times total'.
verdicts.reason: A rate reported against a hand-picked denominator, and a wrong absolute. The corpus contains footnoteDefinition = 6 AND footnoteReference = 10 = 16 footnote nodes, not '6 times total' — I re-derived both from the same s_*.json the researcher used. Choosing 6 rather than 16 inflates the ratio 2.67×, and it is the only denominator choice in the claim that is not stated. Compounded with the double-count and the false positives, the headline ratio moves by 8.1×. In fairness I tried to make this worse and failed: I grepped the vault for Obsidian inline footnotes (`^[...]`, which GFM/mdast cannot parse) and got 131 hits — but every one is a regex character class (`^[1234]` ×32, `^[\w.\-]` ×22, `^[0-9]` ×20). Footnote scarcity itself is real and survives.

verdicts.claim: [Claim 1, method] 'Typed-into-a-file strain' is the measure that recurs every day.
verdicts.reason: The corpus is 93.7% AI-authored on this metric and the researcher applied the authorship correction to Claim 2 (emoji) but not to Claim 1. Deduped instances: AI-authored (vaultmd + knowledge + frontmatter/docs) 33,533 over 973,903 lines = 34.43 per 1k; human-authored (readmes + k8s + ghdocs + rustbook + obshelp) 2,247 over 319,419 lines = 7.03 per 1k. Ratio 4.89×. Kubernetes alone is 1.01 per 1k, the Rust Book 2.03. The 'colonInBold' samples in the vault are dominated by `proj-*.md` files, which are MACHINE-GENERATED by Sagnik's own sgnk-snapshot skill (27 such files, each emitting '**Last commit:** …', '**Commits:** …', '**Remote:** …'). Those are not a human straining against markdown; they are a template.
verdicts.correction: The human strain rate is 7.03 per 1,000 lines, ~5× lower than the AI rate, and the headline figure should be reported split, exactly as Claim 2 was.

verdicts.claim: [Claim 2] Emoji DENSITY is 23× higher in human READMEs (105.52 vs 4.46 per 1k lines); AI corpora use emoji as a status enum, humans use them decoratively.
verdicts.reason: Two separate failures, both from the absence of any concentration check. (a) ONE file supplies 10,880 of 14,783 README emoji = 73.6%: /tmp/claude-501/mdmax/readmes/punkpeye_awesome-mcp-servers.md. Top-3 files = 79.5%. The MEDIAN emoji-bearing README has 9 emoji. Excluding that single file, README density falls 105.52 → 28.64 per 1k and the ratio falls 23.7× → 6.42×. (b) Worse, the dichotomy is refuted by its own top-4 evidence. I read that file's Legend section verbatim: '📇 – TypeScript (or JavaScript) codebase', '☁️ - Cloud Service', '🏠 - Local Service', '🍎 – For macOS'. The four glyphs cited as proof humans are 'topical/decorative' (☁1891 🏠1857 📇1824 🍎1193 = 6,765 = 45.8% of README emoji) are a hand-rolled, explicitly-declared, per-row TYPED ENUM — the exact construct the research says only AI reaches for. The AI/human split is an artifact of a whitelist (✅❌⚠🟢🔴🟡🟠⬜☐☑✔✖⛔🚫❗) picked from AI output, which by construction cannot see a user-defined enum.
verdicts.correction: The density ratio is 6.42× on the non-outlier corpus, and the sharpest human-corpus finding is the opposite of the one reported: humans DO build status/facet enums out of emoji, they just declare the alphabet in a legend first. That is a declared-shape precedent that argues FOR design item 2, and it was scored as decoration.

verdicts.claim: [Claim 3] kubernetes/website writes raw HTML tables 24.7× more often than markdown tables, 'driven by cell merging — which GFM tables cannot express at any price'; it is 'the largest professional human-authored technical documentation corpus in the sample'.
verdicts.reason:
Every raw number reproduces exactly (1,037 `--field-manager string     Default: "kubectl-edit"` — a CLI-flag generator faking indentation with   and spanning a 2-col grid, not a semantic merged-cell need. Likewise 722 of 1,037 `` (69.6%) are in auto-generated kubernetes-api reference, all emitting the same ``.
FieldDescription
verdicts.correction: The finding is: two doc GENERATORS emit HTML tables from a fixed template. It is evidence about kubernetes-sigs/reference-docs, not about humans needing merged cells. The DO-NOT-ADD verdict happens to be right, but it is right for a reason the evidence does not support.

verdicts.claim: [Claim 4] The link `title` slot is a 'semantics-free' channel, 99.94% unoccupied, on 3 of the 25 node types via the shared `Resource` mixin.
verdicts.reason: The occupancy numbers all reproduce (40/67,790 = 0.059%; 20/3,546 = 0.564%; 14/764 = 1.832%), the 25-node-type denominator is correct (mdast RootContentMap has exactly 25 keys), and only Definition, Image and Link extend Resource. But 'semantics-free' is refuted by the researcher's OWN cited file. node_modules/@types/mdast/index.d.ts lines 103–107, verbatim: 'Advisory information for the resource, such as would be appropriate for a tooltip.' And html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html, verbatim: 'Relying on the title attribute is currently discouraged as many user agents do not expose the attribute in an accessible manner as required by this specification (e.g., requiring a pointing device such as a mouse to cause a tooltip to appear, which excludes keyboard-only users and touch-only users…)'. There is also unacknowledged prior art for a sigil in exactly this slot: pandoc's changelog records 'Add `fig:` as title for images with captions' and 'Omit "fig:" prefix in image titles. This is used internally to…' — a magic title prefix consumed as a control signal for a decade. Pandoc's `link_attributes` extension also already types links: `[ref]: foo.jpg "optional title" {#id .class key=val}`.
verdicts.correction: The slot is low-OCCUPANCY, not semantics-free: it is the HTML advisory/tooltip channel, the spec discourages relying on it, and pandoc has already burned a prefix in it. Also '99.94% unoccupied' is the link-only figure; across all three Resource-bearing types it is 74/72,349 = 99.898%.

verdicts.claim: [Claim 5] GitHub preserves title/lang/dir/align/width/height/colspan/rowspan/cite/itemprop and strips rel/target/aria-label/role/download/loading/itemscope/itemtype; id survives but is rewritten to user-content-*.
verdicts.reason: Independently re-probed live 2026-08-01 against POST api.github.com/markdown mode=gfm with the researcher's exact input. Output byte-for-byte as claimed: `l` and `x`. The asymmetry the claim rests on — semantically correct `rel` destroyed, semantically vacuous `title` preserved — reproduces exactly. This is the strongest claim in the set.

verdicts.claim: [Claim 6] On GitHub a fence's meta survives as data-meta and lang as a lang attribute, but ONLY when the first word is not a Linguist-highlightable language.
verdicts.reason: Independently re-probed live. `\`\`\`decision status=open owner=sagnik` → `<pre lang="decision" data-meta="status=open owner=sagnik" class="notranslate">`; `\`\`\`mdmax.record type=decision` → `<pre lang="mdmax.record" data-meta="type=decision">`; `\`\`\`json title="config.json" mdmax:id=abc123` → `<div class="highlight highlight-source-json"><pre class="notranslate">` with lang and meta both gone. I extended the probe: `plaintext` is FREE (keeps data-meta), while `console` → highlight-text-shell-session, `jsonc` → highlight-source-json-comments and `vim-script` → highlight-source-viml all destroy the meta. Worth flagging for the design, though not against the claim: `lang` on `<pre>` is the BCP 47 natural-language attribute, so `lang="mdmax.record"` is an invalid language tag that GitHub itself hedges with `class="notranslate"`.

verdicts.claim: [Claim 7] The reserved set a fence carrier must avoid is exactly 1,240 tokens (816 language entries + 424 aliases), enumerable and fetchable; anything outside it survives with dispatch token and payload intact.
verdicts.reason: The CARDINALITY is right and the SET is wrong — membership was asserted from a count that happened to match, without testing the normalization the consumer applies. Linguist's alias index is keyed on `default_alias`, i.e. `name.downcase.gsub(/\s/,'-')`. 191 of the 816 language names contain a space. The researcher's method stored the space form ('Vim Script' → 'vim script', '1C Enterprise' → '1c enterprise'), so their set contains 191 members that are NOT reserved and OMITS the 191 tokens that ARE — a 15.4% error rate, and it errs in the dangerous direction. Live probe confirms: `\`\`\`vim-script foo=1` — a token the researcher's set reports as FREE — routes to `highlight-source-viml` and destroys the meta. Same exposure for `abap-cds`, `ant-build-system`, `answer-set-programming`, `adblock-filter-list` and 187 others.
verdicts.correction: The reserved set is 1,240 tokens under `name.downcase.gsub(/\s/,'-')` ∪ aliases. Rebuild it with that transform; the naive-lowercase set is wrong for 191 members in both directions.

verdicts.claim: [Claim 8] Obsidian publishes an explicit documented degradation contract: an unknown callout kind renders note-styled with its TITLE being the kind in title case; this makes design item 3's Obsidian degradation safe.
verdicts.reason: Both quotes verify verbatim in pub_obshelp/'en_Editing and formatting_Callouts.md' — 'Unless you [[#Customize callouts]], any unsupported type defaults to the `note` type. The type identifier is case-insensitive.' and 'By default, the title of the callout is its type identifier in title case.' and the `.callout[data-callout="custom-question-type"]` CSS hook. But the composite is an INFERENCE joining two sections: the title sentence is documented for supported types in the 'Change the title' section; the unsupported-type sentence documents only that the TYPE (colour + icon) falls back to note. That the unknown identifier is retained as the title is not stated anywhere, and the claim bills it as 'documented by the vendor, not inferred'. More seriously, the same page refutes the design built on it. Immediately after the title sentence: 'You can change it by adding text after the type identifier', example `> [!tip] Callouts can have custom titles`. Design item 3's proposed syntax is `> [!DECISION] status=open` — so in Obsidian that renders as a callout TITLED 'status=open', with the kind name gone from the visible surface. The stated degradation ('title is the kind in title case') is wrong for the researcher's own syntax.
verdicts.correction: Either drop the trailing k=v (put it in the block-scoped comment of design item 4) or accept that Obsidian shows the payload as the heading. The degradation must be re-derived for the syntax actually proposed.

verdicts.claim: [DESIGN 1] TYPED LINK on Resource.title: 'zero visual noise', 'Round-trip: IDENTICAL (measured)', and 'a plugin cannot close it — hoisting to frontmatter (what all 5 existing implementations do) changes what is being said'.
verdicts.reason: Three problems. (a) 'Zero visual noise' contradicts the same sentence's own degradation description ('i.e. a hover tooltip'). A tooltip IS visual noise, it fires on every hover over every typed link, and per the HTML spec quoted above it is keyboard- and touch-inaccessible. (b) Round-trip identity is delimiter-conditional. I tested through mdast-util-to-markdown: `[a](./x.md "@rel")` IDENTICAL, but `[a](./x.md '@rel')` and `[a](./x.md (@rel))` both normalize to the double-quote form. The claim states 'IDENTICAL (measured)' without the qualifier. (c) The prior-art claim does not survive a single GitHub API search. michaelpporter/breadcrumbs, 806 stars, README verbatim: 'Breadcrumbs lets you add _typed links_ to your notes' and, under 'Ways to define relationships', 'Frontmatter properties (typed links), tags, and **Markdown lists**' plus Dataview queries — i.e. it already reads typed edges from the body, at the point of reference, not only frontmatter. Querulantenkind/obsidian-typed-links-plugin ('Add semantic relationship types to links in Obsidian') also exists.
verdicts.correction: A plugin has closed a large part of it. The defensible residual argument for MDMAX is block identity across the git boundary (§1.1a), not 'nobody has built this' — and that argument should be made instead of the refuted one.

verdicts.claim: [DESIGN 5] TRANSCLUSION via comment-delimited regions; design item 4's HTML comment is 'byte-identical on round-trip as an html node'.
verdicts.reason:
The standalone comment does round-trip byte-identically (verified: `<!-- mdmax block=b7f2 kind=decision status=open -->

para
` → identical). The REGION form does not: `<!-- mdmax:include src=./part.md sha=91af -->
text
<!-- /mdmax:include -->
` re-serializes with blank lines inserted around both markers. That is the same §15.3 round-trip hazard class the research flagged for design item 3 and ranked it down to 3 for — and it was not flagged here, in the item pitched as the one 'where the degraded form is the correct form'. Also confirmed while testing: the `> \[!KIND]` escape fires on plain `> [!NOTE]` too, so the hazard is a pre-existing GFM property, not something MDMAX kinds introduce.

survived: Claim 5 in full — re-probed live against api.github.com/markdown 2026-08-01, output byte-identical to the report, including id → user-content-i rewriting. The rel-destroyed / title-preserved asymmetry is real.
Claim 6 in full — re-probed live; `decision` and `mdmax.record` keep lang + data-meta, `json` loses both. I extended it: `plaintext` is free; `console`, `jsonc`, `vim-script` are not.
Claim 4's occupancy counts — 40/67,790 links (0.059%), 20/3,546 images (0.564%), 14/764 definitions (1.832%), and none of the 40 existing titles begins with `@`. Re-derived from the same s_*.json.
Claim 4's node-type denominator — mdast RootContentMap has exactly 25 keys, and exactly Link, Image and Definition extend `Resource` (index.d.ts lines 585, 748, 805).
Claim 3's raw counts — 1,037 `<table`, 42 mdast table nodes, 1,632 colspan, 8 rowspan, ratio 24.69. All reproduce exactly.

Claim 3's sample representativeness, which I tried to break and could not — the 500-file k8s sample is 71.2% `reference/`, and the actual repo tree from api.github.com is 1,163/1,674 = 69.5% `reference/`.
Claim 8's two verbatim quotes and the `data-callout` CSS hook — all present in pub_obshelp/'en_Editing and formatting_Callouts.md'.
Claim 7's cardinality — 816 top-level entries + 424 alias lines = 1,240 distinct, with zero name/alias collisions.

Footnote scarcity itself — I attacked this by grepping the vault for Obsidian inline footnotes `^[...]` (unparseable by GFM) and found 131 hits, but every one is a regex character class. The counter-attack failed; footnotes really are near-absent.
Claim 2's arithmetic — 105.52, 4.46, 23.7×, 76.4%, 88.2%, 2.0%, and k8s 0 emoji in 97,404 lines. Every figure recomputes.
The DO-NOT-ADD list's conclusions — all six are defensible outcomes even where the supporting evidence is weaker than stated (notably tables, per the verdict above).
The double-quote form of the typed-link title round-trips byte-identically through mdast-util-to-markdown, including embedded `k=v`, escaped quotes and parentheses.
killed: 51,620 — double-counts 15,840 instances; true deduped union is 35,780, defensible RECORD count 17,065.
8,603:1 — becomes 5,963:1 deduped, 2,844:1 strict, 1,067:1 against all 16 footnote nodes.
'the footnote … appears 6 times total' — 6 definitions plus 10 references = 16.
39.91 per 1,000 lines and 12.7 per file — 27.67 / 8.78 deduped, 13.19 / 4.19 strict.
'Emoji DENSITY is 23× higher in human READMEs' — 73.6% of that corpus's emoji come from one file; 6.42× without it.
'humans use emoji decoratively' — the top-4 human glyphs (45.8% of README emoji) are a declared enum legend: 📇 TypeScript, ☁️ Cloud Service, 🏠 Local Service, 🍎 macOS.
'driven by cell merging' (k8s) — 99.6% of colspans are the identical colspan="2", 69% inside generated kubectl reference, exactly 1 in a hand-authored page.
'the largest professional human-authored technical documentation corpus' — 69.6% of its HTML tables are auto-generated API reference.

'the link title slot is … semantics-free' — the cited mdast d.ts calls it 'Advisory information … appropriate for a tooltip'; the HTML spec discourages relying on it; pandoc used a `fig:` sigil in that exact slot for a decade.
'99.94% unoccupied' as a property of the Resource mixin — that is the link-only figure; across all three types it is 99.898%.
'zero visual noise' for the typed link — it produces a hover tooltip on every typed link, keyboard- and touch-inaccessible per the HTML spec.
Claim 7's reserved SET — 191 members are the wrong (un-hyphenated) form and 191 genuinely-reserved first-word tokens are absent; `vim-script` is reported free and is not.
Design 3's Obsidian degradation — Obsidian turns text after the type identifier into the callout TITLE, so `> [!DECISION] status=open` renders titled 'status=open', per the same page the claim cites.
Design 1's 'a plugin cannot close it' — michaelpporter/breadcrumbs (806★) reads typed links from Markdown lists and Dataview inline fields, i.e. in-body at the point of reference.
'Round-trip: IDENTICAL (measured)' for the typed link — holds only for the double-quote delimiter; `'…'` and `(…)` both normalize.
new_defects: OVERLAP NEVER TESTED. Two metrics were summed as if disjoint without a single check that they are. The scanner's own output contained the tell (`recordInListItem` ≈ the double-counted set in every corpus) and it was not read. Any two counters that can fire on the same node must be measured as a union over node identity, never added.

INCONSISTENT NORMALIZATION ACROSS CLAIMS. Claim 2 correctly splits AI-authored from human-authored corpora and makes that split the whole finding. Claim 1 aggregates the identical mixed corpus with no split, and 93.7% of its instances are AI-authored. The same correction must be applied to every claim in a report or to none.

CLASSIFIER BUILT FROM THE CONCLUSION. The status-glyph whitelist was assembled from AI output, so a human-authored enum expressed in different glyphs is structurally invisible to it. The dichotomy it 'discovers' is the one it encodes. A category classifier must be validated against held-out instances of the category it claims to be absent.

NO CONCENTRATION CHECK ON ANY DENSITY OR RATIO. Every rate in the report is a corpus mean with no Gini/top-k/median reported. One file supplies 73.6% of one headline; one code generator supplies 69% of another. A per-1,000-lines figure without a top-k share is not a measurement of the corpus, it is a measurement of its largest file.

GENERATED TEXT COUNTED AS AUTHORED STRAIN. Nowhere does the method separate machine-emitted markdown from human-typed markdown, yet the entire thesis is 'strain' — which requires someone to strain. The vault's `proj-*.md` files are emitted by Sagnik's own sgnk-snapshot skill; the k8s tables come from kubernetes-sigs/reference-docs; the kubectl colspans come from the kubectl doc generator. Deduplicate by generator template before counting.

SET MEMBERSHIP INFERRED FROM A MATCHING CARDINALITY. 816 + 424 = 1,240 was treated as proof the set was right. The count was right and 15.4% of the members were wrong, because the consumer's normalization (`gsub(/\s/,'-')`) was never read. When enumerating a set someone else will match against, apply their transform and spot-probe members you believe are free.

ABSENCE-OF-PRIOR-ART ASSERTED WITHOUT A SEARCH. 'A plugin cannot close it' and '820 forum likes have produced almost no supply' are falsified by one api.github.com/search/repositories call that returns an 806-star plugin literally named for the construct. Any 'nobody has built this' must cite the search that was run.

ROUND-TRIP IDENTITY REPORTED WITHOUT ITS VARIANT COVERAGE. 'IDENTICAL (measured)' was true for the tested spelling and false for two other legal spellings of the same construct. Round-trip claims must state which surface variants were exercised — and the transclusion region in design item 5 was never tested at all, though it fails.

per_area.title: Adjacent-field transplant — capabilities documents have never had
per_area.headline: Every capability on the transplant list is downstream of one prerequisite documents have never had (a stable coordinate independent of content), but a second prerequisite decides which ones are actually buildable — a dependency substrate — and I measured markdown's to be nearly empty (sub-file references are 0.61% of internal edges in `md` and 0.02% in `knowledge`, transclusions 0.13% and 0.00%, and there are ZERO declared `^block-id`s across 2,262 files), which kills the spreadsheet and Figma/prefab transplants outright and moves the whole opportunity into the metadata plane, where the substrate is dense and the defects are real (a shipped template with 0/253 conformance, one section living under three names across 167 files, and a `status` enum violated by a case-only `ACTIVE`).

findings.claim: Markdown's sub-file reference substrate is empty in real corpora — which kills the premise that block identity's value is repairing existing block/heading references, and replicates johnnydecimal's complaint quantitatively.
findings.evidence: Census script over ~/Desktop/GitHub/md (1,989 .md, 50,480,470 bytes): wikilinks 16,160 of which wikilink_file 16,144, wikilink_heading 15, wikilink_block 1; transclusions 21; TOTAL internal reference edges 16,626; SUB-FILE granular 102 (0.61%); TRUE VALUE FLOW (transclusion) 21 (0.13%); 'declared ^block-ids in corpus 0'. Replicated on ~/Desktop/GitHub/knowledge (273 .md): wikilinks 4,143, wikilink_heading 1, wikilink_block 0, transclusions 0, SUB-FILE granular 1 (0.02%), declared ^block-ids 0. Script: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-sagnikmitra-Desktop-GitHub-frontmatter/9e5a4a9f-8c4a-4758-b560-0afea2b30447/scratchpad/adjacent-census.py

findings.claim: Early cutoff (Salsa's 'backdating') is the highest-yield build-system transplant AND its yield is 8.6× sensitive to whether the compiler stratifies the interface by durability — this is the direct, measured answer to Obsidian's stated performance blocker.
findings.evidence: Over 416 commits of ~/Desktop/GitHub/md, 362 modified .md file-revisions: 'STRUCTURAL interface unchanged (heads+links+bids+fm KEYS): 250 (69.1%)' vs 'FULL interface unchanged (also fm VALUES): 29 (8.0%)'. The entire gap is one low-durability key: top churning frontmatter keys = [('mirrored', 207), ('public_slug', 44), ('generated', 12), ('title', 9)]. On ~/Desktop/GitHub/knowledge (45 commits, 135 revisions) both figures are 37.8% — no gain, because its churning keys (fidelity, key_terms, entities, length) are content-derived. Scripts: scratchpad/earlycutoff.py and scratchpad/ec2.py

findings.claim: Excel — the canonical dependency-graph system — deliberately does NOT implement early cutoff, so transplanting 'the spreadsheet' would import the weaker of the two available dependency engines.
findings.evidence: learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office/vba/excel/concepts/excel-performance/excel-improving-calculation-performance, verbatim: "Excel continues calculating cells that depend on previously calculated cells even if the value of the previously calculated cell does not change when it is calculated." Same page: "The smart recalculation engine in Excel tries to minimize calculation time by continuously tracking both the precedents and dependencies for each formula (the cells referenced by the formula) and any changes that were made since the last calculation." And on the incrementality break-even: "For some complex workbooks, the time taken to build and maintain the dependency trees needed for Smart Recalculation is larger than the time saved by Smart Recalculation."

findings.claim: Salsa states early cutoff precisely and gives it a name and a mechanism, plus 'durability' as an explicit optimization — this is the transplantable design, not Excel's.
findings.evidence: raw.githubusercontent.com/salsa-rs/salsa/master/book/src/plumbing/terminology/backdate.md, verbatim: "Backdating is when we mark a value that was computed in revision R as having last changed in some earlier revision. This is done when we have an older memo M and we can compare the two values to see that, while the dependencies to M may have changed, the result of the query function did not." And book/src/reference/algorithm.md: "If a tracked function depends (transitively) only on high durability inputs, and you change a low durability input, then we can very easily determine that the tracked function result is still valid, avoiding the need to traverse the input edges one by one."

findings.claim: Microsoft publishes the exact latency budget a document compiler should be held to, and it is a four-band UX spec, not a vibe.
findings.evidence: Same Microsoft Learn page, verbatim: "For calculation times of less than about a tenth of a second, users feel that the system is responding instantly." / "Between a tenth of a second and one second, users can successfully keep a train of thought going, although they will notice the response time delay." / "As calculation time increases (usually between 1 and 10 seconds), users must switch to manual calculation when they enter data." / "For calculation times greater than 10 seconds, users become impatient and usually switch to other tasks while they wait."

findings.claim: The Figma-component / game-engine-prefab transplant (transclusion-as-components, the #2 most-liked Obsidian request at 553 likes) has essentially NO substrate — human-authored cross-file block duplication is 0.14–1.23%, and the headline 26% figure is an artifact of a machine-generated mirror.
findings.evidence: scratchpad/dup2.py: md/ HUMAN-AUTHORED (excl Mirrors, Skills, .sgnk): files=385, distinct blocks=16,156, cross-file duplicated 198 (1.23%). md/Research only: 218 files, 11 (0.14%). knowledge/: 273 files, 16 (0.20%). frontmatter/docs: 45 files, 5 (0.32%). The full md corpus scores 12,972 (26.32%) ONLY because Mirrors/skills-registry contributes machine-generated boilerplate — top duplicate is in 415 files: 'The skill executes when its trigger fires (slash command, natural-language match, or direct invocation)...'. The largest human-authored duplicates are template artifacts, not content: [69] "## How I'd apply this to my Claude Code env", [27] '**Relevance to stack:** high  |  **Priority:** P1'.

findings.claim: The duplication that DOES exist is at the TYPE level, not the instance level — and the declared type has ZERO conformance while two emergent types have 87 and 53 members. This is Shipman & Marshall's 'Formality Considered Harmful' measured locally, and it validates PLAN §1.3's inferred-over-declared choice independently.
findings.evidence: ~/Desktop/GitHub/knowledge ships templates/synthesis-note.md with 8 h2 sections (## TL;DR / ## The ecosystem (map of the work) / ## Key ideas / ## Frameworks / models / methods / ## Notable quotes / data / ## How I'd apply this / ## Connections / ## Open questions). Measured over 253 non-template notes: 'EXACT h2 skeleton match to template : 0', 'superset of template h2 sections : 0'; every one of the 253 is missing 'the ecosystem (map of the work)'; 251 missing 'frameworks / models / methods'. Meanwhile 39 distinct h2 skeletons cover 199 notes, largest two: [87 files] ['tl;dr','timeline map','key ideas','demos / frameworks / commands',"how i'd apply this to my claude code env",'open questions / contradictions','connections'] and [53 files] ['tl;dr','map of the work','key ideas','reusable frameworks & methods','quotes & numbers',"how i'd apply this (sgnk)",'connections']. One semantic section under three names: "how i'd apply this to my claude code env" 88 files, "how i'd apply this (sgnk)" 61, "how i'd apply this" 18 — 167 files, and ZERO links point at any of them.

findings.claim: PLAN §1.3's open risk — that the flagship `status: activ` schema-violation demo had zero real instances in 3,228 documents — now has a real, live instance, and its true shape is case drift plus prose-in-an-enum-slot, not a typo.
findings.evidence: scratchpad/fmvals2.py (YAML `#` comments stripped) over ~/Desktop/GitHub/md, 722 files with frontmatter: status n=575 distinct=5, majority [('active',368),('done',203)], OUTLIERS(3) = [('ACTIVE', 2), ('finalized — quality verdict + Nx assessment backed by a coordinator-run E2E (145 assertions, 1 defect fixed); see AIOS-E2E-Test-Results-2026-07-01.md', 1), ('PROPOSED — not yet reviewed by Sagnik', 1)] — 3/575 = 0.52%. category n=544 distinct=8 mixes three casing conventions in one key: [('General',230),('ai',172),('Printing Press',116),('Design',8),('Planning',8),('computer-science',4),('sgnk',4),('Codex',2)].

findings.claim: The human-authored schema already exists in the corpus — written as YAML comments — and PLAN §1.5's wedge is sharper than stated: the market leader deletes exactly that channel.
findings.evidence: scratchpad/fmvals2.py: knowledge/ has 13 frontmatter lines carrying an inline `#` comment, 5 of which declare an enum (contain '|'), across keys {'item_type': 1, 'fidelity': 1, 'status': 2, 'entity_kind': 1}. Verbatim from knowledge/templates/synthesis-note.md: `item_type: generic        # book|paper|video|podcast|article|doc|dataset|code-repo|course|slides|sheet|image|web|generic`, `fidelity: verbatim        # verbatim|ocr|auto-transcribed|partial|summary-only`, `status: done              # queued|processing|done|failed|skipped`. PLAN §1.5 records that Obsidian's processFrontMatter "deletes YAML comments outright".

findings.claim: SQL already supplies the complete decision procedure for 'what happens when you delete something that is referenced', including the deferred-checking middle ground that solves the nag-while-typing problem — and no document tool has any of it.
findings.evidence: raw.githubusercontent.com/postgres/postgres/master/doc/src/sgml/ref/create_table.sgml: five referential_action values are specified — NO ACTION ("Produce an error if the deletion or update would create a foreign key constraint violation"), RESTRICT ("Produce an error if a row to be deleted or updated matches a row in the referencing table. This prevents the action even if the state after the action would not violate the foreign key constraint"), CASCADE ("Delete any rows referencing the deleted row"), SET NULL, SET DEFAULT. Deferral: "If the constraint is INITIALLY DEFERRED, it is checked only at the end of the transaction." Contrast the nearest markdown prior art, IWE's CLI table (raw.githubusercontent.com/iwe-org/iwe/master/README.md): "| `delete` | Remove a note and clean up references |" — one hard-coded CASCADE, no declaration site, no RESTRICT.

findings.claim: Typed holes are a shipped, specified language feature whose defining property — the program still compiles and still runs with the hole in it — is exactly what a document needs, and no markdown tool models an unfilled value as anything but a string.
findings.evidence: raw.githubusercontent.com/ghc/ghc/master/docs/users_guide/exts/typed_holes.rst, verbatim: "During compilation these holes will generate an error message that describes which type is expected at the hole's location, information about the origin of any free type variables, and a list of local bindings that might help fill the hole and bindings in scope that fit the type of the hole" and "you can run and test a piece of code containing holes, by using the -fdefer-typed-holes flag. This flag defers errors produced by typed holes until runtime, and converts them into compile-time warnings." Substrate measured locally: 90 empty-string frontmatter values (`key: ""`) across 253 non-template knowledge notes, plus placeholders in the shipped template (`title: <title of the work>`, `created: YYYY-MM-DD`, `id: YYYYMMDD-slug`).

findings.claim: LSP defines 69 requests; Marksman — the most advanced markdown language server — ships roughly 11 of them and NONE of the structural-analysis ones, so the IDE transplant is not 'adopt LSP', it is 'implement the two-thirds of LSP nobody implemented for prose'.
findings.evidence: raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/vscode-languageserver-node/main/protocol/metaModel.json (434,788 bytes) parsed this session: 69 requests, 26 notifications; textDocument/* = 35, workspace* = 18. Absent from Marksman's own feature list (raw.githubusercontent.com/artempyanykh/marksman/main/docs/features.md, full ✅ list = document symbols, workspace symbols, link completion, hover preview, goto definition, find references, wiki-link diagnostics, multi-folder workspaces, custom parser, CodeLens '# references', rename refactor): textDocument/prepareCallHierarchy, callHierarchy/incomingCalls, callHierarchy/outgoingCalls, textDocument/prepareTypeHierarchy, typeHierarchy/supertypes, typeHierarchy/subtypes, textDocument/moniker, textDocument/linkedEditingRange, textDocument/inlayHint, textDocument/semanticTokens/*, workspace/diagnostic, workspace/willRenameFiles, workspace/willDeleteFiles. Marksman's roadmap still lists as unbuilt: "🗓 Add \"check\" command for standalone workspace checking."

findings.claim: Parameterized transclusion — the actual Figma/prefab analogue — is NOT unclaimed: MediaWiki has run it at Wikipedia scale since 2002, and its source shows the transplant requires an evaluator, which PLAN §2.4's no-runtime invariant excludes.
findings.evidence: raw.githubusercontent.com/wikimedia/mediawiki/master/includes/Parser/PPFrame.php declares `getNumberedArguments()`, `getNamedArguments()`, `getArgument($name)`, and "Returns true if the infinite loop check is OK, false if a loop is detected — public function loopCheck( $title );" plus "Set the 'volatile' flag... Callers should avoid caching the result of an expansion if it has the volatile flag set." PPFrame_Hash.php carries `public $loopCheckHash;` ("having been encountered previously in parent frames"), `private $maxPPExpandDepth;`, `$this->maxPPNodeCount`, `$this->childExpansionCache`, and emits 'Node-count limit exceeded' / limitationWarn('expansion-depth-exceeded'). Note the exact mirror of Excel's escape hatch: both dependency engines needed a 'volatile' flag for impure nodes.

findings.claim: Even the best-funded component system in the world loses overrides on swap — so 'instances with overrides' is not a solved problem being withheld from documents, it is a hard problem whose leading implementation degrades.
findings.evidence: help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/360039150413, verbatim: "Figma will try to preserve any overrides when you select a different variant, or swap between instances in the Instance menu." / "Figma only preserves text overrides. To keep any changes you've made to text layers, rename the layers so they're unique." / "If you swap a component with other overrides applied, we won't apply these to the new component." Unity (docs.unity3d.com/Manual/PrefabVariants.html): "A prefab variant inherits properties from a base prefab. Overrides in the variant take precedence over the base values."

findings.claim: git notes is the exact precedent for a tier-4 sidecar that never touches the artifact — and gitattributes is the precedent for declaring a merge policy per unit, but both stop at file/object granularity, which is the gap block identity fills.
findings.evidence: raw.githubusercontent.com/git/git/master/Documentation/git-notes.adoc, verbatim: "Adds, removes, or reads notes attached to objects, without touching the objects themselves." / "A typical use of notes is to supplement a commit message without changing the commit itself." raw.githubusercontent.com/git/git/master/Documentation/gitattributes.adoc built-in merge drivers: `text` ("Usual 3-way file level merge"), `binary` ("Keep the version from your branch in the work tree, but leave the path in the conflicted state"), `union` ("Run 3-way file level merge for text files, but take lines from both versions, instead of leaving conflict markers"). All are keyed on PATH — nothing operates below file level.

findings.claim: The typed-link vocabulary that the market's most-demanded unbuilt markdown feature needs already exists as a maintained standard — nobody has to invent it, and nobody has connected the two.
findings.evidence: raw.githubusercontent.com/sparontologies/cito/master/docs/current/cito.ttl (146,447 bytes), owl:versionIRI <http://purl.org/spar/cito/2026-06-22> (i.e. maintained six weeks ago). Parsed: 98 owl:ObjectProperty declarations; 43 with `rdfs:subPropertyOf <http://purl.org/spar/cito/cites>`. Ontology's own description, verbatim: "CiTO contains just two main object properties, cito:cites and its inverse cito:isCitedBy, each of which has forty-one sub-properties." Names include agreesWith, disagreesWith, disputes, extends, confirms, corrects, critiques, givesSupportTo, citesAsEvidence, citesAsDataSource, includesQuotationFrom, usesMethodIn. Prior research recorded the demand: Obsidian FR #6994 typed links, 820 likes, 213 posts, 49,514 views, OPEN 5.8 years.

findings.claim: Scientific publishing has machine-readable supersession/retraction semantics that ordinary documents completely lack — and this is the single cheapest transplant that directly serves G3 (an AI reading a stale .md has no way to know it is stale).
findings.evidence: Live read of api.crossref.org/works?filter=update-type:retraction&rows=1: `"update-to":[{"DOI":"10.1016/j.micpro.2020.103768","type":"retraction","label":"Retraction","source":"publisher"}]` and `"updated-by":[{..."type":"retraction"...},{"DOI":"10.1016/j.micpro.2024.105020","type":"erratum","label":"Erratum"}]`. Crossref's own framing (crossref.org/documentation/crossmark/): "The Crossmark button gives readers quick and easy access to the current status of an item of content, including any corrections, retractions, or updates to that record."

findings.claim: Circular-reference detection and dead-code elimination are false transplants at the link layer — cycles are normal and benign in prose, and the unused-import analogue has essentially no population.
findings.evidence: scratchpad/adjacent-census.py on md: 'link-graph back edges 347', 'transclusion-graph back edges 0'. Dead code: 'link ref definitions 6; UNUSED 0 (0.0%)' and 'footnote defs 0' across 1,989 files; knowledge: 0 refdefs, 0 footnote defs. The only dangling-reference population found anywhere was 9 footnote USES with no definition, in 1,989 files. Cycle detection is meaningful only on the expansion graph — which is why MediaWiki needs loopCheckHash — and that graph has 21 edges in md and 0 in knowledge.

findings.claim: EDA's design-rule checker, not CAD's constraint solver, is the transplantable half — and its shape (per-rule severity, a custom-rule language, per-violation waivers) is already the right UX for PLAN §6's confidence ladder.
findings.evidence: docs.kicad.org/8.0/en/pcbnew/pcbnew.html, verbatim: "The Violation Severity section allows you to configure the severity of each type of design rule check. Each rule may be set to create an error marker, a warning marker, or no marker (ignored)." / "The Custom Rules section contains a text editor for creating design rules using the custom rules language. Custom rules are used to create specific design rule checks that are not covered by the basic constraints or net class settings." / "Individual rule violations may be ignored in the Design Rule Checker."

findings.claim: Non-destructive editing (the DAW transplant) is not a feature — it is an indirection layer that only exists because the medium has a stable coordinate independent of the content, which is precisely the thing block identity would create for documents.
findings.evidence: manual.ardour.org/working-with-playlists/understanding-playlists/, verbatim: "A playlist is a list of regions ordered in time. It defines which parts of which source files should be played and when." / "a track has a playlist" / "the playlist associated with a track can be changed at (almost) any time" / "tracks can even share playlists." The invariant axis is time; in video it is timecode; in CAD it is the feature tree; in a build system it is the target label; in a database it is the primary key. A markdown document has never had one — which is the structural reason none of these capabilities exist for prose.

findings.claim: The rename/impact-preview blast radius is real but modest at file granularity and effectively zero at heading granularity, so 'impact preview' must be sold on the metadata plane, not the link plane.
findings.evidence: scratchpad/adjacent-census.py on md: distinct link targets 6,487; mean/median fan-in 2.49/1; fan-in==1 is 4,154 (64.0%); fan-in>=5 is 756; fan-in>=20 is 17; max 58 ('Anthropic=58', 'Claude Code=56', 'projects-index=48'). Sub-file: 'distinct heading-targeted anchors 10 (uses 15)', 'distinct block-targeted anchors 1 (uses 1)'. Anchor ambiguity for a rename: headings with duplicate text inside the same file = 402 of 10,285 (3.91%) in md, 19 of 3,562 (0.53%) in knowledge; heading slug collisions 403 (3.92%) and 19 (0.53%).

findings.claim: CORRECTION to a likely assumption: structural search-and-replace over markdown DOES exist — ast-grep lists Markdown as a first-class supported language — so the codemod transplant is partially claimed and the honest gap is cross-file symbol resolution, not pattern matching.
findings.evidence: raw.githubusercontent.com/ast-grep/ast-grep/main/crates/language/src/lib.rs line 259-288: `pub enum SupportLang { Bash, C, Cpp, CSharp, Css, Dart, Go, Elixir, Haskell, Hcl, Html, Java, JavaScript, Json, Kotlin, Lua, Markdown, Nix, Php, Python, Ruby, Rust, Scala, Solidity, Swift, Tsx, TypeScript, Yaml }` — Markdown is present and included in `all_langs()`. For scale of the surrounding ecosystem (npmjs.org/downloads/point/last-week, fetched this session): remark-parse 45,820,243; mdast-util-to-markdown 44,940,019; unified 45,345,676; markdownlint 2,886,431; remark-lint 324,705 — the lint layer is 1/16th the parse layer, and all of it is single-file.

findings.claim: Bazel supplies the exact query vocabulary an 'impact preview' needs, already named and specified — this is a naming/UX transplant, not a research problem.
findings.evidence: raw.githubusercontent.com/bazelbuild/bazel/master/site/en/query/quickstart.md: "To see what targets depend on a particular target/package, you can use rdeps(universe_scope, target)" and "Two functions can help you find dependency paths: somepath() and allpaths(). Given a starting target S and an end point E, find a path between S and E by using somepath(S,E)... somepath() gives you a single path out of the two options, whereas allpaths() outputs every possible path." site/en/basics/hermeticity.md: "Hermetic build systems use this hash to identify changes to the build's input" and "The output of an action can be cached, and the action need not be run again unless inputs change."

unclaimed: Durability-stratified early cutoff over a document vault — recompute cross-file queries only when a file's INTERFACE hash moves, and declare per-frontmatter-key durability so a sync bot's timestamp cannot invalidate the world. Believed unclaimed because Marksman's shipped feature list contains no incremental/caching entry and its roadmap still lists a basic `check` command as unbuilt; IWE's throughput claim ('20,000 files in under a second') is a full-scan figure, not an incremental one; and Excel's own documentation proves the canonical dependency engine skips backdating deliberately.

Declared referential actions on document delete/move — RESTRICT | CASCADE | SET NULL | NO ACTION as a per-link-type declaration. Believed unclaimed because the closest prior art, IWE, ships exactly one hard-coded behaviour ('Remove a note and clean up references') with no declaration site and no RESTRICT, and no editor surveyed exposes any referential action at all.

Deferred (save/commit-time) constraint checking for documents — Postgres' INITIALLY DEFERRED applied to prose. Believed unclaimed because every markdown checker found is either per-keystroke editor lint or CI-only; the middle ground that makes constraints tolerable while writing has no markdown analogue.

Typed holes in documents with defer semantics — an unfilled value is a first-class node with an expected type, enumerable across the vault, and the document still compiles and still projects. Believed unclaimed because no markdown tool models an unfilled value as anything but a string; 90 empty-string frontmatter values sit in one 253-note corpus with nothing enumerating them.

Inferred document CLASS plus totality (missing-required-section) checking, with the declared template treated as a hypothesis rather than law. Believed unclaimed because the one corpus that ships its own template has 0/253 conformance to it while two emergent classes have 87 and 53 members, and every existing validator (remark-lint-frontmatter-schema and siblings) checks a DECLARED schema only.

Source maps from an AI-facing projection back to source bytes, so an edit expressed in projection coordinates splices into the original. Believed unclaimed because every AI markdown integration surveyed round-trips through a stringifier (DesktopCommanderMCP #440 is the documented damage), and the TC39 source-map model has never been applied to a prose projection.

Content-addressed, out-of-band BLOCK annotations — git notes below file granularity. Believed unclaimed because git notes annotate commits and blobs, and no markdown tool has a stable sub-file address to hang them on: zero declared `^block-id`s across 2,262 files is the proof of absence.

Per-block merge policy declaration — gitattributes' `union`/`binary`/`text` choice made per block type instead of per path. Believed unclaimed because `.gitattributes` is path-scoped by construction and nothing in the markdown world operates below file level.

Machine-readable supersession and retraction for ordinary documents — a plain .md saying 'I was superseded by X' or 'this claim was corrected' in a degradable channel. Believed unclaimed because Crossref's update-to/updated-by exists only for DOI-bearing scholarly works; an AI reading a stale .md has no signal whatsoever.

A standardized typed-link vocabulary applied to notes — adopt CiTO's 43 sub-properties of `cites` instead of inventing a relation set. Believed unclaimed because CiTO has been maintained since 2010 (versionIRI 2026-06-22) and typed links is the single most-liked unbuilt markdown feature (820 likes, 5.8 years), and nobody has connected the two.

Call hierarchy, type hierarchy, monikers, linked editing ranges and pull-diagnostics for documents in a WRITING editor. Believed unclaimed because LSP specifies all of them (69 requests in metaModel.json), Marksman implements none of them, and Marksman's integrations are exclusively programmer editors (VSCode/Neovim/Vim/Emacs/Helix/Sublime/Zed).
per_area.design:
THE ORGANISING PRINCIPLE (this is the finding, the six designs are consequences).

Every capability on the transplant list is downstream of TWO prerequisites, not one.
  P1 — a stable coordinate independent of content. Spreadsheets: the cell address. IDEs: the symbol in a symbol table. Build systems: the target label + input hash. Databases: the primary key. VCS: the object hash. CAD: the feature id. DAWs: timecode. Documents have never had one; MDMAX's re-anchoring is the first candidate. The starting evidence was right that this is the unlock.
  P2 — a DEPENDENCY substrate for the capability to chew on. This is the one the starting evidence missed, and it is where the ranking is decided. I measured markdown's: sub-file references are 0.61% of internal edges in `md` and 0.02% in `knowledge`; transclusions 0.13% and 0.00%; declared `^block-id`s are ZERO across 2,262 files.
So the transplants split three ways:
  CLASS A — need P1 plus the METADATA plane, which is densely populated (36.3% of md files carry frontmatter, 78 distinct keys, 42 keys in >=10 files, an 87-file emergent document class). BUILD THESE.
  CLASS B — need a link/transclusion substrate that does not yet exist and that the product must CREATE before the capability has anything to operate on. Buildable, but the editor must write the substrate first; sell later.
  CLASS C — need an oracle for what prose MEANS. Not a compiler feature. Never sound.

THE SIX, ranked by (real analogue) x (buildable on a markdown compiler with block identity) x (nobody has it).

1. EARLY CUTOFF WITH DURABILITY STRATIFICATION  [from build systems: Salsa backdating + Bazel; explicitly NOT Excel]
   Ship: pass 2 emits, per file, TWO hashes — an INTERFACE hash over (heading list with levels, outgoing link targets, declared block ids, frontmatter KEY set) and a CONTENT hash. Every cross-file query (backlinks, reference counts, schema check, outline of other files) depends only on the interface hash. When a file is re-parsed and its interface hash is unchanged, BACKDATE: mark the derived value as last-changed in the earlier revision and skip every dependent. Frontmatter keys carry a durability tier declared once per vault (HIGH = schema-bearing: type, status, tags; LOW = machine-written: last_synced, mirrored, content_hash); LOW keys are excluded from the interface hash by construction.
   Why it wins: measured 69.1% of 362 real file-revisions leave the structural interface unchanged, against 8.0% for the full interface — an 8.6x swing produced by ONE key (`mirrored`, 207 of 362). It is the literal answer to the vendor's stated blocker ("monitoring heading changes automatically is impractical from a performance perspective"), and it is held to a published budget: Microsoft's own <0.1s = "instant" band.
   CLI: `mdmax why <file>` (what invalidated this), `mdmax rdeps <target>` (Bazel's name, use it), `mdmax stat --cutoff` (hit rate).
   Degradation: none — nothing reaches disk.

2. REFERENTIAL ACTIONS, DEFERRED  [from SQL]
   Ship: every reference kind (wikilink, transclusion, frontmatter value naming another doc) gets a declared action from Postgres' exact five — NO ACTION, RESTRICT, CASCADE, SET NULL, SET DEFAULT — with a vault default and per-key overrides in frontmatter. Deleting or moving a referenced block/file runs the declared action; RESTRICT blocks with a listed blast radius; CASCADE rewrites and shows the diff; SET NULL leaves a typed hole (see 3). Checking is INITIALLY DEFERRED by default: constraints are evaluated at save/commit, not per keystroke.
   Why it wins: IWE already proves the CASCADE half is implementable and useful, but hard-codes it with no declaration and no RESTRICT. The deferred half is the actual invention — it is how you get compiler-grade integrity without a linter screaming at a half-written sentence.
   Carrier: the declaration is a frontmatter key (tier 1). A dumb viewer sees a key it ignores.
   Honest scope: blast radius is modest — mean fan-in 2.49, 64% of targets have fan-in 1, max 58. Sell it as "never silently break", not "save hours".

3. TYPED HOLES WITH DEFER SEMANTICS  [from GHC/Agda/Idris]
   Ship: a hole is a first-class node with an expected type — an empty frontmatter value (`key: ""`), a template placeholder (`<title of the work>`, `YYYY-MM-DD`), a `TODO`/`TK` in prose, or a SET-NULL'd reference from (2). The compiler reports, per hole: expected type, where the expectation came from, and candidate fills drawn from sibling documents of the same inferred class — GHC's "valid hole fits" for documents. Critically, holes are DEFERRED by default (`-fdefer-typed-holes`): the document still compiles, still projects, still exports. A hole becomes an error only at a declared gate (publish, export, PR).
   Why it wins: this is the best single fit to G2 and G3. It hands an agent a typed, enumerable, addressable worklist INSIDE a document with zero new syntax and zero adoption from the receiving side — an unfilled value is just an empty value. Substrate is already there: 90 empty-string frontmatter values across 253 knowledge notes.
   Surface: `workspace/diagnostic` (LSP already specifies it; nobody implements it for markdown), plus `mdmax holes --type date` as an agent tool.

4. INFERRED DOCUMENT CLASS + TOTALITY CHECKING  [from type theory + DB schema; NOT declared templates]
   Ship: cluster documents by (heading skeleton, frontmatter key set) into inferred CLASSES. For each class report totality failures — a member missing a section that >=80% of the class has; an enum value outside the class's observed value set; a section present under a variant NAME (the alias case). Never prescribe: the class is a hypothesis with a member count and a confidence, surfaced as "212 of 253 notes have `## Key ideas`; this one does not", not "invalid".
   Why it wins: measured 0/253 conformance to a template the repo SHIPS, against 87- and 53-member emergent classes, and one semantic section living under three names across 167 files with zero links pointing at any of them. That is Shipman & Marshall measured locally, and it is a fresh, independent confirmation of PLAN §1.3's inferred-over-declared bet. The `status` enum is violated by 3/575 including a case-only `ACTIVE` — the real, non-fabricated instance PLAN §1.3 said it lacked.
   Gate: do NOT build this before the precision experiment below. It is the one design whose value is entirely a precision question.

5. PROJECTION SOURCE MAPS  [from JS build tooling; TC39 source-map]
   Ship: every tier-4 projection — the token-efficient AI view, the outline, the graph — emits a mapping in the shape of the TC39 spec's Original Position Record (source, line, column) alongside the projected text. An agent edits in projection coordinates; the mapping resolves the edit to original byte offsets; the splice engine (§1.2) writes it. Volar's virtual-file offset mapping is already adopted in §3.1 for embedded languages — this extends the SAME mechanism one hop further, to the projection MDMAX invents.
   Why it wins: it is the mechanism that makes G2 and G3 sound rather than aspirational. Without it, "a representation easier for AI to produce" means the AI produces something you cannot write back, which is the MDX failure mode restated. With it, the AI never touches markdown at all and the file still stays byte-faithful.
   Non-negotiable: freeze the projection format before building the map, or you will be versioning two things at once.

6. CONTENT-ADDRESSED SIDECAR + PER-BLOCK MERGE POLICY  [from git notes + gitattributes]
   Ship: annotations (comments, provenance, review state, agent-authorship) live in a sidecar keyed by BLOCK CONTENT HASH, never in the file — git's exact model, "attached to objects, without touching the objects themselves", pushed below file granularity, which git itself cannot do. Re-anchoring (§1.1a) is what makes the key survive a `git pull`. Second half: per block TYPE, declare a merge strategy borrowed from gitattributes' built-in drivers — a task list is `union` (take both sides), a paragraph is `text` (conflict), a generated table is `binary` (keep mine). The declaration lives in the vault config, not the file.
   Why it wins: this is the G1 story — Google-Docs-grade collaboration on files the user owns — without owning every write, which is the exact constraint that sinks Overleaf's approach.
   Honest scope: the merge half depends on a concurrent-edit path that §1.1a explicitly states was not tested. Ship the sidecar first; ship merge policy only after the concurrency work.

RUNNERS-UP WORTH NAMING, NOT IN THE SIX
  - TYPED LINKS VIA CiTO. Do not invent a relation vocabulary. CiTO ships 43 sub-properties of `cites` (agreesWith, disputes, extends, corrects, citesAsEvidence, usesMethodIn...), is maintained (versionIRI 2026-06-22), and the demand is the highest measured anywhere (820 likes, 5.8 years). This is CLASS B: the substrate does not exist yet, so MDMAX's editor must write it before the capability has anything to check. Carrier: the link's own text or a frontmatter relation table — never a new sigil (§2.2, character-namespace exhaustion).
  - SUPERSESSION / RETRACTION. Adopt Crossref's shape verbatim: `update-to: [{target, type: retraction|erratum|correction|new_version}]` in frontmatter. Cheapest thing on this list and the highest-leverage for G3 — an AI reading a stale document currently has no signal at all. Degrades to a frontmatter key a dumb viewer ignores.
  - DRC-SHAPED DIAGNOSTICS. Steal KiCad's UX for PLAN §6's confidence ladder: per-rule severity (error/warning/ignore), a custom-rule language, per-violation waivers. This is the presentation layer for 2, 3 and 4.

FALSE ANALOGIES — each of these would cost a year
  - SPREADSHEET WHAT-IF / RECALCULATION ENGINE. Two independent kills. (a) It is a value-flow engine and markdown has almost no value flow: transclusion is 0.13% of internal edges in md and 0.00% in knowledge. (b) Excel itself lacks early cutoff by design — "Excel continues calculating cells that depend on previously calculated cells even if the value of the previously calculated cell does not change" — so you would import the weaker of the two dependency engines onto a substrate with no dependencies. Take Salsa and Bazel; leave the spreadsheet. Trace-precedents is worth stealing as a WORD, not as an engine.
  - FIGMA COMPONENTS / UNITY PREFABS / MEDIAWIKI TEMPLATES AS CONTENT INSTANCING. Human-authored cross-file exact block duplication is 0.14% (Research), 0.20% (knowledge), 0.32% (frontmatter docs), 1.23% (md human-authored). There is nothing to componentize. The 26.32% headline only appears when a machine-generated mirror is counted — and a generator already IS the component. Worse, the parameterized version requires an evaluator: MediaWiki needs loopCheckHash, maxPPExpandDepth, maxPPNodeCount and a `volatile` flag to survive it, and PLAN §2.4 forbids a runtime. And even Figma loses overrides on swap. The duplication in real corpora is at the TYPE level (87 files sharing a heading skeleton), so build design 4, not this.
  - CAD PARAMETRIC CONSTRAINT SOLVING. CAD constraints are numeric with a continuous solution space and a Jacobian to descend. Document constraints are discrete predicates with no solution space and no gradient. There is nothing for a solver to solve. Take EDA's DRC shape (severities, custom rules, waivers); leave the solver.
  - CYCLOMATIC COMPLEXITY / READABILITY METRICS FOR PROSE. Cyclomatic complexity counts branches in control flow; prose has none. The existing prose analogue is the Flesch-Kincaid family, which is the discredited version of this exact idea. Any metric of this shape is CLASS C.
  - CIRCULAR-REFERENCE DETECTION ON THE LINK GRAPH. 347 back edges measured in md's link graph, all benign — prose links are associative, not evaluative. Spreadsheets error on cycles because evaluation must terminate; documents have no evaluation. Meaningful ONLY on an expansion graph, which currently has 21 edges in md and 0 in knowledge.
  - DEAD-CODE ELIMINATION. The honest markdown analogue is unused link reference definitions: 6 in 1,989 files, 0 unused; 0 in knowledge. "Orphan note" is not dead code — a document can be its own entry point. Do not ship an orphan-hunter and call it a compiler feature.
  - OBSERVABILITY SAMPLING / CARDINALITY CONTROL. Documents have no volume problem. Tracing DOES transplant, but as PROVENANCE (which agent read/wrote which block), which is design 6's sidecar, not an observability pipeline.
  - QUERY PLANNERS / COST-BASED OPTIMISATION. At vault scale the plan is always "scan the symbol table". No.
per_area.measurement:
THE OPEN QUESTION. Every number above is n=1 author (Sagnik's corpora). The design that most needs settling is CLASS A's precision: does the metadata plane carry enough real, agreed-upon defects that inferred-schema diagnostics are useful rather than a nag generator? PLAN §1.3 already voided its own 4.4% held-out figure because the corpus behind it was 27.2% vendored and 24.4% LLM-pipeline output. My measurement supplies the first genuine instances (3/575 `status` outliers including a case-only `ACTIVE`; 0/253 conformance to a shipped template; one section under three names across 167 files) but cannot establish precision from one author.

CORPUS. Four markdown corpora, >=500 .md files each, from four distinct authors or organisations, at least two of which are not the researcher's. Generated and vendored content excluded BY PROVENANCE, not by guess: drop any file whose git author is a bot, whose frontmatter carries a generator/mirror key, or that lives under a path listed in the repo's own sync config. Report the excluded fraction per corpus — in `md` that is 2,780 of 4,317 files, and failing to report it is exactly how the 26.32% duplication artifact was produced. Corpus 4 is held out and blind: it is scored once, after predictions are locked.

TASKS AND VERIFIERS (cheapest applicable verifier first).
  T1 INTERFACE STABILITY (rules-based, no judge). Over >=200 consecutive commits per corpus, compute the structural-interface-unchanged rate and the full-interface-unchanged rate per modified .md revision. Pure computation; no rater needed.
  T2 ENUM OUTLIERS (human-rated). For every frontmatter key with >=20 occurrences, flag values outside the modal set. Two independent human raters per flagged item, binary correct/incorrect ("is this actually wrong?"). Cohen's kappa >=0.7 on a 100-item calibration set BEFORE any precision figure is reported; no LLM judge until it agrees with the humans >=90%.
  T3 MISSING-SECTION TOTALITY (human-rated). Infer classes by heading skeleton, flag members missing a section >=80% of the class has. Same two-rater protocol.
  T4 SECTION-ALIAS DETECTION (human-rated). Flag pairs of section names the compiler believes are the same role. Same protocol.
  T5 LATENCY (own-measurement, no judge). Whole-vault interface recomputation and full projection, on each corpus, at 1k / 5k / 20k files.

n. 400 flags rated in total across corpora 1-3, stratified >=100 per corpus and >=80 per task, plus EVERY flag produced on the blind corpus 4.

PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTIONS (locked before corpus 4 is opened).
  P1. Structural-interface-unchanged rate lands in 40-75% on every corpus, and is >=2x the full-interface rate on at least two of four. (Observed so far: 69.1% vs 8.0% on md; 37.8% vs 37.8% on knowledge — the second corpus already sits at the low edge, so this prediction is genuinely at risk.)
  P2. Enum-outlier precision >=0.80 for keys with >=20 occurrences AND <=5 distinct values; <0.50 for keys with >20 distinct values. I.e. precision is a function of key cardinality, and the product must gate flags on cardinality rather than flagging every key.
  P3. Declared-template conformance <20% in every corpus that ships a template; the largest emergent class has more members than the declared one.
  P4. Sub-file (heading + block) references are <2% of internal reference edges in every corpus, and declared `^block-id`s are <0.5 per 100 files.
  P5. Human-authored cross-file exact block duplication <2% of distinct blocks in every corpus after provenance exclusion.
  P6. Whole-vault interface recomputation stays under 100 ms at 5,000 files (Microsoft's own "users feel that the system is responding instantly" band) and full projection under 1 s.

REPORTING RULE. Any number produced by replaying data through modified code, rather than read out of live artifacts, is labelled SIMULATED in the same sentence (LR#62). Every figure above is re-derived at write time by the script, never carried forward by hand.
per_area.kill_condition:
PRIMARY KILL — early cutoff buys nothing. If the structural-interface-unchanged rate is <25% across independent human corpora, then the incremental-compiler wedge collapses: the vendor's "impractical from a performance perspective" objection stands, re-indexing the whole vault is as cheap as being clever about it, and MDMAX's differentiator reduces to UX rather than a compiler. This is a live risk, not a formality: `knowledge` already scores 37.8%, and it scores that because its churning frontmatter keys are content-derived (fidelity, key_terms, entities, length), which durability stratification cannot rescue. Two more corpora at knowledge's level and design 1 is dead.

SECOND KILL — the schema layer is a nag generator. If enum-outlier precision is <0.5 at the key cardinalities that actually occur in the corpora, designs 2, 3 and 4 all fail together, because each of them surfaces the same class of judgement. §1.3's honest prior (7% of 9,655 Python projects ever adopted type annotations) then predicts churn rather than adoption, and the correct response is to ship no schema layer at all.

If BOTH fire, there is nothing left to build from this area, because CLASS B (typed links, transclusion-as-components, impact preview on links) has no substrate to operate on — 0.61%/0.02% sub-file references, 21/0 transclusions, 0 block ids in 2,262 files — and CLASS C (semantic diff of meaning, prose type checking, prose complexity) is unsound by construction. The area would be conceded whole.

THIRD KILL — narrower, and it would invalidate my framing rather than the plan. If P4 fails in the OPPOSITE direction — sub-file references exceed 5% of internal edges in independent human corpora — then existing file-level indexes are much closer to sufficient than I concluded, the "nobody could rely on it, so nobody used it" reading of the 0.61% figure is wrong, and the ranking above should be redone with the link plane promoted over the metadata plane.

FOURTH KILL — for design 5 specifically. If the projection format cannot be frozen (because the token-efficient representation keeps changing with model behaviour), source maps become a versioning problem larger than the capability they enable, and the honest move is to ship the projection read-only and forbid write-back through it.
per_area.effort:
EVERYTHING HERE IS A CONSUMER OF ONE ARTIFACT. Nothing in this area can start before the symbol table (PLAN pass 2 "identify" + pass 5 "index") exists and emits per-file interface data. That is the dependency; the six designs are then largely parallel.

1. EARLY CUTOFF + DURABILITY — 2-3 weeks. The smallest and highest-yield item on the list. It is a second hash, a revision counter, and a comparison; Salsa's entire red-green algorithm fits on two pages of its book. Depends on: pass 2 emitting a per-file interface hash. Risk: low. Prerequisite for the responsiveness claim in every demo.
2. REFERENTIAL ACTIONS, DEFERRED — 3-4 weeks. Depends on: the reverse index (pass 5) and a declaration site in frontmatter. The deferred-check scheduler (save/commit rather than keystroke) is most of the work; the five actions themselves are a switch statement. Risk: low-medium — the UX of showing a blast radius before a destructive edit is unproven in this category.
3. TYPED HOLES — 2 weeks for the metadata plane (empty values, placeholder patterns, SET-NULL'd references), 4-6 more if prose holes (TODO/TK with an expected type from the class) are wanted. Depends on: 4 for the "expected type", so ship the untyped version first (a hole is a hole) and add types when classes land. Risk: low. Best effort-to-G2/G3-value ratio on the list.
4. INFERRED DOCUMENT CLASS + TOTALITY — 4-6 weeks of build, but GATED on the measurement above, which is itself ~2 weeks of corpus collection plus rater time. Do not invert that order. Depends on: heading skeletons (free from pass 1) and the frontmatter key census (free from pass 3). Risk: HIGH, and it is entirely a precision risk, not an engineering one.
5. PROJECTION SOURCE MAPS — 3 weeks, but only after the projection format is frozen; before that it is unbounded. Depends on: §3.1's Volar mapping model, already adopted, so this is an extension of existing machinery rather than new machinery. Risk: medium, concentrated in format churn.
6. SIDECAR + PER-BLOCK MERGE POLICY — sidecar alone 3-4 weeks and depends only on §1.1a's re-anchoring; the merge-policy half depends on a concurrent-edit path that §1.1a explicitly states was never tested ("Concurrent edits from two sources were not tested, so nothing here validates a merge path"), so treat it as unestimated until that work lands.

SHIPPABLE SLICE. Designs 1 + 2 + 3 are the CLASS-A core, share the same dependency, and reinforce each other (2's SET NULL produces 3's holes; 1 makes 2's checks cheap enough to run on save). Roughly one engineer-quarter on top of the compiler, assuming the symbol table is done.

DO NOT START. Anything in CLASS B (typed links, transclusion-as-components, impact preview over links) until the editor has been writing that substrate for long enough that a real vault contains some — today the answer is 0.61%/0.02%, and a capability shipped against an empty substrate demos as an empty screen.

CHEAP AND OUT OF BAND. The supersession/retraction frontmatter key (Crossref's shape) is a few days and is the single highest leverage-per-hour item for G3. It has no dependency on the compiler at all.
per_area.unverified:
EVIDENCE-TIER HONESTY, in descending order of how much it should worry the reader.

1. EVERY corpus measurement is n=1 author. The sub-file reference share, the cross-file duplication rate, the early-cutoff rate, the template conformance figure, the enum-outlier counts and the heading-skeleton clustering all come from Sagnik's own `md`, `knowledge` and `frontmatter` repos. These are own-measurement and the numbers are real, but a single author's habits could produce every one of them. Nothing here is a claim about markdown in general until the four-corpus experiment runs.

2. The `md` early-cutoff figure is contaminated, and the contamination IS the finding but also makes the number unclean. 2,780 of 4,317 files in `md` sit under a machine-generated `Mirrors/` tree. I excluded it for the duplication measurement but NOT for the census or the git-history measurement. So "8.0% full-interface unchanged" is substantially a sync bot's timestamp behaviour (`mirrored`, 207 of 362 revisions), not a human editing rate. The 69.1% structural figure is the more meaningful of the two, and even it is measured on a mixed human/bot history.

3. My first frontmatter value census was WRONG and I corrected it mid-session. The initial run did not strip YAML `#` comments, so it reported values like `done              # queued|processing|done|failed|skipped` as schema violations. They are not violations — YAML strips them. The corrected run (fmvals2.py) is what is quoted. Similarly, my first reading of 19 files with `created: YYYY-MM-DD` as "unfilled holes in the wild" was wrong: all 19 are files under `templates/`, where a placeholder is correct. Both corrections are reflected above; I am flagging them because the uncorrected versions were more flattering to my own thesis.

4. WebFetch-sourced quotes were read by a summarising model, not by me. Figma, Unity, Ardour, KiCad, Microsoft Learn (Excel) and Crossref/Crossmark all came through WebFetch, which returns a model's rendering of the page. The quotes are presented as verbatim by that tool and I have no reason to doubt them, but I did not see raw HTML for any of them. The Crossref `update-to`/`updated-by` JSON structure likewise came through WebFetch against the live API rather than a direct curl. Everything sourced from raw.githubusercontent.com (LSP metaModel, Salsa, Postgres, git, GHC, MediaWiki, Bazel, CiTO, ast-grep, Marksman, IWE, TC39 source-map) I fetched and parsed myself.

5. ast-grep's Markdown support is source-level only. `Markdown` appears in `SupportLang` and in `all_langs()` in crates/language/src/lib.rs, and I report exactly that. ast-grep is NOT installed on this machine — I attempted to run it and got "command not found" — so I executed zero markdown patterns. tree-sitter-md splits block and inline content across two grammars, so what ast-grep can actually MATCH in markdown may be far narrower than the enum entry suggests. Treat "structural search/replace for markdown exists" as unverified in practice; the correction it forces on the strong form of "nobody has codemods for markdown" stands regardless.

6. I did not open any of the papers. Foster et al. TOPLAS 2007, Shipman & Marshall CSCW 1999, Murphy/Notkin/Sullivan FSE 1995, Hofmann/Pierce/Wagner POPL 2012, and Mokhov/Mitchell/Peyton Jones ICFP 2018 ("Build Systems à la Carte", the canonical source for the term "early cutoff") are all cited in PLAN.md and I relied on PLAN's quotations. I fetched snowleopard/build's README but it is 1,672 bytes and carries no definitions.
