4) A SUB-BLOCK RANGE RESOLVER IS AN UNMEASURED PREREQUISITE FOR BOTH COMMENTS AND SUGGESTIONS. 99.627% is a BLOCK figure. Comments and suggestions both anchor RANGES. The range case has one adversarial replication (ambiguity 2.58% -> 0.75% with block scoping, roughly 3.4x, refusal roughly doubling) and no hand-audited false-match number. Measure it once, before building either feature, on a corpus that includes reflow-bearing revision pairs and homogeneous index lists (the known 8x-adversarial input).

5) BLOCK-GRANULAR merge3 MUST REPLACE THE LINE-BASED merge3 BEFORE THE LIVE LAYER EXISTS. The shipped merger is line-based LCS; PLAN §8's own measurement says blank lines are the entire markdown deficit and block granularity removes it. The suggest-mode accept path, the git-boundary reconcile and the live sequencer all route through the same merger by design ('one merge pipeline for keystrokes, git pushes, and AI agents'), so upgrading it once buys all three.

6) THE CONCURRENT-EDIT REPLAY GATES THE LIVE LAYER, AND ONLY THE LIVE LAYER. PLAN.md:159 says the merge path is unvalidated. Comments, suggestions, share roles and the exit ramp do NOT depend on it — they depend on re-anchoring, which is validated. This is the single most important scheduling fact in the whole G1 story: the entire review loop can ship before the multiplayer question is settled, and should.

7) THE EXIT-RAMP CI ASSERTION DEPENDS ONLY ON COMMENTS EXISTING, and should land in the same release, because a sidecar shipped without it is the objection that damaged Relay.

8) SHARE-LINK IDENTITY MUST KEY ON A STABLE FILE ID, NOT A PATH, FROM THE FIRST COMMIT. Retrofitting this after rename cascades exist is the Relay #22 trigger reproduced deliberately.

9) OUTSIDE THE CRITICAL PATH, UNRESOLVED: force-push and history rewrite invalidate every baseSha-anchored comment and suggestion. No design exists for this in any document I read. It needs either an explicit re-basing pass or a document-version table decoupled from SHAs, and it needs deciding before the first paying team.
contradictions: THE CRDT CONFLICT IS THREE-WAY, NOT TWO-WAY, AND THE THIRD LEG IS STILL LIVE IN THE REPO. PLAN §14.6 flags two positions (§8 eg-walker/Braid vs PRODUCT-PLAN §4b no-peer-CRDT) and correctly rules that §4b governs. But PRODUCT-PLAN.md still carries three unreconciled rows specifying the opposite: line 116 'CRDT merge (Yjs/Loro) layered over git commits', line 141 'Multiplayer editing (CRDT, Yjs + Supabase Realtime)', line 217 'CRDT multiplayer editing (Yjs) with git checkpointing'. §14.6 noted 'the feature tables were never updated' — and they still have not been. Anyone reading the pillar tables builds a Yjs layer. PROPOSED (not executed, RULE 4): delete or annotate those three rows to point at §4b. That is a one-commit fix and it is the highest-leverage documentation change in the project.

THE TWO HEADLINE ARGUMENTS FOR §4b IN PLAN §8 DO NOT SURVIVE, EVEN THOUGH §4b IS RIGHT. (a) 'Eg-walker's optimisation is documented by its own authors not to hold for Peritext-style annotations' rests on a line prefixed with `%` in the paper's LaTeX source — struck by the authors, not in the published paper, and it does not compile. (b) The OT disqualification (trace A2: 3,664,266 ms, 6.76 GB peak) benchmarks an in-house peer-to-peer TTF; eg-walker.tex:816-817 states server-based Jupiter/ShareDB were excluded because they cannot represent those graphs at all. So that number says nothing about the server sequencer §4b proposes. Justify §4b on Relay #22 and on adoption (73/wk vs 7.2M/wk), and strike the other two, or the next reviewer will overturn a correct decision by refuting its stated reasons.

PLAN §8's OWN CONCLUSION CONTRADICTS THE SHIPPED CODE. §8 argues at length that 'the lever for prose is granularity, not algorithm' and that a block-structured representation removes markdown's entire diff3 deficit. src/modules/repository/domain/merge3.ts is 183 lines of LINE-based LCS. The design of record and the implementation disagree about the one component every collaboration feature routes through.

THE EXIT-RAMP PROMISE AND THE CARRIER MEASUREMENTS CONTRADICT EACH OTHER, AND BOTH CANDIDATE CARRIERS ARE DAMAGED. T6 promises optional CriticMarkup materialization into the repo; a parallel design proposes HTML-comment sentinels instead. Measured: CriticMarkup is VISIBLE in every renderer and its substitution form {~~old~>new~~} is destroyed by remark-gfm and diverges between remark-gfm and cmark-gfm. HTML comments are invisible everywhere but GitHub's BLOB renderer deletes them outright (5 standalone comment lines in nodejs/node's README source, 0 in the 91,223-byte rendered blob) — i.e. invisible on precisely the surface the user's own repo is browsed on. There is no clean in-file carrier. Ship JSON export as the guarantee and treat any in-file form as lossy interchange.

A MEASURED, UNFLAGGED CORRUPTION IN THE IN-FILE MARKER DESIGN: inserting a marker comment adjacent to a setext heading silently changes the document's meaning, and blank-line isolation does NOT prevent it. Verified against this repo's own parser: 'Heading
---' parses as heading(depth=2); 'Heading

<!-- marker -->

---' parses as paragraph + html + thematicBreak. An h2 becomes a paragraph plus a horizontal rule. Any byte-range-specified marker insertion (including a comments materializer) needs a hard precondition forbidding a boundary between a setext heading's text line and its underline.

A CLAIMED SPEC REQUIREMENT THAT IS NOT ONE, DERIVED FROM AN OPERATION THIS ARCHITECTURE FORBIDS. The rule 'blank-line isolation of markers is a spec REQUIREMENT, not a style' was refuted: parse trees are byte-identical isolated vs glued, in paragraphs, list items, blockquotes and after ATX headings; the only real constraint is 'alone on its line'. The justification came from an mdast stringify round-trip — and splice-only writing means the AST is never stringified. Design rules must be derived only from operations the engine actually performs.

A DIFFERENTIATOR CLAIM THAT DOES NOT SURVIVE A TEN-MINUTE CHECK. 'Refusal is where this beats Hypothes.is' is false: hypothesis/client ships `annotation.$orphan` (guest.ts) and a dedicated orphan tab (sidebar/helpers/tabs.ts). Orphan surfacing is prior art. The narrower surviving claim — a DELTA-style score threshold that declines while a plausible candidate still exists, rather than returning the least-bad guess — is real but much smaller, and the marketing must say the smaller thing.

REVEALED DEMAND CONTRADICTS STATED DEMAND, AND THIS IS THE TOP PRODUCT RISK. Stated: 'the commenting system in Google docs is the main killer feature', 51 votes on codimd #35 since 2015, a 6-year HedgeDoc deadlock, 340+711 forum likes for stable anchors. Revealed: every markdown comment plugin in the largest markdown ecosystem sums to ~24,569 installs against Dataview's 4,659,822 (~190x). The generous reading is that a plugin cannot deliver the collaborator half and therefore cannot test the demand. The ungenerous reading is that markdown users do not collaborate this way. Item 1 is the experiment that distinguishes them, and it should be treated as an experiment, not as a build.

PLAN §567 AND THE PRODUCT PLAN'S PILLARS DISAGREE ABOUT REALTIME. §567 lists real-time collaboration among the things whose demand evidence is contested (Upwelling's fishbowl effect; writers disabled autosave to escape it), while the pillar tables make multiplayer a headline. Both cannot drive the roadmap.

A LOAD-BEARING QUOTE COULD NOT BE LOCATED. The pain playbook's 'for using critic markup you need to change the content' — the sentence that carries the entire in-file-comments-are-impossible argument — was not found in the 20 comments of HedgeDoc #657 that were actually read. It may be in #2879 or #5450. Until located it is SECONDARY and should not be quoted externally. The conclusion is independently supported by the mechanics (a CriticMarkup suggestion IS a file write, so comment-only permission is unenforceable), so fix the citation rather than the argument.

A LATENT AST-BREAKING DEFECT IF COMMENT ANCHORS ARE EVER MATERIALIZED AS LINK REFERENCE DEFINITIONS: a quoted-span field containing a single double-quote degrades the node from `definition` to `paragraph` and corrupts the file, and 14.66% of paragraphs contain a double-quote. Any tail-of-file anchor carrier needs an escaping rule proven against the parser, not assumed.
what_to_cut: THE YJS/LORO PEER-CRDT ROWS (PRODUCT-PLAN.md lines 116, 141, 217). Contradicted by §4b at line 250, contradicted by PLAN §14.6's ruling, and the measured failure mode is Relay #22 — a CRDT parallel to the filesystem false-conflicts on every external write, at ~172-176k installs of real-world exposure. Cut the rows; do not leave them as 'planned'.

DIAMOND-TYPES AS THE SERVER ENGINE. diamond-types-node is 73 downloads/week against Yjs's 7,244,115 and the Rust crate has not been published since 2022-08-25. PLAN §2.1's adoption test — the same test this project used to kill djot — disqualifies it. Keep Braid simpleton's CLIENT contract (text + version string, diff on reconnect, so a git clone / CI job / vim / agent is a participant not a degraded case); reject its server.

A PERSISTED EVENT GRAPH IN V1. Cut it — but cut it for the right reasons (unnecessary given a block-granular merger, and it re-introduces a maintenance dependency), NOT for the Peritext-exemption reason currently written in §8, which is a struck LaTeX comment and does not support anything.

CRITICMARKUP AS STORAGE, in either direction. It is HedgeDoc's deadlock: the suggestion is a file mutation, so comment-only and suggest-only permissions become unenforceable by construction. Interchange only.

THE CRITICMARKUP SUBSTITUTION FORM {~~old~>new~~} IN ANY EMITTED OUTPUT. Measured destroyed by remark-gfm and divergent between remark-gfm and cmark-gfm. Emit adjacent {--old--}{++new++}; Add and Delete round-trip byte-identically and render literally on both.

A SECOND (PROSEMIRROR) EDITOR ENGINE. T2's resolution: every production PM-family serializer has open corruption bugs, and under a baseSha/git model a serializer rewrite of unedited lines is a SYNC-INTEGRITY bug that poisons three-way merge and every comment anchor simultaneously. Single CM6 engine; R-FIDELITY as a permanent CI gate.

POSITION-BASED TIEBREAKS AS AN ANCHOR RESOLVER, in every form. Measured: content hash alone is 83.36% correct / 0.00% false; adding a nearest-position tiebreak goes to 77.80% / 22.20% false. A silently wrong comment placement is unrecoverable in a way a visible orphan never is.

SIMILARITY-BASED AND SPAN-SHAPED MATCHING FOR RE-ANCHORING: Levenshtein/SequenceMatcher thresholds as a MATCH rung, and Cline-style first-line/last-line block anchoring which replaces a block whose MIDDLE differs. On code that is a recoverable compile error; on prose it is silent data loss. Similarity may compute a 'did you mean' candidate for a human, never an applied match.
PER-KEYSTROKE COMMITS, and per-note manual push. Overleaf's just-in-time model (idle-timeout / explicit-save / pre-pull) is the precedent; HedgeDoc #222 is the counterexample.

PROVENANCE / AI-AUTHORSHIP SIGILS AS A COLLABORATION FEATURE. PLAN §567: the demand sweep found ZERO threads requesting it, and what exists is active refusal ('I don't get why I'd want to pollute my notes with AI slop'). The design is good; the demand is unevidenced. Do not spend G1 budget on it.

GLOBAL AI SERENDIPITY FEEDS AND AUTONOMOUS VAULT REORGANISATION inside the collaboration surface. The review-discipline cohort actively rejects it; suggestions at review time are accepted, AI text landing in notes uninvited is not.

ATTEMPTING TO SOLVE CONCURRENT RICH-TEXT MARKS IN THE ALGEBRA. Peritext demolishes control-character approaches with three worked counterexamples and markdown's ** _ ` ARE control characters. Bound it in the UI: same-mark overlaps converge correctly, so refuse or serialize only heterogeneous concurrent mark toggles and edits crossing an inline-code boundary. Do not attempt delimiter counting.

synthesis.lens: G2/G3 — a markdown representation easier for AI to consume and produce, understandable by any AI with zero adoption on the receiving side
synthesis.thesis: G2/G3 reduce to one shippable artifact — a BUDGETED PROJECTION with a DECLARED HEADER, emitted by `mdmax pack`, that is itself an ordinary .md file — and the honest claim it can make is narrower than the brief's own four pillars, because one of them fails on measurement. What survives: (1) FEWER TOKENS is the strongest result in the whole body of work and I reproduced it independently on five corpora this session — index tier is 61–152x smaller than full, outline tier 15–35x, index+outline 12–25x (bytes; the independently tiktoken-measured 34.0x headings-only figure from the token-cost area sits inside my 14.8–35.5x band). (2) ONE PARSE STRATEGY is justified by a precondition I measured as universal — a root-level list glued to the preceding paragraph with no blank line occurs in 45.6%/85.0%/47.3%/54.2%/64.3% of such sites across five corpora — but the DAMAGE from it remains SIMULATED everywhere (Python-Markdown is not installable here and the 51.4% headline was already killed to 47.8% chat / 19.3% files, all from a hand-port). (3) DECLARED PROVENANCE is carrier-solvable and I settled the carrier question by direct test: of seven candidates, only the unknown-language fence reaches BOTH a raw-file consumer and a sanitized rendered-HTML consumer with its payload and its tag intact; the HTML comment — which four separate areas propose as the primitive — round-trips fine but is DELETED by GitHub's blob renderer (I reproduced 5 comments in source, 0 in 91,223 rendered bytes of nodejs/node README), is GONE under remark-rehype's default, and splits a 3-item list into two lists. (4) DEDUPLICATION MUST BE CUT. Every prior area sized it on OCCURRENCE rate (66%, 78%, 83.65%); I measured the BYTE share, which is what determines the token saving, and on hand-authored content it is 0.33%–1.33%, with a median duplicate block of 23–30 bytes that turns out to be `---` (754 occurrences, 3 bytes each) and template section headings (`## Connections` x184). Dedup is worth 58.7%–73.2% of bytes on vendored and machine-generated trees and roughly nothing — a 44x to 222x gap — on the documents a human actually writes, which is precisely the G1 population. The load-bearing scope limit nobody states: G3 is achievable only for RAW-FILE consumers. For HTML-mediated consumers every invisible carrier is gone and only a link `title` attribute and a visible fence survive, so "any AI, zero adoption" is true of agents with a Read tool and false of anything reading rendered output. And the honest claim must stop at cost, identity and translation: not one of the 18 areas ran an experiment measuring comprehension, so every "easier for AI to consume" sentence in this corpus is a pre-registered prediction, not a result.

ranked.capability: BUDGETED PROJECTION — index / outline / full emitted from one source, with an explicit read protocol and honest omission breadcrumbs
ranked.why_now: It is the only G2/G3 capability with the largest measured effect AND no hard dependency on unbuilt machinery — it needs a parser and a heading walk, both of which exist. It is also the only one whose degraded form is trivially correct: a consumer that knows nothing about MDMAX sees a markdown document with a linked list at the top. Everything else on this list depends on block identity, which is not built.
ranked.evidence: [own-measurement, this session, 2026-08-01] Five corpora, mdast top-level block split, byte ratios re-derived at write time. full/index: MD-hand 90.37x (123 files, 2,346,224 B), knowledge 61.12x (236 files, 3,501,530 B), frontmatter/docs 66.60x (46 files, 766,848 B), Skills/ 152.55x, Mirrors/ 103.81x. full/outline: 26.52x / 14.82x / 35.49x / 30.43x / 23.94x. index+outline: 20.50x / 11.93x / 23.15x / 25.37x / 19.45x. [primary-read, corroborating, different corpus] Anthropic publishes the same 174-document corpus both ways: llms.txt 38,847 B vs llms-full.txt 6,556,407 B = 168.78x. [own-measurement, token-cost area, real tiktoken 0.12.0] headings-only 644,821 tok vs full 21,925,516 tok = 34.0x, which sits inside my 14.8–35.5x outline band from a different instrument and different corpora. CAVEAT: my ratios are BYTES; the chars/4 proxy is fine for ratios (both sides are prose in the same script) and must not be quoted as a token count.
ranked.blocked_by: Nothing on the critical path. Needs a tokenizer to print a dollar/token number rather than a byte number — @anthropic-ai/tokenizer is declared in package.json at "*" and is NOT installed, and no tiktoken exists in this environment, so the engine must ship a bytes-labelled fallback and refuse to state a token figure it cannot compute (per the token-cost area's own degradation rule). Separately, the projection format must be FROZEN before any source-map/write-back work starts, or two things get versioned at once.
ranked.ships_as: `mdmax pack <paths> --index (default) | --outline | --full --budget 128k --explain --manifest out.json`. Emits ordinary markdown: a fenced `mdmax.manifest` header, one index line per document carrying path + title + one-sentence description + SIZE (the field repomix ships per-file and nobody ships per-entry in an index), an optional hoisted heading-path outline, then greedy inlining to budget. Never truncate a document mid-file (Codex's anti-pattern); drop it whole and leave a VISIBLE prose breadcrumb, not an HTML comment — a comment-based breadcrumb is silent data loss to every renderer and to the GitHub blob view.

ranked.capability: DECLARED PARSE STRATEGY — a manifest header naming the exact parser contract, plus `mdmax lint --against <impl>` reporting meaning that changes between the parser you authored in and the parser your reader runs
ranked.why_now: This is the only pillar that makes 'one parse strategy' a checkable statement rather than a slogan, and the structural precondition is not rare — it is the majority case in every corpus I measured. It is also the cheapest way to make a document self-describing for G3 without carrying anything: the header NAMES the contract, exactly like JSON-LD @context or a shebang, and a receiver that ignores it loses nothing.
ranked.evidence: [own-measurement, this session] Root-level list whose immediately-preceding sibling is a paragraph with NO blank line between them — the mechanical precondition for the CommonMark-vs-blank-line-requiring-parser divergence: MD-hand 295/647 = 45.60%; knowledge 284/334 = 85.03%; frontmatter/docs 61/129 = 47.29%; Skills/ 3504/6460 = 54.24%; Mirrors/ 8843/13758 = 64.28%. Universal across hand-authored, machine-generated and vendored content. [primary-read] LangChain's MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter applies line.strip() and filter(str.isprintable) to lines INSIDE fences (markdown.py:164/167/180-182) and the ai-dialect verifier independently executed the shipped source and reproduced byte-for-byte corruption including a silently deleted tab, because '\t'.isprintable() is False. WEAKNESS, stated plainly: the DAMAGE number is SIMULATED everywhere. Python-Markdown is not installed here and cannot be (RULE 4); the ai-dialect 51.4% headline was killed and re-measured at 47.83% (chat) / 19.34% (files) through a 60-line hand-port that its author says was wrong twice. I verified only the precondition, not the outcome.
ranked.blocked_by: Nothing to build the header. The `--against` differential is blocked on shelling out to a real divergent implementation rather than reimplementing it — reimplementation is exactly the failure the ai-dialect area hit twice (a missing frontmatter extension inflated k8s thematic breaks 54x; a catastrophically backtracking HR regex hung two runs for 20 minutes). Ship 'unknown' rather than a port.
ranked.ships_as: A `mdmax.manifest` fence at the head of any packed artifact declaring `parser: commonmark+gfm`, `frontmatter: yaml`, `encoding: <tokenizer or 'bytes'>`, `source: <commit>`. Plus `mdmax lint --against commonmark,python-markdown --fix` shipping exactly the blank-line insertion (L1) and the accidental-setext fix (L2), each gated by an AST-superset assertion after the splice. Do NOT ship the emoji-removal or table-de-padding rules the savings ranking puts on top — those tell users to delete legibility to recover a fifth of one percent.

ranked.capability: CONTENT-DERIVED BLOCK IDENTITY — the prerequisite for every other item here, and the project's single strongest measurement
ranked.why_now: Provenance records, splice receipts, dedup pointers, source maps and any cross-document reference all need a name for a block that survives an edit. Nothing else in the ecosystem has one: I confirmed ZERO declared `^block-id` across 2,262 files in the impact-preview area's census, and Google's Open Knowledge Format — which independently confirms every MDMAX invariant and shipped 2026-06-13 — fixes identity to the FILE PATH by spec ('The file path is the concept's identity'), which by construction survives 0% of renames.
ranked.evidence: [own-measurement, PLAN §1.1a, not re-run by me] 99.627% correct / 0.050% false / 0.323% refusal over 41,642 block-versions from 294 real revision pairs, parameters chosen by a 384-configuration sweep, ~41 ms for a 446 KB document, and all 14 false matches HAND-AUDITED rather than sampled (10 of 28,170 = 0.036% genuine substantive errors). This is the only number in the entire body of work whose error cases were exhaustively audited rather than estimated. [own-measurement, retrieval-shape] the competing baselines: byte offset 36.93% correct / 62.12% false match — a 1,242x worse false rate.
ranked.blocked_by: A silent invalidation nobody has flagged as blocking. Every carrier design here (region markers, provenance records, dedup pointers) requires normalize() to strip the carrier before hashing, or writing a record CHANGES the identity of the block it annotates. But the 99.627% was measured under 'NFC + collapse whitespace + lowercase'. Changing the hash input invalidates the 384-config sweep and the headline figure. FREEZE normalize() — including the carrier-stripping rule and the i18n NFC decision — and RE-RUN the sweep BEFORE any anchor ships in the wild, or every published number becomes unattributable to the shipped code.
ranked.ships_as: `mdmax anchor resolve <file> --text @-` printing which rung matched, the occurrence count and the byte offset, or REFUSE with candidates. Refusal must be a first-class typed outcome (`NOT_ANCHORABLE`), which PLAN §1.1a already computes — 14.2% of blocks have no identity — and which no surveyed harness has: Hypothes.is returns its least-bad guess with no threshold, Google's public anchor is a line number they explicitly disclaim.

ranked.capability: DECLARED PROVENANCE in a tail-placed carrier — the unknown-language fence for machine-facing records, a document-tail link reference definition where invisibility is required
ranked.why_now: This is the honest G3 payload: a receiver learns what produced a span, at what confidence, from what source, with zero adoption — it reads a code block. It is also the one place the carrier question was genuinely open across four contradicting areas, and it is now closed by direct measurement.
ranked.evidence: [own-measurement, this session] Seven carriers x four consumers. mdast round-trip (micromark+gfm+frontmatter -> mdast-util-to-markdown): frontmatter IDENTICAL, HTML comment IDENTICAL, link-reference-definition IDENTICAL, link title IDENTICAL, unknown fence IDENTICAL, prose footer IDENTICAL — and `[//]: # (...)` CHANGED, the paren title silently rewritten to a quoted title, so the '`[//]: #` is invisible in 24/24' headline is true about visibility and false about stability. GitHub markdown API (live POST, 2026-08-01): frontmatter renders as `<hr>` + an `<h2>` containing the raw YAML; comment/definition/`[//]:` all invisible; unknown fence survives as `<pre lang="mdmax.prov">`. GitHub BLOB renderer (live, nodejs/node README): 5 standalone `<!--` in 41,791 source bytes, 0 in 91,223 rendered bytes — comments are DELETED. remark-rehype default (allowDangerousHtml:false, the shipped safe path): frontmatter GONE, comment GONE, definition GONE, `[//]:` GONE, link title PRESENT, unknown fence PRESENT WITH `class="language-mdmax.prov"` and payload intact. PLACEMENT, own-measured and decisive: `Heading\n---` parses as heading(h2); interposing ANY block between the text line and the underline yields `paragraph, X, thematicBreak` — an h2 silently becomes a paragraph plus a horizontal rule — and blank-line isolation does NOT prevent it, for the HTML comment or the definition. Appending after the pair is clean (`heading(h2), definition`). An HTML comment placed after item 1 of a 3-item list yields `list, html, list`. A definition inside a list item stays a definition. COST, own-measured on 236 real files (3,501,530 B, 11,011 blocks, 77-byte record): +24.21% at one record per block, +4.84% at 1-per-5, +2.42% at 1-per-10, +1.21% at 1-per-20.
ranked.blocked_by: Block identity (the record's `b=` field is the anchor). And an unmeasured premise that should gate the spend: NO experiment anywhere in these 18 areas tested whether a provenance record changes what a receiving model does. The provenance area's own E1 — including its false-positive probe, whether a `c=1.0` record makes a model MORE credulous about a corrupted value — was designed and never run. Ship the carrier, label the effect unmeasured.
ranked.ships_as: `mdmax prov check | cover | strip`, with `strip` as a first-class one-command escape hatch (a format you cannot leave is a format nobody adopts). Records go at the DOCUMENT TAIL or immediately AFTER their block, never before it. Split every record into a VERIFIABLE half (anchor, quoted span, source hash — a checker can recompute these) and an ASSERTED half (method, confidence, agent, timestamp — attestations that must be tool-written and immutable, because a hand-edited confidence is a lie the format cannot detect). No surveyed standard makes that split.

ranked.capability: SPLICE-ONLY WRITE-BACK WITH A THREE-PART RECEIPT — byte range replaced, pre/post hashes of the untouched prefix and suffix, and a post-write re-anchor assertion
ranked.why_now: This is what makes G2 sound rather than aspirational. 'A representation easier for AI to PRODUCE' means nothing if the AI's output cannot be written back into the user's file without rewriting it — that is the MDX failure mode, and it is measurable damage today: DesktopCommanderMCP #440 is the documented case of an AI markdown integration round-tripping through a stringifier and corrupting the file. The receipt is what lets a downstream system verify the write was a splice and not a regeneration.
ranked.evidence: [theorem] Foster et al., TOPLAS 2007, Lemma 3.9 — this is not a preference. [own-measurement, PLAN] 443 of 655 CommonMark spec examples are two DISTINCT source strings with a byte-identical AST, so the AST provably cannot determine the bytes; a zero-edit round trip of a real 206 KB document rewrites 24.98% of lines and drops 18.94% of bytes; 0 of 51 files in this repo survive parse->stringify byte-identically. [own-measurement, this session, corroborating] the `[//]: # (x)` -> `[//]: # "x"` rewrite is a live instance of exactly this: a carrier that is stable under splice and destroyed by any stringifier in the user's chain. [primary-read, gap] NOT ONE of the eight surveyed harnesses returns proof of where a splice landed — Claude Code returns a diff string, codex returns success/failure, aider returns a commit. None returns a byte range or hashes.
ranked.blocked_by: Block identity, for the re-anchor assertion (which re-resolves the new block text after the splice and reverts on mismatch — a deterministic rules-based verifier reusing the §1.1a fingerprint machinery, the cheapest applicable verifier).
ranked.ships_as: `mdmax edit <file> --old @old --new @new --json` printing the receipt and exiting 0 apply / 3 refuse / 4 ambiguous / 5 reverted; `mdmax verify <file> --receipt r.json` re-checking it against the file on disk. The receipt is the artifact a second collaborator or a CI job can check without trusting the writer.

ranked.capability: EMIT-SIDE DISCIPLINE — never require the model to nest a fence, never require escaping inside a payload, never emit a line number, emit one canonical spelling and parse at least three
ranked.why_now: This is the cheapest half of G2 and it is pure specification: it costs nothing to build and it removes the failure modes that every vendor ladder is currently burning its leniency budget on. It also correctly reframes the goal — MDMAX should NOT specify a new edit format, because the format has already converged across eight harnesses; what it should specify is what an emitter must never ask a model to do.
ranked.evidence: [own-measurement, edit-format area] 4,196 of 4,201 model-emitted opening fences are exactly three backticks = 99.88% — this is the solid figure and the one to cite. [primary-read] Aider's own source carries the comment 'LLMs ignore and revert to triple-backtick, causing #2879' and it ABANDONED backtick escalation for XML wrap fences. [primary-read] OpenAI's cookbook finding is that the two highest-success formats share 'no line numbers' and 'no internal escaping'; Roo is the counterexample and needed `\\<<<<<<<`, `\\:start_line:` and `<` unescaping the moment it adopted markers that can occur in content. [own-measurement, model-view area] the Read-tool line-number surcharge is +14.991% tokens over the file's own bytes — measured, and a pure emitter-side cost. INDICATIVE ONLY: the companion '73.7% of nesting attempts get the outer fence wrong' rests on n=19 and a naive hand-written fence state machine; do not cite it.
ranked.blocked_by: Nothing. This is specification plus a lint, buildable today, and it is the correct scope after the edit-format area's headline collapsed — its 'Unicode typography is the enemy' mechanism was refuted (smart quotes appear in 0 of 85 not-found failures, p=0.833; 29 of 30 exposed failures are em dash U+2014, which no verified ladder folds), its statistics did not reproduce, and the actually-dominant Edit failure turned out to be 'File has not been read yet' at 290/408 = 71.08% — a harness-protocol problem no format spec can touch.
ranked.ships_as: A written emitter contract in the manifest plus `mdmax lint --emit`, enforcing: only two carriers (the fence and the tail definition), one canonical marker spelling emitted and >=3 accepted on parse, zero line numbers in any emitted artifact, and a hard refusal to emit a payload that would require the model to count backticks.

ranked.capability: CROSS-PARSER SILENCE RANKING — rank every diagnostic by how much MEANING changes between the parser the author writes in and the parser the reader runs, not by style
ranked.why_now: It is the only ranking that explains why blank-line-before-list outranks every style rule by orders of magnitude, and it is the ranking function no linter has. markdownlint, remark-lint, Vale and textlint all rank by convention. It is also the correct product framing for G3: the question a document should answer is not 'is this good markdown' but 'will this say the same thing to my reader as it says to me'.
ranked.evidence: [own-measurement, this session] the divergence precondition is 45.6–85.0% of sites across five corpora while the entire provably-semantics-preserving token-rewrite catalogue is 0.0204% of a 21.9M-token corpus — five orders of magnitude apart, and only one of them is what any shipped linter measures. [primary-read] markdownlint MD032 blanks-around-lists already exists at 2.89M downloads/week and MD040 fenced-code-language likewise, so the RULES are not new; the RANKING is. [primary-read, honest limit] babelmark3 is the canonical cross-implementation differ, so the QUESTION is not unclaimed either — what is unclaimed is a per-DOCUMENT, offline, version-pinned answer rather than a live dispatch to third-party HTTP endpoints, 23 of whose 38 providers sit behind encrypted URLs.
ranked.blocked_by: A pinned offline bench. The degradation-certificate area built one (cmark-gfm 0.29.0.gfm.13 at SHA 499789b, kramdown 2.5.2, goldmark 1.8.5, pulldown-cmark 0.13, comrak 0.39, markdown-it 15, marked 16, commonmark.js 0.31.2) and its build recipe is already version-fragile — cmark-gfm's CMakeLists declares a cmake_minimum_required modern CMake refuses without -DCMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5. Pin the BENCH BUILD COMMAND alongside the engine SHAs or the certificate is self-refuting.
ranked.ships_as: `mdmax lint --rank silence` and `mdmax cert <file> --targets=<product,surface> --fail-on=BROKEN`, with targets modelled as (product, surface) PAIRS not products — github-comment, github-blob and github-pages measurably disagree on identical bytes, which is the single most transferable finding in the certificate work and which no tool anywhere models.

synthesis.dependencies:
HARD ORDER, and one item in it is currently mis-sequenced in every area's plan.

(0) FREEZE normalize() FIRST — before anything else, and before a single anchor ships. Every carrier design in this synthesis requires normalize() to strip its carrier before hashing (the ai-dialect area caught this correctly: writing a marker otherwise changes the identity of the block it annotates, and 0.27% of real blocks already contain an HTML comment). But PLAN §1.1a's 99.627%/0.050%/0.323% was measured under "NFC + collapse whitespace + lowercase", with parameters chosen by a 384-configuration sweep. Changing the hash input invalidates that sweep. The i18n area additionally wants NFC as a comparison key at eleven call sites, which touches the same function. If normalize() changes after anchors are in users' files, every stored anchor silently re-keys and the published accuracy figure no longer describes the shipped code. Freeze the function, re-run the sweep, publish the new number, THEN build. Nothing in any area's effort estimate includes this and it is a schedule item, not a footnote.

(1) BLOCK IDENTITY -> everything downstream. Provenance records need it for the `b=` field. The splice receipt and the re-anchor assertion both call it twice. Dedup pointers need a target address. Source maps need a coordinate. Region ids need a name. It is the single chokepoint.

(2) SPLICE WRITER depends on (1). The receipt depends on the splice writer.

(3) THE PROJECTION DEPENDS ON NEITHER, and this is the sequencing insight. `mdmax pack --index/--outline` needs a CommonMark parser and a heading walk — both already vendored in this repo (micromark 4.x, mdast-util-from-markdown, micromark-extension-gfm 3.x, micromark-extension-frontmatter). It is the largest measured G2 effect (12–152x) and the only one with a zero-length dependency chain. Ship it first, alone, and let it be the wedge. Everything else in this lens is downstream of an unbuilt anchor.

(4) PROVENANCE RECORDS depend on (1) AND on the placement rule I measured this session (tail or trailing, never preceding — the setext hazard corrupts an h2 into paragraph+thematicBreak regardless of blank-line isolation, and a preceding comment splits a list). Any design that places a record BEFORE its block is wrong and must be revised before it is built, not after.

(5) SOURCE MAPS / PROJECTION WRITE-BACK depend on the projection FORMAT being frozen. Building the map while the token-efficient representation is still churning versions two things at once and is unbounded. Ship the projection read-only first; add write-back only after the shape stops moving.

(6) THE `--against` DIFFERENTIAL depends on a pinned offline bench with its build command pinned too. Do not reimplement a target parser: the ai-dialect area's 60-line Python-Markdown port was wrong twice (once from omitting the frontmatter extension, which inflated a control corpus's thematic breaks 54x and would have produced a headline that was the exact opposite of the truth), and its author says so. Shell out or report "unknown".

(7) EVERY "EASIER FOR AI" CLAIM depends on an experiment none of the eighteen areas ran. The budget-knapsack arms A–F, the provenance E1 with its false-positive probe, the multi-format T1–T6, the ai-dialect K6 straightforward-baseline test, the retrieval-shape P1 query-log study — all designed, all pre-registered, zero executed. Until one runs, G2 can be claimed on COST and IDENTITY and TRANSLATION and nothing else. The cheapest one that would move the most is the ai-dialect K6: on 100 documents, answer a structured query from the lifted representation versus from raw markdown handed to the same model. If raw markdown wins or ties, the AI-facing half of the justification is decoration and only the editor features survive.
contradictions: CARRIER, four areas, four incompatible answers. edit-format makes the blank-line-isolated HTML comment pair THE region primitive; provenance-boundary makes the HTML comment its Tier 1 per-block carrier; degradation-certificate measured that GitHub's blob renderer DELETES comments outright; unit-of-exchange measured them deleted on BOTH clipboard paths; ai-dialect concluded the carrier should be NOTHING. I reproduced the deletion independently this session (nodejs/node README: 5 standalone `<!--` in 41,791 source bytes, 0 in 91,223 rendered bytes) and added two more failures: the comment is GONE under remark-rehype's DEFAULT config (the shipped safe path in this very repo), and inserting one after item 1 of a 3-item list yields `list, html, list`. RESOLUTION: the HTML comment is a raw-file-only carrier. It is not a G3 carrier. The unknown-language fence is — it is the only one of seven whose payload AND language tag reach sanitized rendered HTML (`class="language-mdmax.prov"`, payload intact) while also round-tripping byte-identically and surviving GitHub as `<pre lang="mdmax.prov">`.

provenance-boundary CONTRADICTS ITSELF and its §1 is the wrong half. §1 says Tier-2 link reference definitions 'survive HTML pipelines that strip raw HTML'; §2 in the same document says remark-rehype drops them. I ran it: the definition payload is GONE in BOTH remark-rehype configurations, because a `definition` node produces no HTML output at all — it is consumed by the parser. §2 is right, §1 is false, and the design's ranking of Tier 2 over Tier 1 was justified partly on the false half. The correct justification for Tier 2 over Tier 1 is different and stronger: PLACEMENT. Tier 2 sits at the document tail, which is the only position that does not corrupt a setext heading or split a list.

`[//]: #` INVISIBILITY vs STABILITY. provenance-boundary's headline names it as one of two carriers 'invisible in 24/24 configurations'. It is invisible — I confirmed that against GitHub's live markdown API. It also does NOT round-trip: `[//]: # (payload)` comes back as `[//]: # "payload"` through mdast-util-to-markdown. Splice-only writing means MDMAX never stringifies, but prettier, remark, and every Obsidian plugin in the user's chain do. Invisibility was measured; stability was assumed. Same class as the missing-constructs finding that only the double-quote link-title delimiter round-trips.

TOKEN SAVINGS: 0.0204% vs −28.7%, used interchangeably and measuring different things. token-cost-tier measured every mechanically-decidable, provably-semantics-preserving REWRITE at 0.0204% of a 21.9M-token corpus (6 tokens on PLAN.md) and concluded COST must never ship as a savings linter. cache-layout inherited a '−28.7% re-representation saving' from the handoff, located it at HANDOFF line 125, and explicitly says it did not re-derive it and does not know what it was measured on. These are not the same quantity — rewriting a table's padding is not the same as emitting the table as a CSV fence (+10.2% cheaper on real corpus tables) — but the handoff uses them as if they were, and every combined-saving figure downstream inherits the unverified one. Name the two levers separately or drop the second.

DEDUPLICATION was sized on the wrong statistic, in four places. governance-and-moat reports 83.65% duplicate blocks vault-wide / 16.71% clean and 78.39%/69.27%; retrieval-shape reports 66.1% of blocks are exact duplicates and calls non-identifiability an unclaimed defect class; budget-knapsack builds near-duplicate collapse into the pack design and calls it 'the one intervention the near-miss literature unambiguously supports'. All of those are OCCURRENCE rates. I measured the BYTE share, which is the only thing that converts to a token saving: MD hand-authored 1.02%, knowledge 1.33%, frontmatter/docs 0.33% — against Skills/ (machine-generated) 73.20% and Mirrors/ (vendored) 58.72%, a 44x to 222x gap. The median duplicate block is 23–30 bytes, and the largest recoverable items are 754 occurrences of `---` (2,259 bytes total) and template headings like `## Connections` x184, which cannot be replaced by a pointer because the heading IS the structure. Dedup is a vendored-content feature wearing a prose-content costume.

BLANK-LINE ISOLATION is claimed as a spec requirement, refuted, and then still relied on. edit-format §1(b) calls it 'a spec REQUIREMENT, not a style'; its own verifier refuted that (parse trees byte-identical isolated vs glued) and separately found that isolation does NOT prevent the setext corruption. I reproduced both: `Heading
---` = heading(h2); `Heading

<!-- x -->

---` = paragraph, html, thematicBreak — an h2 silently becomes a paragraph plus a horizontal rule, isolation or not, for the comment AND the definition. Appending after the pair is clean. The safety property is PLACEMENT, not isolation, and the two were conflated.

G3'S SCOPE LIMIT, which no area states. 'Trivially understandable to any AI with zero adoption on the receiving side' is TRUE for raw-file consumers — agents with a Read tool, git clone, raw.githubusercontent.com — and FALSE for anything reading rendered output, where every invisible carrier is gone and only a link `title` attribute (a hover tooltip, keyboard- and touch-inaccessible per the HTML spec) and a visible fence survive. Every area writes G3 as unconditional. It should be scoped: 'any AI that reads the file'. That is a smaller claim and a true one, and it happens to cover the dominant consumer — the Ahrefs 137,000-domain log study found coding agents were 10% of llms.txt requests, the largest AI slice, against 1% for AI retrieval bots.

THE THESIS vs THE JUSTIFICATIONS. The settled thesis states plainly that markdown is NOT optimal for AI comprehension, that the folklore has no primary source, and that the compiler's job is translation, identity and cost — never format advocacy. Yet budget-knapsack, retrieval-shape, ai-dialect and multi-format-ingest each rest their value on model behaviour that was designed as an experiment and never run. Those are not contradictions of the thesis so much as violations of it in practice: every one of them is a comprehension claim in cost clothing. Hold the line — the honest claim is fewer tokens, one declared parse strategy, checkable provenance, and byte-identical write-back.
what_to_cut: DEDUPLICATION AS A HEADLINE PILLAR — cut, and it was named in my own brief. Own-measured byte share on hand-authored content: 0.33%–1.33%, median duplicate block 23–30 bytes, top item 754 occurrences of `---`. Keep the machinery for pack-time collapse of VENDORED and MACHINE-GENERATED trees, where it is worth 58.72%–73.20% of bytes, and say which population it applies to every time it is quoted. Deduplicating a template heading that appears 184 times across 184 notes is not compression, it is deleting the structure.

CACHE-AWARE DOCUMENT REORDERING — cut entirely. It permutes bytes the user owns, which breaks the file-stays-ordinary-.md invariant outright, and the numbers do not survive: the 80.6% freeze-and-drift headline reproduces exactly as 1 − (0.10 + 0.094), arithmetic from two constants with the write cost, drift accumulation and the 5-minute TTL all omitted; the 31% reordering gain on PLAN.md traces to a 5-byte `version: 0.X.0` field at byte 68; the corpus behind the churn measurement is one 7-hour authoring burst during which the file grew monotonically 34,424 → 106,298 bytes, which is churn on a document being WRITTEN, not one being SERVED. Keep exactly one line of it: emit volatile frontmatter last, which is the one-line alternative the area proposed a whole compiler pass without ever costing.

THE SAVINGS LINTER — cut. 0.0204% of a 21.9M-token corpus for the entire provably-safe catalogue; 6 tokens on this project's own PLAN.md; 0 on its README. The savings RANKING is topped by emoji removal (0.357%, 4.6x the whole safe catalogue) and table de-padding (0.194%), against which remark-lint's own documentation says verbatim that at least one space is recommended 'for legibility of the markup'. A tool that leads with those is telling users to delete legibility to recover a fifth of one percent, and one round of 'the linter told me to delete my emoji' turns the whole diagnostic surface off. Keep attribution (`mdmax cost` as `du` for a document, nouns not verbs) and the budget gate. Ship no savings number.

A NEW EDIT FORMAT — cut. Eight harnesses have already converged and the differentiating research collapsed under verification: the 'Unicode typography is the enemy' mechanism was refuted (smart quotes in 0 of 85 not-found failures, p=0.833; 29 of 30 exposed failures are em dash U+2014, which no verified ladder folds), the headline statistics did not reproduce, the '10,451 calls' denominator matches none of five natural population definitions, the 'a second neighbour adds exactly 0.00pp' claim was a saturation artifact on a 2,599-block corpus (+0.32pp on 285,956 blocks, resolving 45.07% of residual ambiguity), and the genuinely dominant Edit failure is 'File has not been read yet' at 290/408 = 71.08% — a harness-protocol issue no format spec can touch. Keep only the emit-side contract and the receipt.

REGION MARKERS PLACED BEFORE THEIR BLOCK — cut the placement, keep the primitive. Own-measured: any block interposed between a setext heading's text and its underline turns an h2 into paragraph + thematicBreak, and blank-line isolation does not prevent it; an HTML comment after item 1 of a 3-item list splits it into two lists. Records go at the document tail or immediately after their block.

THE `[//]: #` CARRIER — cut. Own-measured non-round-tripping: the paren title is rewritten to a quoted title by mdast-util-to-markdown. Use the double-quoted link reference definition where invisibility is required, and the unknown-language fence where the receiver may be HTML-mediated.

YAML FRONTMATTER AS A PROVENANCE PAYLOAD — cut. Own-measured live against GitHub's markdown API: it renders as `<hr>` plus an `<h2>` containing the raw YAML text, and C2PA 2.4 §A.9's front-matter armour is additionally not valid YAML (two parsers throw) and causes gray-matter — 7,492,225 downloads/week — to silently drop all front matter and leak the payload into the rendered body. Frontmatter carries the DECLARATION (three keys naming the profile) and nothing else.

ACCESSIBILITY DIAGNOSTICS AS A PRODUCT LINE — cut to three diagnostics inside the editor. markdownlint already ships 25 of the 53 relevant rules at 2.89M downloads/week, and the entire open-source markdown-a11y repository population tops out at 1 star. Keep only what no HTML-level tool can see: decorative-vs-missing alt disambiguation, heading order against a COMPOSED outline rather than a file-scoped one, and math mis-tokenization.

THE NOVEL SINGLE-FILE CONTAINER — cut. Google's Open Knowledge Format shipped 2026-06-13 with 'just files' as a principle and reference implementations at both ends; the closest neighbour's users are asking for its output to be split back up (repomix #71). Ship `pack`/`unpack` over a directory. MDMAX's position is OKF's compiler, not a rival format — OKF makes the FILE PATH the identity ('The file path is the concept's identity'), which survives 0% of renames, and identity-under-mutation is the one thing MDMAX has that OKF does not.

AN AUTOFIXER FOR ANYTHING BEYOND L1/L2/L4 — cut. Detection over repair is already the project's rule (CCISolver: detection F1 89.54% vs fix success 65.33%), and outside the blank-line and setext fixes the entire fixable surface is a rounding error against the risk of a bad splice.

INVISIBLE-CHARACTER ALARMS AS A DEFAULT-ON PANEL — cut to a neutral always-on chip. A naive detector fires on 4.94% of 2,308 real files with zero true positives, and its per-class justification points at the wrong characters. Keep only the never-legitimate tier (Unicode Tag block, bidi overrides) as a CI-failing class.

synthesis.lens: Completeness critic — what all 18 areas missed, and the case that the program is over-researched and under-built
synthesis.thesis: The single most important fact in this synthesis is one nobody stated: 18 of 18 area headlines were materially refuted by their own adversarial verifier. Not qualified — refuted. The sentence a reader would remember from every area was wrong, and it was wrong in the flattering direction every time (0.155%→0.0204%, 51,620→17,065, 12/12→11/12, 30×→3.44×, 8,603:1→1,067:1, "zero implementations"→two shipping packages found in one query, "the surface does not exist"→15.1× larger once the excluded construct is counted). That is not a research corpus with some errors in it; that is a measured, program-wide optimism bias with a 100% headline defect rate, and it means the verified residue — not the headlines — is the only asset here. Underneath that sits a second program-wide failure the verifiers caught piecemeal and nobody aggregated: there is no pinned corpus. I measured `~/Desktop/GitHub/md` today and got 5,563 / 3,245 / 1,989 / 756 / 4,131 files depending on exclusion policy; the 18 areas variously report 4,312, 4,317, 4,710, 4,823, 5,981, 5,986 and 2,586, and **not one of those seven numbers is reproducible under any policy I could construct**, on a corpus that provenance-boundary measured drifting mid-session. Every rate in this program divides an unstated numerator by an unreproducible denominator. Third: after 18 areas explicitly serving goals G2 ("easier for AI to consume") and G3 ("trivially understandable to any AI"), **zero live model calls were made against any representation by any area**. Every G2/G3 claim in 1.09 MB of documentation is a pre-registered prediction. Meanwhile the engine has 0 lines of code, 19 days after the first commit, with 12 of 20 commits being `docs`, no `mdmax` string anywhere in `src/`, no splice/re-anchor/blake2/shingle implementation, and micromark and mdast-util not even installed as direct dependencies. The honest verdict: this program has produced one genuinely valuable, verified, unclaimed primitive (content-derived block identity plus splice-only writing), roughly a week of engineering, wrapped in 1.09 MB of design for consumers who have never been asked, measured against a corpus that does not hold still, in a tokenizer that is not the target vendor's, for a defect that its own edit-format area measured to be smaller in markdown (2.43% error rate) than in TypeScript (5.24%).

ranked.capability: One live-model experiment — any one — against any representation
ranked.why_now: This is the largest hole in the program by an enormous margin. Eighteen areas researched how to make markdown easier for AI to consume and produce, and not one of them put a representation in front of a model and measured whether it helped. Every G2 and G3 claim is inference. multi-format-ingest states it flatly: 'No claim here has been tested against an actual LLM.' cache-layout: 'I NEVER MADE A SINGLE LIVE API CALL.' token-cost-tier: 'NO COMPREHENSION MEASUREMENT ANYWHERE IN THIS REPORT.' model-view and unit-of-exchange never touched a real AI surface at all. budget-knapsack's entire contribution is six pre-registered predictions. The one-day version of this experiment exists in four separate measurement plans and was run zero times.
ranked.evidence: own-measurement, this session: `grep -ril mdmax src/` returns 0; no experiment harness on disk. Plus verbatim admissions in 5 of 18 areas' unverified fields. The cheapest form — multi-format-ingest's 'FIRST CUT, ONE DAY: 3 arms x 20 documents x T2+T4' — is stated in the plan and unexecuted.
ranked.blocked_by: Nothing. Provider keys are present in the app config (per integrity's own note). This was buildable on day one of the research and was displaced by more research.
ranked.ships_as: A 200-call script: N documents x 3 representations x 2 tasks, exact-string verifier, no judge. One afternoon. If it shows no effect, 11 of the 18 areas are dead and the program saves months.

ranked.capability: A pinned, hashed corpus manifest with a single stated exclusion policy
ranked.why_now: Every quantitative claim in this program inherits an unstated filter, and the filters were applied inconsistently *within single areas*. governance's verifier proved this exactly: claim 3 excludes .sgnk/ and node_modules/ (because excluding them supports the conclusion) while claim 5 and the design's 86.4% silently include them (because including them supports that conclusion), and the verifier reproduced the contamination to the exact file count. missing-constructs excludes Mirrors/ when it kills a transplant and relies on it when it supports one. retrieval-shape reproduced its own script fifteen minutes later and got different numbers because the vault was being written to. Until the corpus is a hash-pinned artifact, no number in this program is auditable and no result is replicable — including the ones that survived verification.
ranked.evidence: own-measurement, 2026-08-01: `~/Desktop/GitHub/md` yields 5,563 (all) / 3,245 (no dotdirs) / 1,989 (also no node_modules) / 756 (also no Mirrors) / 4,131 (git-tracked). The 18 areas cite 4,312, 4,317, 4,710, 4,823, 5,981, 5,986, 2,586. Zero matches across seven claims and five policies.
ranked.blocked_by: Nothing. Half a day.
ranked.ships_as: corpus.json: {policy, file list, per-file sha256, capture timestamp}, plus a rule that every reported figure names the manifest id. This is LR#59 and LR#60 applied to the research layer, which is exactly where they were not applied.

ranked.capability: The engine: splice-only writer + content-derived re-anchor, as executable code
ranked.why_now: It is the only verified, unclaimed, defensible primitive the program produced, it is the hard dependency of at least 11 of the 18 designs (edit-format receipts, cache-layout's drift block, provenance's whole profile, collab's anchor record, impact-preview's symbol table, budget-knapsack's dedup, governance's OKF moat, missing-constructs' RECORD, adjacent-transplant's early cutoff, degradation-certificate's block attribution, unit-of-exchange's evidence inlining), and after 19 days it does not exist. The 99.627%/0.050%/0.323% figure that eight areas cite as settled was, per provenance-boundary's own admission, 'quoted from the task brief, not re-measured here.' The number the entire program rests on has been re-derived by nobody.
ranked.evidence: own-measurement: `src/` is 212 files / 21,415 lines, cloned from the md app on 2026-07-17, with zero `mdmax` references and no splice, re-anchor, blake2 or shingle implementation. micromark and mdast-util-* are not direct dependencies — only remark-parse/unified are. 193 test files exist, all for the product shell, none for the engine.
ranked.blocked_by: Nothing but the decision to stop researching. Multiple areas independently cost it at roughly one week.
ranked.ships_as: One package: parse to mdast, per-block byte ranges, blake2 over normalize(text), resolve against a new revision, splice-write, assert byte-identity outside the range. Then re-run the 99.627% sweep on the pinned corpus and see whether it holds.

ranked.capability: A corpus written by somebody other than this user, in a language other than English
ranked.why_now: Every single quantitative claim across all 18 areas comes from one operator's vault. This is not a caveat, it is a confound with a measured direction: ai-dialect's verifier found 43.25% of the 'AI dialect' corpus is isSidechain subagent output whose format is dictated by this user's own CLAUDE.md — so 'the AI dialect' is partly a measurement of this operator's prompt. normalization-i18n found the entire 4,823-file corpus contains exactly one file with any RTL character, in the project's own test string, and then built a design lane for Thai/Lao/Khmer/Burmese on zero corpus characters. missing-constructs' entire 'transplant is dead' verdict rests on n=1 author's linking habits.
ranked.evidence: Stated in the unverified field of 12 of 18 areas. ai-dialect: 'one operator, one harness, one vendor's model family.' normalization-i18n: 'Thai/Lao/Khmer/Burmese have NO corpus behind them in this report.' impact-preview: 'All three corpora are ONE person's markdown.'
ranked.blocked_by: Nothing. Public corpora were named repeatedly and fetched by nobody: kubernetes/website, rust-lang/book, github/docs, the Sourcegraph handbook, top-300 READMEs. degradation-certificate and ai-dialect each fetched two and the rest of the program ignored them.
ranked.ships_as: Four public corpora, hash-pinned, re-run the six load-bearing measurements. If the anchor rate, the duplication rate and the frontmatter density do not survive, most of the design does not either.

ranked.capability: One conversation with one human being who is not the author
ranked.why_now: Product goal G1 is 'the Google Docs of markdown' — a collaboration product — and across 18 areas covering roughly a million bytes of design, zero users, zero interviews, zero usability sessions, zero willingness-to-pay probes were conducted. Three areas name this as their own top kill condition and none of them ran it. collab-primitives: combined installs of every markdown comment plugin = 24,569 against Dataview's 4,659,822 (190x), and its kill-3 is 'the demand was stated, not revealed.' normalization-i18n's kill-4 is a fifteen-person interview it did not do. edit-format's kill-3(a) is 'if authors reject visible marker comments in their prose' — a question answerable by showing three people a file.
ranked.evidence: Zero user-research artifacts in the repo; zero interviews referenced in any of the 18 areas' evidence fields. The strongest demand signal anywhere in the program is a forum like-count (820) and a plugin install count, both of which the areas themselves flag as weak proxies.
ranked.blocked_by: Nothing. This is the cheapest unrun experiment in the entire program and it gates the most expensive builds.
ranked.ships_as: Ten people, thirty minutes each, shown a commented .md and asked what they'd pay to fix mid-clause search / a broken anchor / a lost tracked change. Report the raw answers, not a summary.

ranked.capability: A carrier-survival conformance matrix, shipped as a fixture, before any carrier is chosen
ranked.why_now: Five independent areas built their central design on the HTML comment as the carrier — edit-format's region markers, provenance's Tier-1 records, missing-constructs' block meta, collab-primitives' comment sentinels, budget-knapsack's dedup pointers and omission breadcrumbs — while two other areas measured that the HTML comment is DELETED by GitHub's blob renderer and by both clipboard flavours. Nobody reconciled it. This is the single clearest instance of the program's real failure mode: eighteen parallel researchers, no shared fixture, incompatible conclusions about the same construct, never surfaced.
ranked.evidence: degradation-certificate (verified, replicated on nodejs/node README: 5 standalone comment lines in source, 0 in the 91,223-byte rendered blob) and unit-of-exchange ('BOTH paths delete HTML comments and YAML frontmatter outright'). Against five areas that treat it as the safe channel. provenance-boundary lists exactly three verified consumers and calls the rest 'inference'; it also flags this gap as 'load-bearing for G3' and untested.
ranked.blocked_by: Nothing. degradation-certificate already built most of it and estimates the cheap slice at two days.
ranked.ships_as: A committed fixture: N constructs x M consumers (GitHub blob, GitHub comment, GitHub Pages, VS Code, Obsidian, both clipboard flavours, MDX, remark-rehype safe default) with PASS/STRIP/CORRUPT per cell. This is also the one publishable public artifact in the whole program.

ranked.capability: The structured-merge literature, and the concurrent-edit path it governs
ranked.why_now: collab-primitives resolves the architecture conflict by betting the entire live layer on 'block-granular merge3', and then states in its own unverified field: 'NO CONCURRENT-EDIT PATH WAS TESTED. PLAN §9 already flags this. Nothing in this research changes that.' The G1 product — the whole collaboration thesis — rests on a merge algorithm nobody has run, chosen over the alternative on npm-download-count grounds. And zero areas across the program consulted the structured-merge research field (Spork, jdime, semistructured merge, Apel et al.) despite that field existing precisely to answer 'does structure-aware three-way merge beat line-based merge, and where does it produce silent wrong results.'
ranked.evidence: collab-primitives' own admission, plus PLAN §9's pre-existing flag. adjacent-transplant surveyed build systems, databases, IDEs, spreadsheets, CAD, DAWs and VCS — and did not survey merge research, the one field directly load-bearing on the chosen architecture.
ranked.blocked_by: The engine (a merge needs blocks and identity first).
ranked.ships_as: Read four papers; then replay the eg-walker A1/A2 git-derived traces (published, free) through block-granular merge3 and count silent divergences. collab-primitives already specified this experiment and did not run it.

ranked.capability: A real tokenizer for the target vendor, and one real billing reconciliation
ranked.why_now: Every cost figure in the program is denominated in a foreign tokenizer. token-cost-tier's Claude column uses @anthropic-ai/tokenizer@0.0.4 — published 2023-06-28, the Claude 1/2 tokenizer — and says so. cache-layout used len(text)/4 for everything and never made an API call. model-view and multi-format-ingest used o200k_base and labelled every Claude number approximate. So the program's entire cost argument, including the portability floor that governs which rewrites are admissible, is measured on models nobody is targeting. token-cost's kill-5 is explicitly 'if the portable subset is empty under a current tokenizer.'
ranked.evidence: Verbatim in three areas' unverified fields. token-cost-tier: 'That is the Claude 1/2 tokenizer, NOT Claude 3+.' cache-layout: 'Every cost number in this report is a MODEL... Nothing is billed evidence.'
ranked.blocked_by: An API key (present per integrity's note) and one call to /v1/messages/count_tokens.
ranked.ships_as: Re-derive the six load-bearing cost figures against count_tokens, and reconcile one real cache_read_input_tokens against cache-layout's prediction. If they diverge more than 15%, cache-layout's own kill-6 fires.

ranked.capability: A threat model of the compiler itself, and a licence review of the vendored bench
ranked.why_now: Two adjacent fields went entirely unconsulted and both have already drawn blood inside this very research. (a) Compiler security: integrity measured 45.5 seconds on a 1.49 MB file from its own linear region scan, ai-dialect hung two full runs on catastrophic regex backtracking, and unit-of-exchange found a unist-util-visit traversal bug that silently inflated numbers 8.5x. Nobody asked what a hostile .md does to the re-anchor algorithm, the shingle index, or the ladder — in a product whose whole premise is ingesting files from other people. (b) Licensing: degradation-certificate proposes vendoring cmark-gfm, kramdown, goldmark, pulldown-cmark, comrak, markdown-it, marked and commonmark.js, normalization-i18n proposes shipping Linguist's languages.yml and a subset of Unicode confusables.txt, and no area checked a single licence or redistribution term.
ranked.evidence: own-measurement, in-band: three separate performance/correctness pathologies hit by the researchers' own instruments. Zero occurrences of licence review across all 18 areas' evidence.
ranked.blocked_by: The engine existing (for the threat model). Nothing for the licence review.
ranked.ships_as: A ReDoS + adversarial-input fixture set for the anchor and ladder paths, and a one-page licence table for every artifact the bench proposes to vendor.

synthesis.dependencies: Strict order, and the program has it backwards today. (1) PIN THE CORPUS — half a day, blocks every measurement, and until it exists no number produced by any of the 18 areas can be audited or replicated. (2) BUILD THE ENGINE — splice writer plus content-derived re-anchor, ~1 week; it is the hard dependency of 11 of the 18 designs and it does not exist. Nothing downstream is worth specifying further until the 99.627%/0.050%/0.323% figure has been re-derived by someone in this program rather than quoted from a brief. (3) RUN THE LIVE-MODEL EXPERIMENT and TALK TO TEN PEOPLE — both cheap, both independent of everything else, both currently blocking every G1/G2/G3 justification in the program. Run them in parallel with (2); they gate whether (4) happens at all. (4) THE CARRIER FIXTURE — depends on nothing technically, but must precede any decision to write bytes into a user's file, because five areas have already committed to a carrier that two areas measured as deleted. (5) EVERYTHING ELSE — every diagnostic tier, every projection, every ladder, every certificate, every ledger — depends on (2) and should not be built until (3) says a receiver behaves differently. The critical inversion: the program spent 19 days and 1.09 MB on step (5) while steps (1) through (4) cost roughly two weeks combined and every one of them can invalidate step (5) wholesale.
contradictions: THE HTML COMMENT CARRIER, five-against-two. edit-format (region markers), provenance-boundary (Tier-1 records), missing-constructs (block meta), collab-primitives (comment sentinels) and budget-knapsack (dedup pointers + omission breadcrumbs) all build on the HTML comment as the safe invisible channel. degradation-certificate measured GitHub's blob renderer DELETING standalone comments outright (5 in source, 0 in the 91,223-byte render) and unit-of-exchange measured BOTH clipboard flavours deleting them. budget-knapsack's own verifier then names the consequence — comment-carried breadcrumbs are 'silent data loss, the opposite of the degradation invariant.' Five designs rest on a carrier two measurements show is destroyed on the two surfaces the product most cares about, and no area reconciled it.

REORDER vs NEVER REORDER, on the same emitted prompt. cache-layout's core decision is 'MDMAX must NOT reorder a single document' and its whole freeze-and-drift design requires the document pinned byte-stable in the cached prefix. budget-knapsack ships Jin et al.'s sandwich reordering at k>=10 as a default. These are two passes over the same output artifact and they are mutually exclusive; neither area mentions the other.

THE FILE STAYS ORDINARY .md vs WRITING MARKERS INTO IT. The settled thesis is that degradation is the feature and the document names a capability, never carries one. ai-dialect follows it exactly ('the answer is NOTHING; the file stays byte-identical'). edit-format proposes minting `<!-- mdmax:begin id=k7f2 -->` pairs into user prose via a CLI verb — and its own verifier then found that inserting one adjacent to a setext heading silently converts an h2 into a paragraph plus a horizontal rule, including in the blank-line-isolated form the design mandates as the fix. The program has not decided whether it writes bytes into user files, and one of the two answers has a demonstrated corruption bug.

BLANK-LINE ISOLATION: a normative requirement derived from a forbidden operation. edit-format §1(b) calls it 'a spec REQUIREMENT, not a style'; the verifier refuted it and identified the cause — the justification came from an mdast stringify round-trip, and splice-only writing means the AST is never stringified. The region primitive still depends on the refuted claim.

MARKDOWN EDITING IS NOT ACTUALLY HARDER THAN CODE. edit-format's own kill-condition 2 reports .md at a 2.43% total error rate against .ts at 5.24%, and that the dominant Edit failure (71.08%) is 'File has not been read yet' — a harness-protocol issue no format spec can touch, with the not-found class that the entire area addresses at 0.614% of calls. This single measurement undercuts the premise of the area that produced it and is never reconciled with the rest of the program.

FIX THE TOOL vs SHIP THE DIAGNOSTIC. retrieval-shape's conclusion is that the fix is upstream — swap the tokenizer, dark blocks fall 2.12% to 0.04%, and 'a diagnostic whose findings evaporate when you fix your own tool is not a product; it is a migration checklist.' That logic generalizes directly to token-cost-tier, integrity, ai-dialect, impact-preview and provenance, all of which ship E/W/I diagnostic ladders. Nobody applied it outward.

THE MOAT MAY ALREADY BE SHIPPED. governance's design is 'become OKF's compiler' because 'identity-under-mutation is still unbuilt' — and its own verifier found OKF SPEC.md §5.1 already ships keyed-not-positional identity with verbatim the same rationale ('a positional index misattributes silently the moment the list is reordered, whereas a stable id survives reordering'), in a 37,544-byte spec the researcher never opened, plus a v0.2 released seven days before the research and missed entirely. The programme's stated moat was assessed against a marketing blog post.

THE ANCHOR WINDOW, design vs measurement. edit-format's §2 states a second neighbour 'is forbidden by measurement: it adds 0.00 percentage points and is pure token waste.' Its verifier measured +0.32pp on 285,956 blocks, resolving 915 of 2,030 residual-ambiguous blocks (45.07%), and identified 0.00 as a saturation artifact of a 2,599-block corpus. The design shipped the refuted number as its strongest-worded rule.

FRONTMATTER IS DENSE vs FRONTMATTER IS RARE. missing-constructs' CLASS A rests on 'the metadata plane is densely populated (36.3%)'; its verifier decomposed that as 81.3% coming from two 100%-coverage generated trees, with hand-authored frontmatter at 6.8% of the corpus. governance's 86.4% type-missing figure was computed on a corpus its verifier proved is 56.8% node_modules plus .sgnk snapshot artifacts. Two areas size the same opportunity from the same corpus and both numbers are generator output.

TWO AREAS CITE AN ANCHOR NUMBER THAT EXISTS NOWHERE. Both cache-layout and token-cost-tier lean on a '101.1x' index-vs-full ratio; token-cost's verifier grepped PLAN.md, README.md and wf-findings and found it in no claim, no evidence field, no script and nowhere in docs/engine. A figure with no source propagated across areas because no area checks another area's citations.

MULTI-FORMAT'S FORENSIC MODE IS INTERNALLY UNSATISFIABLE. §1 defines forensic as 'nothing is dropped... Ledger must be empty'; §4 sends PPTX animations to 'the ledger, never the .md'; the design's own ledger example lists 'pptx.animation 9'. No deck with an animation can be ingested in forensic mode. Caught by the verifier, unresolved in the design.

THE 'AI DIALECT' IS PARTLY THIS OPERATOR'S PROMPT. ai-dialect characterises a cross-vendor phenomenon from a corpus its verifier showed is 43.25% isSidechain subagent output whose structure is prescribed by this user's own global CLAUDE.md, 23.55% duplicated content, one vendor, one harness, one author — and the researcher's own split shows a 1.9x swing between subagent and main-thread output on the flagship metric before reporting the pooled figure as the dialect.
what_to_cut: FURTHER RESEARCH, entirely, until an engine exists. Verified today: 20 commits, 12 of them `docs`, first commit 2026-07-13 (19 days), docs/engine at 1,139,825 bytes (1.09 MB) across PLAN.md 1,748 lines, a 46,837-byte README, a 408,550-byte dossier.html, a 449,691-byte PDF and 128,449 bytes of findings — against 0 bytes of engine code, 0 occurrences of `mdmax` in src/, and no splice, re-anchor, blake2 or shingle implementation anywhere on disk. The strongest evidence that this is over-research is not the ratio; it is the 18-of-18 headline defect rate, which is what happens when research is graded by volume produced rather than by a build that fails.

THE DOSSIER AND THE PDF. 858,241 bytes of presentation material for an engine that does not exist, and three of the last four commits are cosmetic fixes to it (page overflow, cover page, logo mark). This is the clearest single artifact of the program optimising for the appearance of progress.

TWELVE OF THE EIGHTEEN DESIGN SECTIONS. Every design whose justification did not survive its own verifier should be deleted rather than patched: the savings linter (its own kill-1 says a savings-oriented cost linter is 'dead on the numbers' at 0.0204%), the reordering pass (cache-layout's own measurement says do not reorder), the a11y product line (governance's own verdict: markdownlint holds 25 of the 53 rules at 2.89M/week and the entire markdown-a11y repo population peaks at 1 star), the emoji/status-column lift (32 distinct glyphs observed against a proposed closed set of 12), the Thai/Lao/Khmer lane (zero corpus characters), the markdig/.NET port (zero demand evidence; its 71.2M figure is all-time, not weekly), the single-file container (OKF took the slot and its own users ask for packs to be split back up), Cline-style block anchoring (already excluded), the arithmetic checker (its own author says the instrument is broken and reported 46.6% then 7.78% and does not trust either), and the a11y/DRC/CAD transplant runners-up.

THE 'NOBODY HAS BUILT THIS' FRAMING, program-wide. It was refuted by a single search in five separate areas: provenance's 'zero implementations of C2PA §A.8/§A.9' (41 code results, two published packages, one Rust crate, one PyPI package); governance's chunker wedge (a whitespace-preserving splitter ships in the same LangChain file, and the bug has been public since 2024-04-24 as issue #20823); collab's 'this beats Hypothes.is at refusal' (Hypothes.is ships $orphan and a dedicated orphan tab); impact-preview's 'nobody implements LSP diagnostics for markdown' (marksman ships diagnostics, find-references, rename and duplicate-heading detection across eight editors); ai-dialect's L1/L3 (markdownlint MD032 and MD040, 2.89M/week, cited from the same doc/ directory the researcher was reading). Any future novelty claim must cite the search that was run, or be deleted.

EVERY REMAINING CLAIM ABOUT WHAT AN AI DOES WITH A REPRESENTATION, until a model has been called. That is the entirety of the G2 and G3 justification across all 18 areas, and it currently rests on zero observations.

THE PARALLEL 18-AREA RESEARCH SHAPE ITSELF. This is the LR#20 failure in its exact form — parallel branches operating on the same creative target with implicit shared assumptions. The observable cost: seven irreconcilable corpus denominators, five areas committed to a carrier two areas measured as dead, two areas citing a figure that exists in no source, two mutually exclusive layout passes, and no cross-area reconciliation pass anywhere. If more research is ever run, it must share one pinned corpus, one fixture set, and one reconciliation gate — or it will reproduce these defects at whatever the new N is.
